Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote. They simply don't believe we all deserve to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062526_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
KATU: Vance calls on Congressional Republicans to pass SAVE Act during speech [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062526_3&amount=25]
Opponents of voting rights are trying everything they can think of to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address Trump's often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. Vice President J.D. Vance called on Congress again this week, begging them to pass this awful bill ahead of the next election.
The SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now, Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062526_3&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062526_3&amount=35]

How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "

Now, Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Overtime should mean double the wage
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
The American people are facing an affordability crisis as skyrocketing inflation outpaces workers’ wages.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260625-6397-footer&t=1&akid=6397%2E420207%2EQsmoa2)
Peter,
The American people are facing an affordability crisis as skyrocketing inflation outpaces workers’ wages.
Right now, 76% of Americans say the cost of living is their biggest economic concern, with 65% saying a middle-class lifestyle is out of reach and 77% saying it’s harder to achieve than a decade ago. In 49 states, the average renter’s wage isn’t enough to afford a two-bedroom apartment. In 37 states, it’s not even enough for a one-bedroom.
Meanwhile, 41% of workers report starting early or finishing late every single day.
**That’s why I’m proud to be co-leading the Double the Wage for Overtime Act, which would raise the federal overtime pay to double a worker’s wage for every hour worked over 40 a week, from the current rate of a time and a half.**
For example, someone who makes $25 an hour and works 10 hours overtime each week would make $6,500 more each year as a result of this bill.
This legislation will ensure that hardworking Americans get the pay they deserve while also deterring corporations from forcing workers into long, unsustainable hours.
It’s just one of many steps we need to take to address the affordability crisis that working people are facing right now. I’m going to keep pushing to get this legislation passed, but I’m counting on your support to keep growing this movement.
[**If you’re with me, will you pitch in $3, or any amount you can, to help me keep fighting for legislation that will make a real difference for working people?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260625.s3-n9X&refcode=em20260625-6397&amount=3&t=2&akid=6397%2E420207%2EQsmoa2)

# **🚨 📺 NEW TV AD IS LIVE 📺 🚨 **
Twenty years ago, I became an American citizen, and I truly can think of no other place on earth where a young immigrant has the opportunity to grow up and one day serve as a member of Congress.

My dad drove a bus, my mom cleaned houses, and I flipped burgers as my family worked to build a better future for me and my sisters here in the United States of America. Like so many families across Arizona, we were looking for opportunity.

_**We simply wanted a shot at the American Dream.**_ _**That's what I fight for every day.**_

But the more time I've spent in Washington, the more frustrated I've become watching politicians put themselves first. Families are working hard every single day just to make ends meet, yet too many elected officials are getting rich from the positions voters entrusted to them.

_**So I did something about it.**_

I stood up to both parties and sponsored legislation to ban congressional insider trading because members of Congress should never be allowed to profit from information unavailable to the American people. Despite what some politicians believe, public office is a responsibility, not an opportunity to get rich.

I haven't forgotten where I came from, and I never will.

**I don’t work for Washington. I work for YOU.**

| | Peter Willis, For years, Washington promised solutions and delivered excuses.

**That's changing.**

President Trump is securing the border, restoring American strength, and putting hardworking Americans first.

And **we're delivering results.**

We passed tax relief that helps families keep more of their hard-earned money. We're working to strengthen our economy, support agriculture, and ensure Kansas families have a stronger future.

But let's be honest: **the fight isn't over.**

The Left is still pushing bigger government, higher spending, and the same failed policies that drove up costs and weakened our country.

That's why I'm continuing to fight every day for Kansas values in Congress.
* **Secure border.**
* **Lower taxes.**
* **Strong agriculture.**
* **More freedom.**
* **Safer communities.**

And right now, we're approaching an important quarterly fundraising deadline.

At the end of the month, campaigns across the country will report their fundraising numbers. Political insiders, outside groups, and potential challengers will all be looking at the results.

**We need to show strength.**

We need to show momentum.

**And we need to show that Kansas conservatives are standing behind our efforts to keep delivering results.**

We’ve got two big wins to share:
Yesterday, we secured a final ruling in our push to permanently block key provisions of Trump’s executive order that attempted to take over state election processes and impose vast voting restrictions across the country.
This executive order was unconstitutional, antidemocratic, and un-American — so as we do when the President brazenly violates the law, we sued. And as we do when we fight with the law on our side, we won .
Yesterday’s major victory was followed up today by a ruling blocking key provisions of Trump’s second elections-related executive order through the midterms. This order (also unconstitutional, of course) would have interfered with states’ authority to run our own elections by restricting mail-in voting and voter eligibility.
Trump tried to rewrite the rules of our elections through illegal power grabs. We fought back. We won.
These wins are thanks to your support — we can’t do any of this without you. Will you keep it going by chipping in any amount today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

Fueled by his fear of losing the upcoming midterms, Trump continues to spread lies and feed into delusions about our elections.
We are clear-eyed that this President’s attacks on voting rights and elections will continue. But I can promise you this: We won’t be bullied, and we won’t stand by and let him trample on our most foundational rights.

# **Senator Hughes Honored with Social Justice Warrior Award**
Senator Hughes was honored to receive the Social Justice Warrior Award from the [Alliance of Community Service Providers](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17595).
Senator Hughes was recognized for his unwavering commitment to protecting and strengthening the social safety net that so many Pennsylvanians rely on.

**Social justice remains a top priority for Senator Hughes**
Senator Hughes has always been an advocate for policies that uplift vulnerable populations and ensure that all Pennsylvanians have access to the care and support they need.
As we started to feel the impact of the chaos and cuts that were coming out of Washington DC in President Trump's second term, Senator Hughes stayed relentless in speaking out for the need to stop federal cuts. He's done everything he can at the state level to push back against cuts to healthcare, SNAP benefits, and social support programs.

**We are stronger together**
Senator Hughes also stands with [the dedicated professionals who serve the community each day](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17596), championing the workforce that is on the front lines of providing supports and services for vulnerable populations. He is committed to being an advocate for funding and legislation that pays these workers a living wage and allows them to live with dignity.

* * *

**Stay in Touch on Social Media**
If you haven't visited Senator Hughes' [Facebook page](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17597), join the conversation by 'liking' the page and following our office on [X](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17598), [Bluesky](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17599), [Instagram](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17600), and [TikTok](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17602). We have lots of information available on these pages about community events and issues affecting our district. If you have questions or concerns, send us an email at [hughes@pasenate.com](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171984.172929.113&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17589).

body:
Under the guise of an event to honor our troops it is ILLEGAL and blatantly INSULTING. Any junior officer who pulled this stunt would be relieved of duties on the spot!
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MBm3ObRrJW2V4lxMvEWvJok4G2KoAzwl3vLFm2KeT3KS_LhA0bPM1LzhWCzj8BRq-ZJ3JnRlfQLije2mV7RL_v0nu0Us77HxWhwCZn9VZrcKC68NM-WX5f3R5BXWvoGAutfn_AGQWK75nYynFjEDNKC9_kyqIPB95HUeiM6h-rXuzEIyVn7JS4Mj4vkXk6NtCR6L9TAZv22j0WFnUkmofYLEAxMoUhLh&c=9ixlYV2SdNc8lyhrerugaQMh6yOgpiEgw32aQhw8HBLdbHVU5V678A==&ch=B2n4MeqEfow5XoQgkwTc8SuxJLUrJ1YgYRamHue2kbOyhvbqSEK2fg==)
---
| Peter,
Last week, Donald Trump came to my backyard to do something FLAT OUT ILLEGAL:
Under the guise of an event to honor our troops, the draft-dodger-in-Chief stopped by and hosted a full-blown campaign rally.
Rather than offering words of gratitude for their bravery and sacrifice, Trump chose to bring my opponent Richard Hudson on stage and tell the soldiers who they should vote for, demanding, "YOU HAVE TO VOTE FOR US."
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MBm3ObRrJW2V4lxMvEWvJok4G2KoAzwl3vLFm2KeT3KS_LhA0bPM1LzhWCzj8BRq-ZJ3JnRlfQLije2mV7RL_v0nu0Us77HxWhwCZn9VZrcKC68NM-WX5f3R5BXWvoGAutfn_AGQWK75nYynFjEDNKC9_kyqIPB95HUeiM6h-rXuzEIyVn7JS4Mj4vkXk6NtCR6L9TAZv23pj_V3CLofknfkDaX3yf0n&c=9ixlYV2SdNc8lyhrerugaQMh6yOgpiEgw32aQhw8HBLdbHVU5V678A==&ch=B2n4MeqEfow5XoQgkwTc8SuxJLUrJ1YgYRamHue2kbOyhvbqSEK2fg==)
---
As someone who served for 24 years, let me be clear: that violates federal law, DoD regulations, and the core principle of nonpartisanship for our military!!
It is ILLEGAL and blatantly INSULTING to tell the men and women who protect our freedoms who they should or should not vote for. To tell them that they should not enjoy that freedom.
ANY junior officer who pulled this stunt would be relieved of duties on the spot!
I've trained soldiers on these rules. I've held people accountable when they violated them.
And I'll be damned if I let Trump use my own brothers and sisters in arms as props for his failing political career.
My years of service will not be in vain and neither will theirs. I will not sit idly by while we are being fundamentally disrespected. ## Supreme Court Strikes Down Hawaii Gun Law
The Supreme Court on Thursday [struck down](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiPTAw0EDi4hm0svRB67gT4ZG9lmrNmvX7G_sFlJJVW9qn_P5anZsd_-6oNUXsPiqSRHOVNctstHSjmyyRx8eFPMV_RkzQISUEgUgIvV7D5LV1u1EgE9alLtMEKHY49DvatB9riasX11dpSgaZTjJBG6DjTayUw1qztNImAr5QR907_Irv2IjxVbi3qoOkmWc4jN_8A-77S6zw3TmHDUTu05n6l6_KlgrmAupTTmle4Vt1_BfMsK5nSdkQ4SJlwxi10XzSy2ywuniyjBrSFa8RYunPQlLBlOHHwFcx2VPQs7xwlvlO3Q7H6q86_-eiv4DgAA___mQoFJ) a Hawaii law barring concealed-carry holders from bringing guns into public-facing businesses without the owner's permission. The vote was 6-3. Critics called it the "[vampire rule](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpSAYBeCn0Q6DqKgFxTZ2d9stDcKP_hsEA7-XuW8_cV5h6pOcfOf8e60vjR7D_lefoMjFNUDJHoggrfsdEmRKaAhjiG9IdKcA1qyCC8m4ZEKuVqP_rH1tlQMQ0NWg2nESvZwGOdaHctC7ru2kdsZO3chnM7VOz9vGu1nIdqtRPW1cCtlyPouhGTawbphk52RrpR6rnoNFiqn5HzHQAc5_Hkxj4ll7dRBduer-VGKpxFJKaVz8elY8eSWWK3okNLkSS76vBCcwE-9ELIOJwTJ9QrAnBGIFAzMxGNAeLDM6pQ_b_A0skyZg-x3YoYtGrJOyV0HvMcuHt58a_Q-HfvXhW4nvAAAA__-uTYpa)," since gun owners needed an invitation to enter shops or restaurants. Hawaii adopted it after a 2022 Supreme Court ruling broadened the right to carry. In the majority opinion, Justice Samuel Alito wrote that the law hobbled Second Amendment rights, exposing lawful carriers to criminal charges for routine errands. [Read the majority opinion here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuhDAQBNCvge6QvYfXpHCRhu7SprR8eM1tZGxkDOj-PiK_kGq6eaP5ftiH48hp_nILmRqyTXRukWqlYuc9Fdpq4alyTvmgUveSyE8WBOBN4A3QesfxbfvWm0AEdG_JSD1Aj4NC3b6M8loQDVrSU2qH9JRuCCqgBtQ9atGyudoEAkohPkB16kk-qAHvAaVHp5tekOeaS_eTOdUXhfi-xnRTXtpoXrWuW3P_bGBsYDzPs9v2tdBCU95L7eZ8NDDmlRPntDUwglp9uLK_SdGjTQvnbvWhLcavJ8fIG17mvDiOf0b91zGHgd8AAAD__16Id54). Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, joined by Justice Sonia Sotomayor, [filed a dissent](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb8GNpB5mBcYPHRhS9eOlrGfiSvHjuyXoPTrK_oLne_VuVfn66qvJsSQ9k9zJ8U-60RHjcRMRe_PVKhyCZZDTvlFhZ8lkbMaBGAnsAPUzoT41rJ1yhMBjS2p4TKDxHnCS3tT5GECKf2ybDhKsLT4cVsWKQbc0Pi5DeqkCQQchFhg6qeNnJ9mHD0ODs2lkYJc4Fz67xwS38jH93mmt_neRnVjftRm_GhgbWA9jqOvNvOzbjHvZ6WB1ZpK9Qxz9Lm47tXF_KCfBta2KPc4Qoyh4jm0302If2D-l42Xgt8AAAD__7JmdMw), calling it a property-rights dispute. The ruling could threaten similar restrictions in New York and California.
## Twin Quakes Devastate Venezuela
Two powerful earthquakes [struck northern Venezuela](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGSnDAQRU8jMk2JHhAQKHBCNk4dUj2oBbI1EpYaqNnTb7F7hE066V-v3v9_HtMDffBx-Y0vMuzSFOksgZgpT8seMxXOfmafYjoo854j2XkCBVoqLUFPFn14T01ljSMCuldk6q6HRvet7qrV6Gboh27o6sbW-LRW9zU5183PHq3Cvqu8uWhKg66VGqC9tU-yru313enaauxEo8h6Tvn2N_nIK7nwvmRuc3pVwazMWxH3XwJGAWN8b6nw9RIwXmABo7oOtALGM-Vg5VVRwHhQpI-dAkrCzOv_Hf9RkcEfJPfNIlOR6JiytHRgYWQfF8mnj_I7KmCssrHb6UPwRV-eywt9-PLiH415GPgMAAD__5DvisU) within a minute of each other on Wednesday, killing at least 188 people and injuring over 1,500. Measured at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, the back-to-back quakes were the country's strongest in over a century. Photos show apartment blocks folded into rubble, with families sleeping in the streets for fear of aftershocks. [See photos here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3unDAQBfDTmM4rf2GgcBEpQkqxaVOiwR7AibE3ZtjV5vQRe4V_PZqn33u_7tMdYop5_Qk7OlrKlPF1JCTCOq1nrnhQjZ5iyeWJlc6aMfhJCWW5sFzZKUBM78k0wS2ICnWDTna9MrZvbddsDhYpbfBoZ6u1nwcrOxDoTWeEwUWLJrorTVhlpRCDam_tjGFpe6sXK4OFjhmBIVKpt98lZtpwSe8Lc_Nlb5LbiB4H09-YGpkaYfZXg-vG1PgjE9YMFx8SU-NBteSVd5LvsOZIZ0COUGn7e8If5BV9qQED9wUO4k_M-O_EBJ_PUt9MjzEw_V1qI_t2GExTXXi8YkrxsJdz3SGmj4u-NObTqf8BAAD__0fXiro). President Trump pledged American aid, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. is [rushing rescue teams](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFypDAQRL9GZGyhAQkIFFxCtpdeSA1oWOYspLUYdgt_vQv_guOu6n79_t3HO3Lg-PiLGzlZ0hjpvQcSoTw-jphpl8yzcIrpRVmOHMnPI1Rgy8qWYEePHM6xKbxbiIDqgpxuO2hsZ2xbrK5tTW3qyda6m7SmdpoW1I0hj33XaLMU7K62yoLVVdWDuZmJ_GI6Wy9We4utairyLCnf_ieOstISzgvmNqetCG4Vee6q_qNgUDDISiuHcGUKhmcKPJ8KBo5COeL1A4OCwfRN1euuPPZy48CC-SyRffmiSF8HBSwJs6yfB37QrmAosvPPN4fAu72AHhvyz0ghv7L2cvAdAAD__6Y4gq0) and supplies to help with disaster recovery. Brazil, Mexico, and El Salvador are also sending crews. The toll is expected to climb. The [U.S. Geological Survey warned](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyszAQhJ8GOjHSIQQUKv7Gnf82JXNGJ6NYSI44zDhPnyGvkH5nv93v4zpdMcSQ7v9xJcs-T4mOLRIzlem-p0IblzBzyCm_qPBeErl5AglGSCPATA5DfE-6dtYTAbU1WdUPoM3Qmb5ebCu1Q5Sj152GoRtJ-ptHpcipsdVAdbBnmzRglJQjdE13I-e7wbTeKGewr7QkFziX5jOHxAv5-D7HNHNe62gX5udWtf8quFRwOY6jOS8cRI8zUMGFsPDyteODxIsSfe8UUaw5McYbJtELJWYsOOMmFCjVg1J1se55hBjDZk7-fcUQf3n8J0kvCz8BAAD__2eifE0) the total number of deaths could keep growing, with dozens of aftershocks still rattling the region.
## Amazon Beats Walmart as Biggest Company
Amazon dethroned Walmart as [America's biggest company](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMlFCiDEOFFxC5ksvpMZowHMrJEoam_J-_Rb-hc27ul-_f7fphhw4rn9xIydLmiIdJZAI5Wl9xkxFMs_CKaYXZXnmSH6ejDagNCgDk0cO78nW3i1EhrqaXHsZjIWhh0v9cLYjc--1JW1xsK0fehjgCp1uCdEOULM72zQYaLW-mr7p7-SXfoBugdYDXiqrybOk3PxPHOVBS3ifMM2ctjq4h8hequ5PZcbKjMdxNC8uTwwz7iwYuMgZrMyIG36nqD4_8IuKOjBsmEVhUbhR5hmLuvO6UhE1p23H-K7MWGfn94ND4AIny7ohh8-2_ErYy5mfAAAA__-2k4JX), taking the top spot on the Fortune 500 this month for the first time. It was close: Amazon brought in $716.9 billion in revenue last year, narrowly edging Walmart's $713.2 billion. Walmart has been the nation's biggest company for the past 13 years. The climb is the real story. Amazon first joined the list at No. 492 about two decades ago, and is just the fourth company ever to reach the summit as the nation's biggest company. The others were General Motors, ExxonMobil, and Walmart itself, now in second place as e-commerce and cloud computing reshape the economy. [See the full chart here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMlFCiDEOFFxC5ksvpMZowHMrJEoam_J-_Rb-hc27ul-_f7fphhw4rn9xIydLmiIdJZAI5Wl9xkxFMs_CKaYXZXnmSH6ejDagNCgDk0cO78nW3i1EhrqaXHsZjIWhh0v9cLYjc--1JW1xsK0fehjgCp1uCdEOULM72zQYaLW-mr7p7-SXfoBugdYDXiqrybOk3PxPHOVBS3ifMM2ctjq4h8hequ5PZcbKjMdxNC8uTwwz7iwYuMgZrMyIG36nqD4_8IuKOjBsmEVhUbhR5hmLuvO6UhE1p23H-K7MWGfn94ND4AIny7ohh8-2_ErYy5mfAAAA__-2k4JX).

## Texas Medicare Fraud Bust
Federal prosecutors unsealed an indictment accusing a [Texas-linked network](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQBuDT4A4LBh52CorXuMu2W1pjGBIkHEeA4-T2KyztCbaF_5_RN9_X-YoxxcftC1ey9R22-UFHSVQr5XklHx1mChl3v-ylesx12YubQYDhwnAws8eYPrPuvF2Ev8iOrBxG0IMcQXV3S16MTsGgL6MhIUelEQf1TxrndNAaumjbMGHASCmUGvpLAAQXABVp5dXItCAf65b7eqdKbywhfbYX5d5ta5fsvdZnYeo_g4nBdBxH75bSFO2fwXRWGEzticH0i-JLTE3OTx1vPH5GeeSVsDW7bP3zaLFiBqbFbcWYzq31b7d6WfgJAAD__2gZfsM) of generating $3.7 billion in false Medicare claims, among the largest health care fraud cases ever prosecuted. Alleged leader Ibrahim Khaldoon Hilmi, arrested in Northern Cyprus, was [returned to the United States](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L_OozAQBPCngc7IrB3-FC6uocu1V6LFXoMVEyJ7HZK3PyXS9wRfPdJofvPvOl8xxHBf_-JOhl_-mO905kjMlOadXLCYyCcsbimZHSZeSrYzSOiE7AR0s8MQ37OunVmkG9uaTNsPoPt2AFVvZlCttF5e9KCklr2DERQOl4vT2nVejnUwnzLZQde2Uqm-GT0gWA-oSCunhkpLcoGP1PBGTC_MPr6PJ6XGHnsdzcb8yJX6U8FUwXSeZ-OP10fxySuYSq5g8ksQSwr3NYsF7U34sgYOTxJobcnkhOoX8eMVX7DIdqOdhMUHl0SCS7rRu07GPc4QY8hdX2m57hjidwn_7r-ngf8BAAD__4QAhn0) last week. He and his co-conspirators allegedly took over [shell companies](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3SmzAQRZ9GdDDSQvgpVKShc9qUzMKu0E6E5ZEEtt8-Y7_CV93unjPn7225oQS573_wYFteLi53fubApXBaDibZMLFLeNJ65kKYynrmbQENfa37GvqFUMJ76Sqyq6bJVGzNMEI3mBHaylvikX85XIe1myaajHGjQU3DOE08koNK7OdM99Abo9t2aCYHCJsDbLlrqR1Vp5mkxNQUz4VfmF14x4tTs8WjCtaX8siq_a1gVjBH2Rvvc7PHS8H8Nf_suUuRi7OCWdaEXo76n8dAMd5rL-EQBXOVLD2eEoLkflCd3g-U8IWUn6W5LPwPAAD__wvyeXc), billed Medicare and private insurers for medical equipment that was never ordered or delivered, and then wired the proceeds overseas. [Investigators](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAMQE8TuiBwwl-RYhu62XZLZBJniBR-FIdh5vYrZrUn-Fo_2fJ7fx7TA0MM2_M3rmTy2-_TRhdHypnStJILFhP5hKebT84OU55PthNU0MqqldBODkP8TLpwZq7cUBdk6q4H3dU9qGIxpKxteqsBW6z10FhUjXWD8g5132gqgrmPVS20dV0p1ZWDBwTrARVp5VQvdEUu5D2VeaFMb2QfP_uLUmn3tYhmyflgoX4JGAWM13WVdubb4uYCxu-KgPEeCRjTyRxwk-nc5BfJf5pR8nkcMVCSKzKHF8n__nIO8Y4k2S60kvTkWDJ-BIxFMu64bsxtJ3T1XDHE72P5ZzlfBv4GAAD__2cnjYE) traced the operation to Centurion Superior Medical, an Austin supplier that billed Medicare for 78,663 items, mostly urinary catheters, in just over a month. Co-conspirator Nika Machutadze was arrested in January in Austin. ## Texas Faces $826M SNAP Cost Shift
The USDA's payment-error figures, released Wednesday, lock Texas into paying roughly $826 million a year toward SNAP starting in 2027. The 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act now requires states to [share food-benefit costs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8Gd1hw4IJdUNzGXbbd0jo2hwQt_hHgOHn7lfMKW44-zYxmvm_jDWOK6_0LF3L1FbZxpbMkqpXyuJCPM2YKGQ8_HaV6zHU6yjyCAMOF4WBGjzG9R914Nwnfy4actB1oKztQzcOpTgOGfyp0vZnIgLUzTlOvpZqtlyI00V1hwoCRUihl2z4AwhwAFWnlVce0IB_rltv6oEovLCG9tyfldt6WJrlHrXth6j-DgcFwnmf788L1ggyGaw2D4WNjMBzFIy8r7pxy3jLPWKnwD-VnTInv-GYwNNn5_dKxGMu0uC8Y06eu_u2kp4PfAAAA__93u3zF) when their payment error rate exceeds 6%. Texas came in at 9.34%, below the 10% line that would have meant a bigger bill. Of the $826 million, about $709 million covers benefits, and $117 million covers administrative costs the state now shoulders. | Letter from the Chair

Together, We Win!
While New York City grabs headlines for electing multiple candidates, both federally and locally, that are fully backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), Nebraskans should know the same movement is already organizing here. DSA has active chapters in Omaha and Lincoln working to push the same agenda that just took hold in America's largest city into The Good Life.
And it's not just DSA. This month, Courier Newsroom officially launched its Nebraska operation, a so-called "news" outlet bankrolled by George Soros and Reid Hoffman that openly admits it isn't interested in objectivity. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. [Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=203259419&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAzMjU5NDE5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODI0Nzg1OTEsImV4cCI6MTc4NTA3MDU5MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.KiypWVXN06Dsb_WHyolPS2sSDG9-8Lo0Y5v0ubz18VU)
* * *
I recently wrote about Missouri's brazen power grab to curtail the right that Missourians have to propose and pass constitutional amendments via ballot measures:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5b3a00a0-8b8c-4e37-984d-3c49e514b5a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Voters vs. lawmakers](https://substack.com/redirect/5b3a00a0-8b8c-4e37-984d-3c49e514b5a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| Feb 25
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/5b3a00a0-8b8c-4e37-984d-3c49e514b5a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In August, the Missouri legislature is asking voters to make it functionally impossible to pass constitutional amendments proposed directly by its citizens. How?
* Currently, citizen-initiated constitutional amendments pass if they win a majority of votes.
* Under the proposed new scheme, citizen-initiated amendments would only pass if they win a majority in **all of the state 's congressional districts**.

There are a few things that are particularly absurd about this proposal:
1. It only applies to citizen-initiated amendments. The legislature also has the right to refer amendments, and these rules wouldn't apply to them. **The legislature is weakening the power of voters while preserving its own power**.
2. Missouri is aggressively gerrymandered, which means that the congressional districts aren't at all reflective of the state's communities.
3. "[As few as 5% of voters could defeat initiative petitions](https://substack.com/redirect/ad4b4888-bc2d-4a2a-8ae5-b6911bcad7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" under this new scheme.

This proposed change is pretty technical, but it's seismic in its impact.
The ballot measure process, [as I've written about](https://substack.com/redirect/5b3a00a0-8b8c-4e37-984d-3c49e514b5a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is hardly perfect. But **Amendment 4 would functionally end the right that citizens have to initiate and pass ballot measures** , which for more than a century has been a critical check on our state legislature.1
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjAzMjU5NDE5LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzgyNDc4NTkxLCJleHAiOjIwOTgwNTQ1OTEsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.yQZpMuwT9tGuowWL5yMCDJ-pEvO_gveNoYgCRnDTGa4?)
### Why the ballot measure process is important
Flawed though it may be, it's worth reflecting on the fact that citizen-initiated constitutional amendments have radically changed the state for the better. Here are a few, wide-ranging examples of what voters have accomplished with ballot measures over the last century.
* [1924](https://substack.com/redirect/9ec20283-e921-44a4-8f00-2b295914c520?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): The state's highway system was funded, in large measure, by an amendment initiated and passed by citizens.
* [1936](https://substack.com/redirect/e1b54e50-7a35-4472-8f80-28342234cf51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): Voters adopted a plan to create the nonpartisan [Missouri Conservation Commission](https://substack.com/redirect/52ff46a5-01c4-4fd0-8b23-4cca8dc42621?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that manages the state's hunting and fishing licenses, wildlife, and conservation policies. Before this amendment passed, jobs managing the state's wildlife were given out as political patronage to people who had no experience at all, and [as a result](https://substack.com/redirect/7239bcc0-8731-4183-943c-ebb48d0dd270?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "fish and wildlife in Missouri were in calamitous decline" until this amendment was adopted.2
* [1940](https://substack.com/redirect/3a30f17a-8460-45ce-9056-daf3792c3413?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): Voters adopted a nonpartisan process for selecting judges so successful that other states later adopted what's now known as the "[Missouri Plan](https://substack.com/redirect/77b9b4eb-1d06-4185-b06c-205599d36920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."3
* [1974](https://substack.com/redirect/d7fb902b-6d95-4e17-ae98-ebef5639870e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): Voters approved campaign finance reforms that included disclosing donors and limiting contributions.4
* [1992](https://substack.com/redirect/2b9e582d-118f-4847-9554-40c1627deb10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): A voter-initiated amendment created term limits for elected officials in Jefferson City.
* [2020](https://substack.com/redirect/5c6da8bf-0c10-4fbf-bc3a-a5aa9046b540?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): Voters expanded Medicaid eligibility, and as a result, [146,000 Missourians](https://substack.com/redirect/b7a9b1bc-2c96-4371-9437-7e6cb927a5e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who previously lacked insurance are now covered--a change that results in [more financial security and better health outcomes](https://substack.com/redirect/c8ff8305-de3b-4f69-954c-556295b03a3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across the state.

It's also a reminder: these aren't partisan issues.5 There's a tendency to focus on recent partisan victories--abortion access, legalized marijuana, etc.--but the examples above are just a few of the lasting, nonpartisan policy wins that either:
1. Limited legislative power and/or corruption; or
2. Went around the legislature when it wasn't doing its job.

That's really important. And if Amendment 4 passes, these checks go away.

### Amendment 4 would end citizen-initiated amendments
If the system worked the way it should, voters would have their say in policymaking by electing representatives in Jefferson City.
In practice, because of gerrymandering, gridlock, personal incentives, primary dynamics, and more, elected officials aren't always that good at representing our interests. That's especially true in Missouri, where legislators are [objectively getting worse at legislating](https://substack.com/redirect/e2622053-fbae-4a55-b1ba-db0ca5919fd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The ballot measure process is one way that we hold elected officials accountable. But if Amendment 4 passes, we lose that check on legislative power.
Yes, the Missouri legislature has found ways to slow down or stop the policies that voters have enacted. But this is _much_ more extreme. The legislature is tired of fighting back against everything that voters pass; why not make it impossible for voters to pass amendments altogether?6
### Congressional districts don't represent Missourians
What Amendment 4 supporters claim is that this change requires constitutional amendments to have broad buy-in from across the state. Perhaps that would be true if congressional districts were drawn in a fair, representative way.
But they aren't. Missouri is a Republican state, with [Trump having won 58.5%](https://substack.com/redirect/84cf98f5-a701-4285-a6e3-3c019ac32754?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the vote. But Republicans don't control that proportion of U.S. House seats; by November, they'll likely control 87.5% of the U.S. House seats, and it's not inconceivable to think that it'll go to 100% by the '28 elections.7
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3111b5a-8b27-4aca-b2f0-aab3eca7d022?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What does all of this mean in practice? Under Amendment 4, every congressional district has veto power. **Even if a majority of the state votes in favor, and even if six of the seven Republican districts in the state vote in favor, a citizen-initiated ballot measure will** _**still**_**fail.** That's bad for everyone--Democrats and independents, obviously, but also for Republicans, whose proposed amendments would still face an insurmountable hurdle because of veto power from MO-01 or _any_ Republican district.8
The structure the legislature is proposing via Amendment 4 puts a hat on a hat:
1. Forcing a ballot measure to pass in eight U.S. congressional districts is already an enormous, unreasonable burden that gives [tiny pockets of Missourians functional veto power](https://substack.com/redirect/ad4b4888-bc2d-4a2a-8ae5-b6911bcad7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
2. Because of how aggressively the state is gerrymandered, the already-slim chance of passing a citizen-initiated amendment becomes even slimmer, because voters in cities and suburbs have had their preferences diluted by partisan mapmakers.

### Rules for thee, not for me
Perhaps the most ridiculous part of Amendment 4 is that it only applies to amendments initiated by voters; **these constraints don 't apply to amendments referred by the legislature**. They're hamstringing our ability as Missourians to change the constitution, but they're keeping the old rules for themselves.
This is, of course, on brand for Missouri, which has for years thrown sand in the gears on everything from [nonpartisan redistricting](https://substack.com/redirect/0a23a871-cbb3-4cb2-bac3-1e523550e8a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [Medicaid expansion](https://substack.com/redirect/d6f9e94e-0d4b-4576-a38c-5355d9b3fafe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [abortion access](https://substack.com/redirect/a11f92e0-e488-4bec-9abe-7ecab4aa621e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) despite all three being--empirically--policies that voters want.
Our state government does hypocrisy pretty well too. Governor Mike Kehoe has complained that funding to defeat Amendment 4 has come from "out-of-state special interests"--never mind that he's doing [literally the exact same thing for Amendment 5](https://substack.com/redirect/9c45ff26-da82-4018-9243-c5460e9832ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Rules for thee, not for me.
Hypocrisy is nothing new in politics. But Amendment 4 would be something new: something bad for voters and something that ends a critical check on legislative power.

1
It was originally written in a way that was intended to deceive. Here was the original language:
> Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to:
> * Stop foreign nationals and foreign adversaries of the United States from providing funding to influence ballot measure elections, and allow criminal prosecution of violators;
> * Punish initiative petition signature fraud as a crime;
> * Require public hearings be held to get public comment before initiative petitions are placed on the ballot;
> * Require a majority of voters in each congressional district to approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; and
> * Make available to each voter the full text of initiative petitions with their ballot?
>

The true crux of the amendment is buried in the fourth bullet point; the first three are already laws. That has since been changed [by the Circuit Court of Cole County](https://substack.com/redirect/9aad1b98-a2d7-473b-aca6-1bf863538857?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to much fairer and more neutral language:
> Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to:
> * Modify current requirements that a statewide majority of voters may approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution;
> * Require a majority of voters in each congressional district to approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; and
> * Make available to each voter the full text of initiative petitions with their ballot?
>

But it's all part of a broader pattern of Missouri's Secretary of State [intentionally trying to deceive voters](https://substack.com/redirect/4396904f-e4c3-4176-9ce2-d2416c5d4fc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
2
For good measure, when the state still wasn't doing enough to protect fish and game in the state, voters initiated and passed [another amendment in 1976](https://substack.com/redirect/dfa58e4b-f17b-483c-8838-ca59a30ef0a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to shore up protections.
3
This is a good example of the impact that Amendment 4 would have. Under Amendment 4, this constitutional amendment wouldn't have passed because it didn't get support from every congressional district. (Sources: the [Official Manual of the State of Missouri 1941-1942](https://substack.com/redirect/9c389813-cccd-4539-b23b-ef21377539e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [ChatGPT](https://substack.com/redirect/dc61fa21-82c2-4a5e-b985-3cd3adfeec24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
Not only was it such a positive reform that it's been replicated across the country, but it also benefited Republicans in Missouri for decades, when the Democrats had [fairly uniform control of statewide bodies and offices](https://substack.com/redirect/f5235220-9c55-4a47-821c-0feb14290f2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
4
Those reforms were reinforced in a citizen-initiated [constitutional amendment in 2016](https://substack.com/redirect/f0b094ee-dd42-4c15-a38d-b858305b49ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
5
Of course, plenty of fights that were partisan then don't seem partisan now. [Amendment 2 in 2006](https://substack.com/redirect/d2d4907d-7fe3-451e-83ec-6aef75a9668f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) comes to mind, which I mostly remember because [its ads (and the general narrative)](https://substack.com/redirect/54f082c0-c97f-481d-b982-4df1f50668a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) were ubiquitous during the [2006 World Series](https://substack.com/redirect/47d9bde7-3cc2-4195-b3a8-4c615e456939?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), even nationally.
6
Here are three citizen-initiated constitutional amendments from the last three cycles. All had support from a majority of the state, and all would fail under Amendment 4, whose thresholds are impossibly high.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c31206ef-5a1b-47c2-b5a6-2d84a65521bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
7
First of all, here are sources for [MO-01](https://substack.com/redirect/bb006cfd-d4c7-440e-9521-a35c4abb674c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-02](https://substack.com/redirect/eb8410c4-f6b8-4352-89eb-95c77751fab3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-03](https://substack.com/redirect/4ed996f5-be3a-47be-be20-087186b25ad7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-04](https://substack.com/redirect/2d7282ee-f0a1-445b-9144-1e6313293811?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-05](https://substack.com/redirect/5df52962-0b4c-4abc-9705-c3a3a95c4655?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-06](https://substack.com/redirect/a0922d08-48d3-4255-ad3c-d3c665a66f75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [MO-07](https://substack.com/redirect/cd26cf82-8fcb-42e1-850b-2305826acb96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [MO-08](https://substack.com/redirect/7be50620-7be7-481a-a8f8-594208c26a74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And second: with the VRA protections for majority-minority districts having been thrown out by the Supreme Court, I think there's a chance they try to carve up St. Louis and make it a Republican-leaning seat.
8
Today, when it comes to ballot measures, voters in Kansas City, Hannibal, and Van Buren all have an equal vote. That's how it should be: we're voting on changes to the state constitution that impact all of us.
But this changes that paradigm completely. Kansas City--whose [growth is driving the state forward](https://substack.com/redirect/4c019d85-e5d4-4469-a888-7f45efc8f00d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--will have hardly any say, because its votes will be split across three congressional districts.

They're hamstringing our ability as Missourians to change the constitution, but they're keeping the old rules for themselves. This is, of course, on brand for Missouri, which has for years thrown sand in the gears on everything from to to despite all three being--empirically--policies that voters want. Our state government does hypocrisy pretty well too. Governor Mike Kehoe has complained that funding to defeat Amendment 4 has come from "out-of-state special interests"--never mind that he's doing . Rules for thee, not for me. Hypocrisy is nothing new in politics. But Amendment 4 would be something new: something bad for voters and something that ends a critical check on legislative power. ? Share this post with Missourians and encourage them to vote in the August 4 primary election. If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, . Here's what I wrote last time about Amendment 5, another bad policy on the August 4 ballot: | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Jun 11 | 1 It was originally written in a way that was intended to deceive. Here was the original language: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: Stop foreign nationals and foreign adversaries of the United States from providing funding to influence ballot measure elections, and allow criminal prosecution of violators; Punish initiative petition signature fraud as a crime; Require public hearings be held to get public comment before initiative petitions are placed on the ballot; Require a majority of voters in each congressional district to approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; and Make available to each voter the full text of initiative petitions with their ballot? The true crux of the amendment is buried in the fourth bullet point; the first three are already laws. That has since been changed to much fairer and more neutral language: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: Modify current requirements that a statewide majority of voters may approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; Require a majority of voters in each congressional district to approve initiative petitions to amend the constitution; and * Make available to each voter the full text of initiative petitions with their ballot? But it's all part of a broader pattern of Missouri's Secretary of State . 2 For good measure, when the state still wasn't doing enough to protect fish and game in the state, voters initiated and passed to shore up protections. 3 This is a good example of the impact that Amendment 4 would have. Under Amendment 4, this constitutional amendment wouldn't have passed because it didn't get support from every congressional district. (Sources: the and .) Not only was it such a positive reform that it's been replicated across the country, but it also benefited Republicans in Missouri for decades, when the Democrats had . 4 Those reforms were reinforced in a citizen-initiated . 5 Of course, plenty of fights that were partisan then don't seem partisan now. comes to mind, which I mostly remember because were ubiquitous during the , even nationally. 6 Here are three citizen-initiated constitutional amendments from the last three cycles. All had support from a majority of the state, and all would fail under Amendment 4, whose thresholds are impossibly high. | | ---|---|--- 7 First of all, here are sources for , , , , , , , and . And second: with the VRA protections for majority-minority districts having been thrown out by the Supreme Court, I think there's a chance they try to carve up St. Louis and make it a Republican-leaning seat. 8 Today, when it comes to ballot measures, voters in Kansas City, Hannibal, and Van Buren all have an equal vote. That's how it should be: we're voting on changes to the state constitution that impact all of us. But this changes that paradigm completely. Kansas City--whose have hardly any say, because its votes will be split across three congressional districts. | | | | | (C) 2026 Ben Samuels 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

name: Power the Polls
subject: Ever thought about working the polls? Here's what it's really like:
body:
| It's easier than you think -- and your community needs you. _You’re getting this message from[ _Power the Polls_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4508?t=1&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35) because you signed up to learn about serving as a poll worker. If you no longer wish to hear from us, [_please unsubscribe here_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9040.934366.-Vvi35&t=2&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35). Marking emails as spam can affect our ability to reach others with important information. _
# [](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/42?t=3&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35)
Hey Peter— "Poll worker" might sound intimidating and like a big commitment – but for most people, it's one long day, a small amount of training, and one of the most tangible ways to serve your community. [**Here's what it actually looks like:**](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4921?t=4&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35)
* **What’s the job?** Poll workers help check in voters, set up and close polling places, and make sure voting sites run smoothly during Early Vote and on Election. Depending on your state, you might be called an "election worker," "election judge," or something else entirely – but the role is the same.
* **How much time?** Most assignments are one day – Election Day itself. Most locations also ask for a few hours of training beforehand, usually on a weekend or evening. If you have time to serve more, then you might be a good fit for running an early voting site, these assignments generally last a week or two.
* **What’s the pay?** Yes, you get paid in most states! Most poll workers earn between $100–$300 for the day.
* **Am I qualified?** In most states you just need to be a registered voter in that county or state, a U.S. citizen, and able to commit to a full day, but it varies by jurisdiction.
* **Done this before?** You need to apply each year.

Ready to see the details for your area?**Enter your ZIP code at powerthepolls.org and we'll show you exactly how to apply in your state — it takes less than five minutes.** [Get started in your state](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4888?t=5&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35) More to come soon, —Power the Polls
---
* * *
This email was sent to [dpwillis67@gmail.com](mailto:dpwillis67@gmail.com). You received this message because you are subscribed to Power the Polls' mailing list. [Click here to unsubscribe.](https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?ak_proof=1&akid=9040.934366.-Vvi35&t=6&akid=9040%2E934366%2E-Vvi35) If you have any questions, please contact us at [info@powerthepolls.org](mailto:info@powerthepolls.org) and a member of our team will be in touch.

name: Dylan for Wisconsin
subject: A Pride Month Note From Dylan
body:
Happy Pride Month!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/3f8483cfa153/c2y1sg9w12-10123127?e=f59034ca3e)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/_dYYKi9X3Ty?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| | | | | | Hi Peter,

Happy Pride Month!
I was honored to speak at Milwaukee PrideFest earlier this month and to share the stage with JoCasta Zamarripa, who’s running for Secretary of State! I’m also proud to share that our campaign was just endorsed by Fair Wisconsin, a leading voice for LGBTQ+ equality across our state.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/aF_GUw0hrTl?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| |

Pride Month is a celebration of LGBTQ+ joy, resilience, and the ongoing fight for equality for everyone. It’s also a reminder that the work of building a more inclusive Wisconsin continues all year long.
Pride began as a protest, and that history matters. Actions like raising the Pride flag and having Pridefests are important symbols of inclusion and a reminder that there’s still work to do to build a future where everyone feels welcome and able to be their true self. This year, Pride feels more important than ever.
I’ve seen that progress firsthand as the first elected LGBTQ+ school board member and village trustee in my rural hometown. When I ran, some doubted a queer candidate could win. Instead, I found neighbors who believed in fairness, respect, and showing up for one another.
Representation matters. It shapes who feels welcome to participate and sends a simple, powerful message: you belong here. That belief helps drive my run for State Treasurer – to help build a Wisconsin where our government reflects the people it serves and public power is used for the public good.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/khftr4rK4NU?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
| |
The next few days will help determine what kind of campaign we’re able to run. With our June 30 fundraising deadline quickly approaching, this is a pivotal moment to make sure we have the resources we need to keep building momentum statewide.
[**If you’re able, I hope you’ll consider donating before June 30. Your support helps us reach voters across Wisconsin, show up in communities across the state, and continue fighting for a future where everyone feels included and able to be their true selves.**](https://us.list-manage.com/bTCtK0Rd7OA?e=f59034ca3e&c2id=997c4beee76ce03997da9db4fe50bd09)
Thank you for your continued support!
Best,Dylan

name: Hanks for Colorado
subject: Proven Service over Polished Mailers
body:
My Appeal to Western and Southern Colorado

| | | | | [|
---](https://hanksforcolorado.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8015ade0e781cf96f029a35b&id=4601e8e9b2&e=934ceb4302)
| | | | | | **Proven Service over Polished Mailers****My Appeal to Western & Southern Colorado**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
My Fellow Conservatives,
If the system was working, I wouldn’t be running.
If we had a real conservative in office, I would be applauding him. But we don’t. We have a 59% “F” rated Republican who has strayed from our conservative values. Mailers by the dozen and phony social media posts don’t change his voting record. His Big Money handlers hope you’ll read “conservative” on a mailer and believe it long enough to vote for him.
President Trump has the agenda to clean up Washington, strengthen the economy and secure our nation. But he has just two years left to get it done. Our congressman has already slowed Trump down — and has zero obligation to do better. Worse still, Trump has no leverage over our “F” rated congressman going forward.
Agreements break easily in Washington. Look at Senator Thune blocking the SAVE Act — a bill 85% of Americans support. We’ve seen our trust broken here in CD3 as well. Just a few months ago, President Trump pulled his endorsement of our “F” rated congressman for breaking his trust.
Years ago, Ronald Reagan framed the right question: Are you better off today than you were two years ago?
Do you think the federal government should lock up more of our land? Put kill switches in your vehicles so bureaucrats decide if you can drive? Hide sexual misconduct cases involving members of Congress? Send more of our money to corrupt and unstable Ukraine? Take away President Trump’s tariff authority? Protect Ilhan Omar’s committee seats at the expense of Congress’s integrity? Let New York lawyers and D.C. lobbyists pour outside money into our races to buy the outcomes they want?
Because those are the positions of our “F” rated, NeverSeen/NeverHeard representative.
If you answer “Yes” to those questions, then you know for whom to cast your vote.
If your answers are “No” then I ask you to vote for me, **Ron Hanks** – on the **Top Line** of the ballot – to move the America First agenda as far as we can in the next two years.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
**MY COMMITMENT IS DEMONSTRATED AND ABSOLUTE**
I am a 32-year Air Force veteran who served as an Arabic linguist and Intelligence Officer. President Reagan was my first Commander in Chief. President Trump was my last. Service across four decades as a Citizen-Soldier cemented my faith in what this nation can and should be.
I served in the Colorado House as a Citizen-Legislator. While I was there I:
* Earned my “A” rating defending our 2nd Amendment – drafting bills for Constitutional Carry and to repeal magazine capacity limits.
* Drafted Election Integrity bills that pre-date the SAVE Act.
* Stood up for the unborn in the longest floor fight in Colorado history.
* Sought funding for water tanks for rural areas to fight wildfires more quickly and efficiently.

I have real-world experience that applies directly to our district. I’ve worked the oilfields in North Dakota, planted saplings in timber country, served in a volunteer fire department. I still run heavy equipment, and I still hold my trucker’s license.
I am beholden to no special interests. I seek no endorsements except from the voters of this district.
I have signed the Tax Pledge (from ATR), the Right to Work pledge, and the Term Limits pledge.
I have SHOWN UP for media interviews. My opponent has refused to do them – a direct insult to YOU, the voters of this district.
I offer unwavering conservative representation. I will represent this district in Washington, meet regularly with constituents, provide clear updates, listen closely to your concerns and seek your ideas for solutions.
President Trump needs fighters in Congress who will deliver America First in his final two years — not fake conservatives who work against him, in servitude to their Big Money handlers.
I am easy to find on the ballot. I’m **Top Line** on the ballot because I stood before the Republican Assembly. The other guy ran away.
I’m **Ron Hanks** , and I humbly ask for your vote. _Respectfully,__Ron_[ www.HanksForColorado.com](https://hanksforcolorado.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c8015ade0e781cf96f029a35b&id=e87b7649dd&e=934ceb4302)

name: Developing:
subject: Trump says military wants to restrict your right to vote
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DEFEND OUR COURTS, NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE
body:
Trump hasn’t hidden his desire to have the military get involved in elections, publicly refusing to roll out deploying the National Guard to voting locations ahead of the midterms.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0017wke0G2hnDvTQUOQULtrLYFSHCuXazcXK0kH2sbH9gyAVVgB8hXb3YmIbamF9lauVH3fzyRqVf36yuGzT379f8RY0A8rDPvJI61YQBCb_bMCQps8Hqo_e1zwOp4HSDcLXN6IeCASIl2kOtYqab1IPA5S0csjjq0R-CjZOdpgHELmeSrrtQN_Sh8_sfAnJPF0CtJ5YZg489drWTydmJX8DgeXIMMPjPOfowz1SB-dNpVqK64LzsI2tw==&c=Wmtm1a2lBLCS1eGI8hmurEjAN9qMfBhGIR9LY8b8MRxgWNV_eYJpew==&ch=8X5vdyfkAtzdxQjHJlgzVefvPTybaHbsMANSeffz7JFqFFhWueooXw==)
---
|
Peter,
Donald Trump took to Truth Social to push Congress to pass the "Save America" Act--the most heinous voting restrictions in the history of the country.
It has already failed to pass in the Senate, with some vulnerable MAGA Senators worried the bill would be so extreme that the backlash would cause them to lose their seats to Democrats.
But Trump has a new absolutely terrifying sales pitch--it's actually the military that wants to restrict your right to vote:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0017wke0G2hnDvTQUOQULtrLYFSHCuXazcXK0kH2sbH9gyAVVgB8hXb3YmIbamF9lauVH3fzyRqVf36yuGzT379f8RY0A8rDPvJI61YQBCb_bMCQps8Hqo_e1zwOp4HSDcLXN6IeCASIl2kOtYqab1IPA5S0csjjq0R-CjZOdpgHELmeSrrtQN_Sh8_sfAnJPF0CtJ5YZg489drWTydmJX8DgeXIMMPjPOfF5YhNQLb8xJj9MzTELjdww==&c=Wmtm1a2lBLCS1eGI8hmurEjAN9qMfBhGIR9LY8b8MRxgWNV_eYJpew==&ch=8X5vdyfkAtzdxQjHJlgzVefvPTybaHbsMANSeffz7JFqFFhWueooXw==)
---
Trump hasn't hidden his desire to have the military get involved in elections. Earlier this year, he refused to rule out deploying the National Guard to voting locations ahead of the midterms.
And how does the Pentagon's top brass feel about it? This was Pete Hegseth's response to Trump on social media:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0017wke0G2hnDvTQUOQULtrLYFSHCuXazcXK0kH2sbH9gyAVVgB8hXb3YmIbamF9lauVH3fzyRqVf36yuGzT379f8RY0A8rDPvJI61YQBCb_bMCQps8Hqo_e1zwOp4HSDcLXN6IeCASIl2kOtYqab1IPA5S0csjjq0R-CjZOdpgHELmeSrrtQN_Sh8_sfAnJPF0CtJ5YZg489drWTydmJX8DgeXIMMPjPOfP3_SiGlIWv1MBR6Twt5fnQ==&c=Wmtm1a2lBLCS1eGI8hmurEjAN9qMfBhGIR9LY8b8MRxgWNV_eYJpew==&ch=8X5vdyfkAtzdxQjHJlgzVefvPTybaHbsMANSeffz7JFqFFhWueooXw==)
---
These are dark, serious, and unprecedented threats.
Since the founding of this nation, the military has separated itself from partisan politics. It's a key tenet of the separation of powers and there are multiple laws and military directives preventing personnel from being used for political purposes. But Trump and Hegseth not only seemed prepared but intending to cross that rubicon.
Trump's assault on free and fair elections escalates every single day. While we don't know what the full picture of his plans for November look like, the pieces are coming together and it's not pretty. The gears are motion and he has the sycophants and crooks by his side ready and willing to do anything and everything necessary to make sure MAGA wins.

As we move through 2026, global markets continue to experience meaningful shifts . While media coverage often focuses on policy and geopolitical developments , there is also increasing discussion around physical supply and demand trends in the silver market.

For many years, silver has often been viewed in relation to gold. However, due to its industrial applications, some analysts now describe silver as playing a more expanded role in modern manufacturing and technology.

Market Perspective

Public figures, including Robert Kiyosaki, have recently shared opinions on the long-term outlook for silver. These views reflect personal perspectives and should not be interpreted as guarantees of future performance.

Key Market Considerations

Supply & Demand Trends: Reports have indicated increased industrial demand for silver, particularly in sectors such as electronics, energy, and defense-related technologies.

Multi-Year Supply Imbalance: Some market analysts have noted that silver production and consumption levels have not always aligned in recent years, which may influence availability over time.

Paper vs. Physical Market Dynamics: The relationship between paper-based contracts and physical metals remains a topic of discussion in the broader commodities market.

Detailed analysis of these shifting physical supply dynamics can be found in our [complimentary 2026 Gold in Modern America Guide](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). subject: God works in mysterious ways...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Troy Downing for Congress
body:
When I was deployed to Afghanistan, I prayed my family would be safe...God answered.

[](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDYyNl9JTC1ZMS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MzkxNTYtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA2MjZfSUwtWTEuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTM5MTU2LTI4OTkifQ/yC5E70xaqrzf6vx-gH2FVQ)God works in mysterious ways...
When I started my first business, I prayed it would be successful... **God answered.**
When I was deployed to Afghanistan, I prayed my family would be safe... **God answered.**
When I saw career politicians turn their backs on Americans to put their pet projects before the interest of the American people, I prayed for a better outcome...
I was surprised when **_God called on ME_** to run for office.
I'm Troy Downing. You might not recognize my name, but that's okay.
I'm a combat veteran. A God-fearing Christian. A husband & a proud dad.
**[I'm also the Republican running for re-election in Congress for Montana in the biggest race in the country.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDYyNl9JTC1ZMS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MzkxNTYtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA2MjZfSUwtWTEuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTM5MTU2LTI4OTkifQ/26wjIS1U9sK4P-A_7VIzRQ)**
I'm not in this to become a household name or for the title. I don't care about any of that.
I'm a simple man who enjoys a beer, likes to hunt and fish with my buddies & puts my family before anything else.
**__But I'm at my wits' end with two-faced politicians and DC bigwigs who say one thing to your face, only to turn around & stab hard-working folks like you & me in the back.__**
I'll always tell the truth. I'll always put America first. I'll always stand up for what's right.
The Radical Left will spread lies about me & throw me under the bus just to end my campaign before the midterms.
**[Peter, can you take a leap of faith on a simple combat vet like me to beat the Left & save our country?](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDYyNl9JTC1ZMS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MzkxNTYtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA2MjZfSUwtWTEuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTM5MTU2LTI4OTkifQ/E-m_J9DALBo7MQaIEG1JNg)**[HELP A COMBAT VET
](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDYyNl9JTC1ZMS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MzkxNTYtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA2MjZfSUwtWTEuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTM5MTU2LTI4OTkifQ/MfpGwefOVGIbBzc9TL2hjg)I know if we win this race, we can bring the entire Democrat Machine to its knees.
Thank you & God Bless,
Troy Downing (R-MT)| |

Dear Friend, The biggest news of the week was the **Maryland Freedom Caucus's** successful primary victories earlier this week. But we also have important information to share from South Carolina, Wyoming, Illinois, and beyond.Let's get into it.
---
|
---
**MARYLAND** The **Maryland Freedom Caucus** had a tremendous night in this week’s Republican primaries.Every incumbent Freedom Caucus member won renomination.But the bigger story is what happened beyond the Caucus itself.The Maryland Freedom Caucus also endorsed four conservative challengers, and all four won their races. Among the biggest victories was **Derek Howell’s** defeat of incumbent liberal Republican Delegate **Kevin Hornberger.** Howell was also endorsed by House Freedom Caucus Chairman **Congressman Andy Harris**.That race became a clear choice between the Republican establishment and the conservative movement. Despite representing one of Maryland’s most conservative districts, Hornberger repeatedly sided with Democrat Governor Wes Moore and Annapolis leadership. This year alone, he supported Moore’s record-breaking state budget, and in previous years he backed green energy mandates, DEI requirements, and corporate welfare programs. The Maryland Freedom Caucus made the case directly to Republican primary voters that conservative districts deserve genuinely conservative representation.The voters agreed.As a result, the Maryland Freedom Caucus will head into next year’s legislative session with a larger, stronger coalition than ever before. The conservative transformation of Annapolis won’t happen overnight.But this week’s elections made one thing clear: It has begun.

---
|
---
**SOUTH CAROLINA
** The **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** spent months getting an over-the-counter Ivermectin bill across the finish line. It passed the House 100-9. The Senate approved it 38-3. Then Republican primary season happened, Freedom Caucus members backed some challengers to establishment incumbents, and House Majority Leader Davey Hiott decided the bill needed to die. In one of his final acts before retiring, Hiott moved to bury the legislation in committee — a procedural kill shot. The stated grievance wasn't policy. It was that Freedom Caucus **Rep. Jay Kilmartin** had endorsed a primary challenger against an incumbent Republican colleague. Let that sink in: a bill that passed with 93% support in the House was killed not because of any objection to its merits, but because leadership wanted to send a message. Enough Republicans crossed the aisle to join Democrats and make it happen. The Freedom Caucus didn't lose the primaries — they won them, and picked up seats. So rather than accept that verdict from voters, establishment leadership used a procedural maneuver on the way out the door to punish the people who beat them. As SC Freedom Caucus member, **State Rep. Thomas Beach** , [wrote](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjnUEcUr9aOBxvq3CictT-2FPYSgMQkaTYquia16avYXZ22QHipALdnQ4DeUgujkKqmTQ-3D-3DRMVA_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerQ6aI2tzGjlhtsh75ydV7REHngUpMxHgJC5IgIzdbXKb9AgLac3gvl7oCtoqRNuyZxH7GsUx3WVhQpgkpYpPuxpM4V6eaz-2B-2BfPRTnyNdzg9IjsOapP7WTzYVYBL7z1QxhPbUPE-2BPtrt-2BZ2PWVNhLbcBTHNCuPS6T3AMjo3twHazwY2NYYnRN0eeacvqM4DGTHdBTbNDfh8EGZhW9K-2BWugXXtYkbMwUIDDNDANZyaok636fTNLwNp0IqIAGYwcJq7K) on social media: "GOP caucus priorities are more about punishing conservatives than helping families who need medical help."
---
|
---
**RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK** Congress continues to delay action on the SAVE America Act, legislation that would require proof of citizenship and voter ID to vote in federal elections.Meanwhile, the **Arizona Freedom Caucus** didn’t wait. In this week’s radio**** clip, Arizona Freedom Caucus member **State Rep. Alex Kolodin** explains how he and his colleagues successfully passed the **SAVE Arizona Act** , placing it on the November ballot so Arizona voters can decide directly.The contrast is hard to miss.While the U.S. Senate continues debating election integrity, Arizona lawmakers acted.When Congress refuses to lead, our State Freedom Caucuses are proving that conservative reforms can still move forward in the states.

clean_body: I’m the newest member of the EMILYs List board, but EMILYs List has been part of my story for a long time. | = = Hey y'all — it's Wendy Davis. I'm the newest member of the EMILYs List board of directors, but EMILYs List has been part of my story for a long time. I've been on the receiving end of early support from this organization, and I've seen up close what it can do for a candidate who's willing to run hard in a tough race. That's why I'm reaching out with just a few days left in EMILYs List's big 3X match campaign. Here's the deal, plain and simple: every online gift through June 30 will be tripled — until we reach $250,000 and unlock $750,000 total to support Democratic pro-choice women running in key races in 2026. = | = As a Texan, I know how tough the fight can be when the other side has the lion's share of power and money, and will do absolutely anything to keep it. You don't win those fights by waiting. You win them by building early — by investing before anyone else thinks a race is winnable. That's what EMILYs List does. We back the toughest races of the cycle. And yes, that includes races in my beloved home state, where we're supporting leaders who are ready to fight and win — like my friend Gina Hinojosa in her campaign for governor. But this match only reaches its full impact if thousands of grassroots supporters step up before the deadline. There were some big primaries in New York this week. In particular, 3 left-leaning candidates, Brad Lander, Claire Valdez, and Darializa Avila Chevalier, won their Congressional primaries, meaning they will certainly be among the newest crop of Democratic members of Congress come January. Valdez and Chevalier identify as DSA members, or Democratic Socialists.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94708368-399a-4f4d-9ee8-58e3893fdd81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Before I return to them, a note on Alex Bores losing a tightly contested Congressional primary to Micah Lasher in NY-12. Alex Bores and Micah Lasher were both State Assemblymembers with real ties to the community and ran strong campaigns. Nearly $28 million was spent by AI PACs on this race as a proxy war on AI regulation, because Alex Bores had sponsored some very sensible legislation on AI guardrails while a state rep in Albany. That's why I like him and supported him. Alex Bores lost, but so did the AI lobby strangely enough; the spending was so rampant that people became dubious as to why they were seeing so much about this one guy. Micah Lasher after his victory said, "The AI companies are going to be disappointed if they think I'm going to go easy on them." Alex lost but his viewpoint won.
As significant as that race was, even more attention is being paid to the other 3 incoming members of Congress. Brad Lander defeated an incumbent, Dan Goldman, who had a ton of resources. So did Darializa Avila Chevalier, who upended Adriano Espaillat, the head of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and a 5-term institution. Beating an incumbent almost never happens. Claire Valdez ran for a vacated seat but beat the establishment favorite. All were endorsed by Zohran Mamdani, whose endorsement carried a lot of weight. I live in New York and saw numerous ads showing Zohran with the candidates.
Darializa Avila Chevalier is the most likely of these 3 to be featured in Republican attack ads - if you google her social media record you'll see what I mean.
Many are saying this signals a sea change within the Democratic Party. The Progressive Left is exultant over the Squad nearly doubling in size. New York City is the power base of the Democratic Party, and both Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer seem in line for challenges to their spots. For 75-year-old Schumer, a real contested primary is all-but-certain in '28.
The trend is real, as establishment power is waning. But it is important to note what actually happened here. These are closed Democratic primaries in a non-presidential year. In NY-7 for Claire Valdez, 64,990 people voted out of 777,000 residents. In NY-10 for Brad Lander it was 79,000 voters out of 757,000 residents. In NY-13 for Chevalier it was about 70,000 out of 778,000 residents. The average turnout was less than 10% of residents. To win one of these races meant getting an extra, say, 20,000 people to the polls in each race. The DSA activists plus Zohran Mamdani have proven able to do this. That is a very big deal in New York politics. I have no doubt that they have very fertile ground given the underemployment rate of 42% among college graduates and their savvy social media game. Part of this translates to other environments as people are very ticked off.
But even statewide, the dynamics would be completely different. You don't have the same levels of density and organization. And in other parts of the country, anything to do with DSA would be a turnoff for tons of voters. What works in New York City won't necessarily work in Florida or Texas or even New Jersey. Indeed, if Democrats are going to win the House in November, they'll be relying heavily on military veterans like Pat Ryan to win contested races in purplish districts.
Ironically, if the Democrats wanted to push back on these new candidates, the most powerful thing they could do would be to open up their primaries and let everyone vote. Independents and Republicans - a plurality or majority of voters even in very blue districts - weren't able to vote in Tuesday's primaries. There was a push for open primaries last year in New York City that Zohran's allies squashed - they know that the more people who participate, the less likely they are to win. DSA candidates prosper in a more confined, ideological limited primary with lower turnout where their folks can make a bigger difference.
Democrats in New York have historically preferred closed primaries because they thought they could more easily control them and who's voting. It turns out that trying to limit the electorate may prove to be their undoing. I anticipate many breathless think pieces on the future of the Party and the results of trying to pack such disparate legislators under the same roof.
The way I'd interpret Tuesday's results is that the pendulum is swinging faster now and moats are disintegrating. If you reflect the status quo, your case is getting tougher by the day. Change is in the air. Whether that change is a good thing is a whole different matter.
