I've spent the last couple of months at Democratic Party events all over Illinois and the country -- fundraisers for James Talarico, for Peggy Flanagan, for a dozen other Democrats worth fighting for. And at almost every single one, I've heard the same question come up from the floor. Not from consultants. Not from staff. From regular people who took a night off and showed up.
The question is this:
**How do we get accountability for the crimes and the corruption of Donald Trump 's administration?**
I want to tell you how proud that question makes me. Because for decades the standard operating procedure in this country has been to forget. To let it slide. To "look forward, not back." To let the corruption fall by the wayside and tell ourselves we're being the bigger people. And meanwhile the rot spreads.
Not this time. The American people are not letting it slide. Good.
Because what we are watching right now is not normal. It is not politics as usual. We are living through a level of corruption that is unprecedented in modern American history.
Donald Trump has stolen billions from the American people. Billions. He has cut loose cop-beaters and drug dealers and crypto scammers -- let them walk straight out of prison -- because they put a little money back in his pocket. He has built a cottage industry for white-collar criminals, where if you're rich enough and connected enough, you can do anything in this country with total impunity.
And at the exact same time? He throws out the rulebook for everyone else. He attacks immigrant communities. He goes after anybody who protests. He comes after independent content creators. He comes after activists -- people like me. He comes after Democratic candidates because he doesn't like what they say. He comes after elected officials. Over and over and over again.
Two sets of rules. One for the billionaires. One for the rest of us.
That's the part I need you to sit with. That two-tier justice system is not a side effect. It is the rot at the core of this country.
And don't tell me this is new. Trump did not invent this sickness. He exploited it. He saw the loophole that powerful men have been using forever and drove a truck straight through it.
We have been letting the powerful walk for a long time.
In 2008, Wall Street torched the entire American economy. They wiped out people's homes, their retirements, their jobs -- millions of lives gutted. And how many of the executives who did it went to prison? Basically none. We bailed them out, dusted them off, and sent them back to work. We are still living with the ramifications of that decision today. A whole generation watched the people who broke the country get rescued while they got foreclosed on, and they learned the lesson we taught them: the rules are for you, not for them.
Go back further. Richard Nixon ran a criminal conspiracy out of the Oval Office, and Nixon never spent a single day in prison, because Gerald Ford pardoned him. We told ourselves it was about "healing the nation." What it actually did was establish the precedent that a president is above the law. That was bad for the country then, and we are paying for it now.
And right on cue -- just yesterday -- Vice President JD Vance stood up at the Nixon Library and praised Dick Nixon. Said his legacy is enjoying "a renaissance," and "deservedly so." Said if Watergate happened today it'd be a 12-hour news story. He's rehabilitating one of the most corrupt presidents in American history out loud, in public, with a smile on his face. Which honestly makes perfect sense, because the man works for a pedophile protector. Of course he thinks the crimes don't count. His whole job is making sure they never do.
That is the whole project. Not just committing the crimes. Not just covering them up. But training the country to stop caring. Training us to believe this country does not belong to us anymore. That government of the people, by the people, and for the people is just some old line in a textbook instead of a promise we are supposed to fight like hell to keep.

* * *
Now here's where I'm going to make some people in my own party uncomfortable.
A lot of our politicians, when this is over, are going to want to go back to the way things were. They're going to want to rebuild the institutions. Restore stability. Return to normal. And I understand the instinct. I do.
But normal is what got us here.
We don't need restoration. We need radical change. And radical change starts with accountability.
Because think about what we're actually saying if we let this go. If the Epstein class -- the people who used little girls and little boys -- walk away clean, and the American people never even learn the truth, what kind of country is that? If Donald Trump can steal, cut deals with foreign governments, manipulate markets to enrich himself and his family, and never face a single consequence -- not him, not his kids, not one person around him -- then what do we actually have left?
I'll tell you what we have. We have a country that deserves what's coming to it. Because a nation that refuses to hold the powerful accountable is a nation that has already decided the powerful are above the law.
The only way this changes is you.
You have to keep getting in the faces of our elected officials and our candidates and demanding accountability. Not because they're bad people -- a lot of them mean every word they say on the campaign trail, and I'm not here to attack our own candidates. But because the gravity of this business pulls everyone back toward the same old, same old. Back toward hunky-dory politics where the comfortable stay comfortable. Left alone, they will drift. The realities of the world will get in the way. They'll do the right thing only if we make the right thing the path of least resistance.
You can be polite about it. You don't have to be mean. But you cannot stop asking.
And here's the part nobody wants to hear:
When we win the midterms this November -- when we take back the House and the Senate -- the fight does not stop. When we elect a Democratic president in 2028, the fight does not stop. We do not get to go back to sleep.
That's the trap. There is an expectation baked into my party that the second we get a boring, decent Democrat back in the Oval Office, everyone exhales. Everyone goes home. Everyone checks out.
That's exactly how we drift. That's exactly how good people in office quietly fail and how 'accountability' becomes a campaign slogan instead of a governing demand. We must be just as loud, just as organized, just as relentless when we're winning as when we're losing.
So keep showing up. Keep asking the hard question. Keep your foot on the gas.
Because accountability isn't something they're going to hand us.
It's something we're going to have to take.

| Hello Republican Friends,
The Massachusetts Republican Party is excited for our series of upcoming regional training days across the Commonwealth. These focused sessions will equip our candidates, volunteers, and activists with essential skills to win in 2026 and beyond.
Topics will include fundraising strategies, effective messaging, political operations and data-driven targeting, as well as practical door-knocking tips to connect directly with voters.
Exact dates and locations for each region will be announced shortly--stay tuned for details and make sure to mark your calendars. This is our opportunity to build a stronger, more prepared Republican team ready to take back Massachusetts!
In Unity, Leanne Harris Chair, MassGOP Public Relations Committee State Committeewoman, Middlesex & Norfolk District X @LeanneHarrisMA [leannejharris@gmail.com](mailto:leannejharris@gmail.com)

INTERNS INTERVIEW
---
> Annalise: Political Science and Law student at George Washington University
> John: Political Science and Philosophy student at Boston College
> Why did you want to be a MassGOP Intern?
> Annalise:
> I wanted to be a MassGOP intern for the opportunity to gain firsthand experience in Massachusetts politics and see how party organizations operate behind the scene. As a political science student, I have been especially interested in party politics and the strategic work that often goes unnoticed. With the 2026 election cycle approaching, the internship has offered a fast-paced environment where there is always meaningful work to do and I am excited to see what comes next!
> John:
> What motivated me to be a Massachusetts Republican Party intern was a combination of factors. Being a long life Baystater I have a strong passion for improving our commonwealth. This passion has only grown seeing the mismanagement and decay of this state. As a political science student the political process was an unknown but deeply interesting machine that I wanted to understand. The Mass GOP internship stood out to me, because it offered a chance to get hands-on experience, meet like minded people and learn more about campaigning, outreach, and party operations. Having spent a full spring and soon to be summer as part of this team this is certainly something that I am glad to be part of.
> What are you looking forward to during the rest of the internship?
> Annalise: Hopefully seeing all our hard work pay off in November!
> John: I am looking forward to not only a triumphant November but also continuing to deepen my understanding of the political process.

As our nation prepares to celebrate its 250th birthday, Massachusetts - the cradle of the American Revolution - is sitting this one out. While almost all other states and territories will send delegations to the Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., Governor Maura Healey is dismissing the Freedom 250 initiative as being "just ridiculous".
This partisan decision is a missed opportunity, of historic proportions, to showcase Massachusetts' history to hundreds of thousands of Americans who cherish our values and to global tourists who want to learn of our history.
The 16-day festival runs from June 25 to July 10th and celebrates America's 250th birthday with exhibits, performances, and cultural heritage from across the country. It is exactly the kind of event that draws families who love Americana: visitors eager to walk Boston's Freedom Trail, explore Lexington and Concord, experience Cape Cod, the Berkshires, and our rich maritime heritage. These are the tourists who support our hotels, restaurants, shops, and small businesses while connecting with the birthplace of our nation.
While other states will be using this national stage to highlight their attractions and economies, the Massachusetts pavilion will be vacant. We are forfeiting valuable exposure that could drive real dollars to our tourism economy, from historic sites to innovation hubs. Governor Healey's decision reveals her priorities: politics over people, partisanship over prosperity.
Massachusetts deserves better. We are a state rich in history, culture, natural beauty, and entrepreneurial spirit. We should be leading the celebration of America's 250th birthday, not boycotting it. The MassGOP urges Governor Healey to put Massachusetts first and support participation in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
Americans who love this country are looking for places that honor its founding. We deserve a Governor who celebrates our commonwealth and puts Massachusetts first.

The President has access to information nobody else has.
The President can move markets with a single social media post.
The President can influence government contracts, tariffs, regulations, foreign policy, and countless other decisions that affect stock prices.

While the Trump administration and RFK Jr. undermine vaccine safety from Washington, states like Colorado are stepping up to protect public health.

name: Tim Kaine
subject: Protecting our LGBTQ+ community
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/xnCuz1ktqkym5P4hGyMXyw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/xnCuz1ktqkym5P4hGyMXyw2]
Derek, I couldn’t let June come to a close without wishing this team a happy National Pride Month!
I’m so glad to celebrate the LGBTQ+ community. I want every LGBTQ+ Virginian and American to know: You are loved for who you are — and I am committed to working to protect your rights and safety, because every single one of us deserves to feel safe as we are.
That starts by finally passing the Equality Act here in the Senate — a bill I’m so proud to cosponsor — so we can ensure no one faces discrimination for who they are or whom they love.
If you’re with me on this and believe the Equality Act should be a priority when Democrats take back the majority, I hope you’ll add your name to my petition today. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/xnCuz1ktqkym5P4hGyMXyw2]
We’ve made so much progress toward true equality, and that’s only been possible thanks to the countless advocates and activists, including so many here in Virginia who never gave up — even against long odds. It’s sometimes hard to believe it was only 2015 when the right to marry became the law of the land.
And we’ve come even further since then, building inclusion and acceptance into communities, hearts, and minds.
But in spite of the progress we’ve made, the LGBTQ+ community is under attack and targeted by hateful legislation in too many states across the country. There is an intentional effort by the Trump administration to make the LGBTQ+ community — especially our transgender and gender-nonconforming friends and loved ones — scapegoats to distract from Trump’s failed policies that are making life harder for Americans.
Take James Talarico, the Democratic Senate nominee in Texas and a vocal advocate of LGBTQ+ rights. Since he won his primary, Republicans have unleashed a wave of hate his way. Stephen Miller even went so far as to falsely claim that Talarico is trans — an accusation that reveals the cynical calculation some are making to win campaigns through targeted bigotry.
Even our LGBTQ+ service members are targets for their bigotry. Under Trump, the Air Force forced trans service members to retire — and then reclassified them as national security risks so they couldn't receive retirement benefits.
It is absurd that the very people who defend our rights abroad come back to having their rights taken away here at home.
Virginians have a memory. We know that our state has targeted marginalized communities in the past, and it did not make our state better. And we recognize that the same thing is happening now.
This month and every month, we should be reminding members of the LGBTQ+ community of all the people who love and support them. We should be reminding them of their beauty and worth. We should be reminding them that there are a lot of people who love and care for them — and who are fighting for them every single day.
Thanks for being here. I’m grateful to be in this fight alongside you.
—Tim
Tim Kaine
U.S. Senator for Virginia
Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
1490-5A Quarterpath Road #272
Williamsburg, VA 23185

name: Adam Dunigan for Congress
subject: We spend the most. We get the least
body:
Forty-seven World Cup nations have universal healthcare. One doesn't. Guess who?

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/2ke8X1KpF8J?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
| | | | | |

# _Policy Brief_
# Healthcare
---
| |
[](https://us.list-manage.com/fzIM1bPnnmE?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
---
| | Friends,
47 of the 48 nations in this summer's World Cup have universal healthcare and guaranteed maternity leave. One doesn't.
Let that sit with you for a second.
This week, Gallup released new numbers. They're brutal.
**2.8 million more American adults couldn't afford healthcare in 2025 than in 2024**. That's not a slow drift — that's a country abandoning its people at exactly the moment they need it most.
And it's about to get worse. ACA subsidies are expiring. Medicaid cuts from the "One Big Beautiful Bill" land this January. Enrollment is already dropping. The people writing these policies aren't the ones who'll feel them.
Here's what makes me angriest: we already pay more for healthcare than any other country on Earth. We just don't get more for it. Worse outcomes. Higher prices. More people one diagnosis away from bankruptcy.
This isn't abstract to me. I've watched what it does to people — to families who did everything right and still ended up choosing between a prescription and rent. That's not a healthcare system. That's a trap.
Here's what I believe, plainly:Healthy people work. They show up for their kids, their neighbors, their communities. They're not one bad month away from losing everything. A country that actually wants a strong economy invests in the health of the people who run it — that's not charity, it's strategy.
So when I get to Congress, I'm going to fight for three things: lower drug prices, real protection for Medicare and Medicaid, and a serious push to decouple healthcare from employment — because no one should have to keep a job they hate just to keep their insulin affordable.
I know this one personally. When I left the CIA to run for this seat, I lost my federal coverage. What I have access to now runs through the VA, because I served. And even with that earned benefit, I've felt the gap firsthand — what it's like when your healthcare changes the moment your job does. Most Americans don't have a VA to fall back on. They just fall.
It's also why I take it seriously when veterans tell me the VA itself is stretched too thin — long waits, understaffed clinics, benefits that are harder to access than they should be for people who already paid the price of service. We don't get to call ourselves a country that supports our troops if we let that system rot. Fixing it isn't optional. It's a debt.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/WKOAdylmSgq?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)_A painfully good day with my amazing chiropractor_[ _Dr. Reza Eftekhar_](https://us.list-manage.com/19mxGFajMja?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) _, only possible via Veterans Affairs benefits._
That's the whole problem in one sentence: healthcare in this country is tied to a paycheck, not to being a person. If you're lucky, you've got a job, or a benefit, or a program that catches you. If you're not, you're on your own.
We have the smartest people and the most money in the world. We can absolutely build a system that works for everyone, not just the people who can afford to be sick. What we're missing isn't capability. It's the will to choose people over profit margins.
I'm asking you to help me get to Congress so I can be one more vote, one more voice, fighting for that.
Every dollar gets us closer to August 4th — and closer to a Congress that remembers healthcare is a human right, not a privilege.

A child plays on the floor in the halls of immigration court at the Jacob K. Javits Federal Building in New York City, on March 05, 2026. Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images.
In April, a 10-year-old Venezuelan boy named Wilfredo Hoyos-Gomez appeared in immigration court in Texas, unaccompanied and without a lawyer. His mother, Nexoli Anyis Gomez Bracho, was arrested during a traffic stop and has been in ICE custody in Houston since December.
Wilfredo entered the U.S. three years ago with his mother. She has a work permit, and their asylum cases are pending. They have no other family in the U.S., and Gomez's former employer has been looking after Wilfredo while he faces deportation hearings alone.
"I was nervous because it was my first time going to a court," Wilfredo told Univision after his hearing. The DHS is seeking to deport him to Ecuador, a country where he knows no one and has never been.
Wilfredo is one of hundreds of thousands of children facing pending immigration cases without legal representation nationwide, according to federal immigration data. His case offers a rare glimpse into a system operating outside of public scrutiny. While technically open by law, immigration hearings for children are effectively blocked from public access.
A new analysis of federal immigration data, conducted by the Vera Institute of Justice in response to questions from Drop Site News, shows that children like Hoyos-Gomez are not an anomaly but part of a wider pattern. More than half of all children facing pending immigration cases are doing so without legal representation, according to data from the Department of Justice. The analysis shows that legal representation appears to be one of the most important factors shaping children's outcomes in immigration court.
Of 751,861 children with pending removal cases, 57%--or 425,093 children--lacked legal representation, according to the most recent data. This rate is slightly higher than that of adults, 54% of whom are unrepresented in immigration court in pending cases. Nearly two thirds of children's cases that are still pending were initiated by the federal government in 2023, under the Biden administration. The gap widens in completed cases. Last year, 64% of children's completed immigration cases went forward without legal representation.
The data, from the DOJ's Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), indicates that children under the age of 18 are increasingly appearing in immigration court without lawyers at a time when deportation orders are surging as the Trump administration attempts to deport more than a million people annually and immigration relief is becoming harder to obtain. The Vera Institute analysis could not determine how many of these children are unaccompanied, because EOIR data does not distinguish between accompanied and unaccompanied children.
Former judges, attorneys, and advocates interviewed by Drop Site describe an immigration court system under mounting pressure to move cases quickly, straining due process protections for the most vulnerable.
"The scale is alarming," said Neil Agarwal, the principal data scientist who led the analysis at the Vera Institute of Justice. These figures reflect the administration's coordinated effort to pursue its "mass deportation scheme," he added.
The Justice Department and ICE did not respond to requests for comment. In an emailed statement, a spokesperson with the Department of Homeland Security claimed that ICE does not separate families. "Parents are asked if they want to be removed with their children or ICE will place the children with a safe person the parent designates," a DHS spokesperson said, adding that the U.S. encourages voluntary departures and if people don't choose to do so they will be arrested and deported. "The United States is offering illegal aliens $2,600 and a free flight to self-deport now."
"Any possible way to be harsh and unforgiving is being utilized by the government at this point," said former immigration judge Dana Leigh Marks, who presided over cases for more than three decades in San Francisco. "It makes me ashamed."
"I don't know if I could remain on the bench today...because my hands would be tied," she said. "I think there was a very small amount of due process before and there was more ability of immigration judges to try to find a way to craft a reasonable solution for children in the court," she added, "and now it's non-existent."
## **A Clear Pattern**
Last year, 7% of children with an attorney in completed cases were allowed to stay in the country with some form of legal relief, either by being granted asylum or some other federal protection, including a change in status or cancellation of removal, compared with less than 1% of children without legal representation. The pattern has continued into 2026. So far this year, 3% of represented children have avoided deportation and received some form of protection, compared with less than 1% of those without lawyers.
This year, 25% of represented children's cases resulted in an outcome allowing them to remain in the country without protections such as asylum, compared with 11% of unrepresented children. Meanwhile, 73% of represented children were either deported or opted for voluntary departure, versus 89% of unrepresented children.
Over the past two years, final court decisions that allow children to remain in the United States have declined, while removal orders have increased.
Tania Cohen, legal director of the New York-based Safe Passage Project, a nonprofit organization that provides free legal representation to migrant and refugee children facing deportation, said she has seen more migrant children heading to hearings alone after parents were detained or deported. "It's alarming and unsurprising," said Cohen. "I have seen an uptick of youth seeking representation who entered with a parent, but now that parent has been deported or is in detention." The youngest child the group has recently represented was just an infant.
"We are concerned that the immigration court system is speeding up cases at the expense of due process," said Jennifer Podkul, chief of global policy and advocacy at Kids in Need of Defense (KIND), a nongovernmental organization providing free legal counsel to unaccompanied refugee and migrant children.
The true number of children navigating immigration court may be even higher. Roughly 11% of people in the EOIR dataset lacked birthdate information and could not be categorized by age, meaning some children may not have been included in this analysis.
## **Hearings Behind Closed Doors**
Because public access to minor immigration hearings is restricted, judges and legal aid organizations are among the few sources of information about these proceedings.
"An immigration court proceeding involving an unrepresented two or three year old can be exactly as nonsensical as it sounds," said Jason Boyd, the vice president of U.S. federal policy and an attorney at KIND. "The hearing may conclude and a child doesn't comprehend what just happened."
For five years, former immigration judge Elizabeth Young presided over thousands of cases on the juvenile docket in San Francisco. Young said she vividly remembered a case involving a four-year-old girl with her father. She had fallen asleep in her father's arms, exhausted in the middle of a noisy courtroom at the beginning of the hearing. As Young began to read out names, she looked to the government attorney to introduce themselves, and saw they were silently weeping. She decided to grant the family a continuance, or extra time, to prepare for a case and secure counsel.
Last year when KIND's Podkul was in a courtroom observing the juvenile docket, there was a child she recalled "running around a tiny car, zoom-zooming on the floor," she said. "They're treating these kids as if it's a regular case, like they're an adult."
"Just the other day, one of our colleagues had to hold a baby in her arms that she was a lawyer for," Podkul told Drop Site.
## **Violations of Due Process**
Attorneys and former judges interviewed by Drop Site say immigration courts can be difficult for adults to navigate, let alone children.
"This is a due process crisis," said Boyd. "It's virtually impossible for an unaccompanied child to navigate the complex and adversarial U.S. immigration system without an attorney at their side, federal data makes that very clear."
In the past, unaccompanied children were more likely to receive extra time to prepare their cases, often two to three months, according to KIND. In recent months, they've observed continuances no longer than two to three weeks, which is insufficient time, Boyd said.
Legal aid and advocacy groups and former judges told Drop Site that due process is being challenged under the Trump administration by "mega masters," or mass hearings with multiple cases involving children and adults being heard back to back. There are sometimes about 100 people scheduled for a morning, Cohen said.
Marks, the former immigration judge, says these hearings are detrimental for children.
"They should have a judge who is able to spend as much time as needed explaining things, making the child feel comfortable enough to be able to tell their story, giving enough time for the judge to be able to assess whether the child is suffering from post-traumatic stress or some of the effects of a dangerous journey to the United States," she said.
Immigration judges are also working under pressure to move quickly through cases--not only from their supervisors but also from attorneys who appear for the Department of Homeland Security in court, Marks said.
"There's just a push to get the cases done," said Young, and the administration has made it clear "they want it done in a way that results in a lot of deportations."
Boyd observed another "disturbing" trend with judges routinely "ordering the removal of unaccompanied children" who had already been granted special immigrant juvenile status, a form of protection guaranteed by Congress for children who experienced parental abuse or abandonment. "By judges ordering those kids removed from the United States, potentially to the very abuse that they fled," he said.
Over the last year the Trump administration has reduced the number of immigration judges [by 25%](https://substack.com/redirect/4182f202-c8ff-4de7-8479-7e1fdd34cf03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"It feels like there is no due process," Cohen said. "Judges are being fired for following the law, and then being fired if they do not take enough of an anti-immigrant stance in their decision making."
## Disruption to Legal Aid
In February 2025, the Trump administration issued a "stop-work" [order](https://substack.com/redirect/cd1cd692-7dd6-4d4d-9cef-9da380d886f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to legal service providers such as KIND that are funded by the Department of Health and Human Services. That order disrupted support for nearly 26,000 children before it was [rescinded](https://substack.com/redirect/8e6003c3-d6be-4caf-81c6-ec19e8247928?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three days later.
The following month, HHS abruptly [terminated](https://substack.com/redirect/26ebf29b-b447-4375-92e6-aadb417c6f04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) major federal grants that supported legal representation for unaccompanied minors. A federal judge soon [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/f29ec5c7-543a-4c96-b6d0-778dd1c7683c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the administration to restore these funds, but legal aid organizations say the funds have not been fully restored. They are now being provided in three month increments while the government appeals the case.
KIND, which [relied on federal funding](https://substack.com/redirect/47807a55-a4ce-438e-9711-d5056d452751?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to cover 68% of its budget to represent more than 4,000 unaccompanied children, has [reduced its staff](https://substack.com/redirect/47807a55-a4ce-438e-9711-d5056d452751?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to work within a strained budget. The organization is currently operating under these three month increments, according to Podkul.
"As an organization that's trying to hire attorneys into representation for children, that's really hard to do at three month increments," Podkul said. "You can't say to a kid, well I can help you now, but I don't know if I'm going to be here in 89 days."
While there are laws in place to offer protection to children in these cases, the impact of these new policies reshaping the immigration system will be felt for years to come, according to legal aid service providers.
"We have laws that Congress passed that provide an avenue for relief and this administration is trying to find all the ways to cut off those avenues," Cohen added, "I think that it's a huge miscarriage of justice."

doors with furniture, officers beaten on the Capitol steps, and five
people dead.

reality.

This is Trump’s game. Stack the federal government — the courts, the DOJ,

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134074005/630024887/2105508926?refcode=ea.82be1c0a-7c71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ms=ea.82be1c0a-7c71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjgyYmUxYzBhLTdjNzEtZjExMS1hYzljLTAwMGQzYTU0YmVkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=q-8XOc7eyB5k6Y74pRia-oqAci7fKXcvviyLyDEQwJI=) Hi there, it's Lily Tomlin. Jane Fonda is one of the most tenacious human beings I have ever known. Trust me, fifty years of friendship tells you a whole lot about a person. So when I say that the work Jane is doing right now with her Climate PAC matters — _in a this-is-not-a-drill kind of way_ — I mean it. I’ve watched her fight for decades, even if that fight sometimes ended with us in handcuffs. **[If you’re already feeling motivated, then I'd love for you to chip in a donation of any amount to Jane’s Climate PAC before Tuesday at midnight. Jane’s team is working to reach 15,000 grassroots online donations ahead of their end-of-quarter deadline. Every single donation from people like you sends a message to Big Oil and the entire fossil fuel industry: people are with us.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134074006/630024888/2105508926?refcode=ea.82be1c0a-7c71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ms=ea.82be1c0a-7c71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjgyYmUxYzBhLTdjNzEtZjExMS1hYzljLTAwMGQzYTU0YmVkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=q-8XOc7eyB5k6Y74pRia-oqAci7fKXcvviyLyDEQwJI=)** Here's the truth: What’s happening in our country isn’t normal, and we can’t let ourselves forget that. An illegal war launched without congressional approval. A government that has decided corporate polluters matter more than the people breathing their poison. Democratic norms being dismantled faster than most people can track. _Business as usual is behind us._ And what comes next is shaped by the people who refuse to go along with it. Jane refuses. Her Climate PAC is doing the unglamorous, essential work of electing brave leaders from public utility boards to Congress who refuse right along with her — people who will fight for our planet, our democracy, and our fundamental freedoms every single time. **What many people don’t realize is that these fights are won long before Election Day. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. | | | In June 1999, the US Supreme Court ruled in Olmstead v. L.C. that Americans with disabilities have the right to live in the community, _outside_ of institutions. With the help of in-home and community services, Americans with disabilities can live and work with full lives. Now, Donald Trump's Justice Department is trying to gut Olmstead. They're arguing that states don't have to provide in-home or community services ... _that segregating Americans with disabilities should be allowed._ This could drag back civil rights for individuals with disabilities and plunge these community members into darkness. **At Able Dems, we elect champions with disabilities who will FIGHT for our rights.** We elect Democrats who speak out for those who cannot speak for themselves. **We can't build power for the disabled community without your help. It's just the truth.Friday, June 26, 2026SCOTUS Hands Trump a Clean Sweep5-minute read · 4 storiesLead Story · The Supreme CourtSUPREME COURT HANDS TRUMP A CLEAN SWEEP — TPS, ASYLUM, AND GUNSWhat's HappeningIn a single Thursday morning the Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a trio of victories. In a **6-3 decision** , the justices cleared the way to end Temporary Protected Status for more than **356,000 Haitian and Syrian immigrants** , holding that the TPS statute bars judicial review of those claims.The SituationIn a companion case, the Court lifted a lower-court order blocking a border “metering” policy that caps how many migrants can claim asylum each day — a tool used in Trump's first term. The same morning, the justices struck down a Hawaii law restricting concealed carry on private property open to the public.
* Justice **Samuel Alito** , writing for the majority, said judges overstepped by second-guessing the Homeland Security secretary, and the Court rejected a claim the Haiti decision was discriminatory
* The White House called it a **“tremendous win,”** arguing protected status was always meant to be temporary, not a path to permanent residency
* The three liberal justices dissented; lawyers for the immigrants warned the ruling puts TPS holders in danger
* The decisions could speed removal of protections the administration has also withdrawn from Afghans and Cameroonians

The PerspectiveFor two years the message from the bench was “not so fast.” Thursday it changed. The Court didn't rewrite immigration law — it told lower-court judges to stop substituting their own judgment for the elected branch's on who gets to stay temporarily and who doesn't. Add a Second Amendment win on top, and it was the kind of day this administration has been waiting on.[Read the full story at CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/znFZ6KFMxBSrAXlxVjOmb3WjcQhcJTyZl8hRIv6OIaHBuwImI%2BR7rPamN9XY%0A70%2BQUh%2FtwKa2VL01vlckN3UVXJiQsGLfYmSqMmbLP%2BEtYBzSjtWz5FMKKEob%0AmNn%2Bt77ihJU3Luoirv%2BmiEuZl0uuiie22Qezqu4lRs919Jz%2BgDIlv%2Fgjb%2FN4%0A%2BZIz%2FqAmG%2FEO8olbJnTkFFsH8x55L%2BzYLw%3D%3D%0A/0569c12117c5cb3f)Foreign Policy · The Iran DealIRAN HITS A SHIP IN HORMUZ AS RUBIO WARNS ALLIES ON TOLLSWhat's HappeningThe Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps struck a cargo vessel near Oman on Thursday, rattling the fragile U.S.-Iran framework meant to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.The SituationWrapping a Gulf tour in Bahrain, Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** warned that any Iranian fee on ships crossing the strait would spread **“like a contagion.”** He said international waterways belong to no single nation and that Gulf allies showed no support for Tehran's toll idea.
* Roughly **a fifth of the world's oil** moves through Hormuz; the interim deal is set to be formalized at a signing in Switzerland
* Rubio's stop was the first high-level U.S. mission since last week's framework agreement
* The strike is a reminder of how brittle the ceasefire remains, even as energy markets price in peace

The PerspectiveA deal on paper isn't a deal at sea. The administration's bet is that pressure plus allied unity keeps the strait open and prices falling. Tehran's bet is that a well-placed missile reminds everyone who sits on the chokepoint. The signing in Switzerland will only matter if the shooting actually stops.[Read the full story at CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/0TnmkOUFlggTjpWf8KUXYo5nRGGJ3LwYPeXFHaxhYIvAkU9OGudIGV%2BzoS7e%0AR%2FsbmJIPTYAhKqVtkLVtFGnDNSUiluASf%2BI08kUvHKvAAZ6c0LKSSlP%2F3%2FNP%0AWubl53LHGNZwUklHYZ0kCewszS4caEFtCFhbCOrM6tqoLeed8vsJf00GwnBT%0AFj46FGNeaY2If59jJlsWUSBIXjsj%2F4I8gQ%3D%3D%0A/cbb839e1c4cc26cd)Capitol HillTRUMP TELLS CASSIDY TO SIT DOWN, PUTS HOUSING BILL ON ICE FOR SAVE ACTWhat's HappeningA closed-door lunch with Senate Republicans turned into a shouting match after Sen. **Bill Cassidy** pressed the president over the Iran war powers question. By multiple accounts, Trump told the Louisiana Republican to sit down.The SituationHours earlier, Trump abruptly canceled the signing of a bipartisan housing-affordability bill — which cleared the Senate **85-15** and passed the House with nearly 400 votes — saying he won't act until Congress passes the **SAVE America Act** , his proof-of-citizenship and voter-ID measure.
* Cassidy, who lost his primary last month to a Trump-backed challenger, said he matched the president's tone; Sen. Ted Cruz called it a **“spirited discussion”**
* A follow-up war powers resolution on Iran failed **45-50** after Cassidy switched his vote and Rand Paul voted “present”
* Speaker Mike Johnson backed the move and urged passing SAVE through reconciliation; House conservatives blocked floor votes in solidarity
* The 10-day signing clock hasn't started — Johnson has not yet formally transmitted the housing bill to the White House

The PerspectiveLeverage is the whole game. The president is willing to sit on a popular, veto-proof housing bill to force a vote on election integrity — and willing to dress down a senator already on his way out to make the point. Allies call it tough love. The open question is whether it actually moves a single vote on SAVE.[Read the full story at CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/adOb27Eml0tpPHHW3fxUd08v3MftyK2uCHUn%2Fxt9tKbBraWOB1YvYvamYu83%0AXydxNgTmWigwvS6LTeyMY9p6PTcm99BrhmUgxnrEzdQQVY3rXbfSNbipEAib%0A9kdtXWT9ANLBk6FvtMKjpHB7VRweqoqcBOUzxkjEz4A3UJ1XSKvaFtb1H2rh%0AgOO2mw7i%2B4KlUXFDsdll5tbgNftYzOOUXA%3D%3D%0A/2eb7865cf430b15b)America at 250TRUMP OPENS THE 'GREAT AMERICAN STATE FAIR' AS THE NATION TURNS 250What's HappeningTrump kicked off the **16-day Great American State Fair** on the National Mall with a roughly 30-minute speech marking the start of America's 250th year, ahead of next month's July 4 milestone.The SituationRun by the Trump-created Freedom 250 partnership, the event is billed as a modern-day world's fair celebrating the country's semiquincentennial. “**America is back** ,” the president declared from the Mall.
* The fair runs 16 days as the centerpiece lead-in to the nation's 250th birthday
* A handful of booked performers backed out earlier, citing the event's political tenor
* Organizers describe Freedom 250 as a nonpartisan nonprofit; critics question the White House's central role

The PerspectiveSet aside who's holding the microphone — 250 years is a real milestone, and a national fair on the Mall is a fitting way to mark it. The next two weeks will tell whether it reads as a unifying birthday party or just another partisan flashpoint.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/UT19HLJD5bUpmzcLdWYPQ6BlTWtULIXw6is8weHptaT8zQd03tKlIiEXBmZJ%0A6f9EN3JIQ%2FGOym0%2FMV9X9%2B1uZ7CHPTTi%2BoPHDNOxk8AGL7azAv6N%2FZ0e5kaO%0AZDhsbOf2EaeshAxyzl2%2F1xDSzxc9gTBc2dNcQjHbkMfQ9c5ZizV5lAPWMIYQ%0ABpETJqghsvpVQbroNoeU3HfeuuEaVTlv4A%3D%3D%0A/e2d8f1b6aa039198)⚡ The Bottom LineThe Supreme Court cleared three administration priorities in a single morning, Rubio leaned on Gulf allies to keep Hormuz open while Iran tested the ceasefire, and the president put a popular housing bill on ice to force an election-integrity vote — all as the country opened its 250th-year celebration on the Mall. **Wins at the bench, leverage on the Hill, and a fragile peace abroad. subject: Why JD Vance's story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
What this says about this moment in America

| | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

name: Team LeftNet
subject: The right to marry who you love is still under attack.
body:
11 years after the Obergefell decision, our right to love who we love is still under attack.
#
Today marks the 11th anniversary of _Obergefell v. Hodges_ , the landmark Supreme Court decision that legalized marriage equality nationwide. But as we look back on how far we’ve come, we have to face a chilling reality. **The right to marry who you love is still under attack.**
70% of Americans support marriage equality — including 40% of Republicans. The overwhelming majority of our country agrees that love is love, and that every family deserves protection and dignity under the law.
But being vastly out of step with the American people has never stopped far-right extremists.
**Earlier this year, anti-LGBTQ+ hate groups backed and funded by the Heritage Foundation launched a coordinated effort called the “Greater Than” campaign.**
Their explicit goal is to shift public opinion and completely overturn _Obergefell_ by pushing the dangerous, false myth that marriage equality harms children.
We know the facts. We know that LGBTQ+ parents are just as effective as heterosexual parents, and that marriage equality provides families with vital stability and legal protections.
But facts alone never stop the far right. They don’t care about the facts.
Today, on the anniversary of the historic _Obergefell_ decision, we refuse to sit and watch our progress be erased. We need to show these extremist groups that the pro-equality majority is ready to fight back.
**[Will you take a moment to sign our petition and reaffirm your support for marriage equality?](https://act.leftnet.org/sign/marriage_equality/?source=em20260626-1674&t=1&akid=1674%2E2118727%2E4MzTcF)**
**[Sign the Petition ››](https://act.leftnet.org/sign/marriage_equality/?source=em20260626-1674&t=2&akid=1674%2E2118727%2E4MzTcF)**
We’re grateful to have you in this fight.
In solidarity,
LeftNet

Can I be honest with you?

My goals as your future governor are really quite simple. Yes, I have
comprehensive plans — as anyone asking for your trust and vote should —
but at the end of the day, I’m fighting to...

* Drive down costs. From the grocery store to the gas pump, from the
doctor’s office to the mortgage bill, far too many hard-working
families across Michigan are struggling to make ends meet.
* Help Michigan families build wealth and get well-paying jobs in the
state. That means a Michigan where teachers can afford to live in the
communities they teach in, and nurses are paid well and taken care of
in the workplace.
* Prepare Michigan to defend our rights, our freedoms, and our
democracy. As Michigan’s Secretary of State, I’ve spent years standing
up to attacks on our democracy and defending our elections. As
governor, I’ll continue fighting for our democracy and never back
down, regardless of who’s in the White House.

Throughout this campaign, I’ve traveled across Michigan, talking directly
with hard-working families about the challenges they’re facing, their
hopes for the future, and one thing is clear: Michiganders need a governor
who cares about making their lives better.

That’s the kind of leadership that can only be elected by running a
campaign powered by the people. A campaign like the one we’re building,
together. One that’s ready to fight tooth and nail to make real change for
Michigan families.

But first, we have to win in November. A movement capable of taking on the

name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
subject: We do not have to agree on everything to agree that women’s pain should be taken seriously
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MGP VICTORY FUND, A JOINT
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
A few weeks ago, my husband and I lost a pregnancy.
The physical toll was something not even my doctor prepared me for.
After 11 weeks of hope about bringing a new member into our family, we learned the pregnancy was no longer viable. After several weeks of bleeding and mourning, my doctor made clear that future pregnancy could be much more difficult if I didn't take medication to expel the retained miscarriage.
Like most women, I was told the medication would feel like a regular period. Maybe a little stronger cramping.
But when I took the medication, the pain was more intense than the pain I experienced delivering my son four years ago. I wasn't even advised to take it when my son was out of the house.
And I am not alone.
Women are routinely told that Ibuprofen is sufficient pain management during miscarriage. In practice, that's the functional equivalent of handing someone a stick to chew on.
Science and medicine have advanced in so many ways, but when it comes to reproductive health, the standard of care for women's pain in this country is still medieval.
I know there are broad differences in beliefs about reproductive health. But we do not need to agree on every policy question to agree that women should not have to endure excruciating pain while managing a miscarriage and protecting their ability to go on and bring a child into this world.
One in four women will likely experience a miscarriage. We can do better than telling them to take Ibuprofen and endure it.
That's why I introduced and passed a simple amendment directing the NIH to study strategies to improve pain management during miscarriage.
If you agree that women deserve better pain care than the status quo provides and that the Senate should pass this amendment, add your name today. [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/women-pain-care]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/women-pain-care]
We don't need to agree on everything to agree on this: Women who lose a pregnancy deserve compassion and dignity.
Thank you,
Marie

# [OpenAI eyes 2027 IPO while Kalshi traders smell huge opportunity](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI **[has yet to hold pre-IPO investor meetings](https://substack.com/redirect/1e10d366-6fc5-4d12-a8a8-31e26bfaaef4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or set an official timeline after its recent confidential S-1 filing, sources said, as the New York Times reported a lean toward 2027 and **[Kalshi traders adjusted odds](https://substack.com/redirect/d45185d6-e760-4301-bbaa-9e5e7f22076b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following caution from SpaceX volatility.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **No Pre IPO Meetings:** Sources confirm the AI company has skipped sessions testing investor demand and pricing so far and will likely start them only once timing becomes clearer.
* **Kalshi Odds Recalibrated:** Traders now assign 59 percent chance of an IPO announcement by March 1 2027, roughly one in three before January 1, and 73 percent by June 2027.
* **SpaceX Caution Grows:** Advisers grew wary of retail appetite after the volatile trading debut of Elon Musk's SpaceX, contributing to tempered expectations away from earlier 2026 plans.
* **Altman And Rival Notes:** The CEO views going public as a financing event not currently the focus, while rival Anthropic also filed confidentially with 70 percent odds seen for its announcement by December.

# [Billionaire predicts Bitcoin collapse while Saylor's bold strategy hits limits](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Billionaire Jeremy Grantham predicted Bitcoin will **[dwindle away over decades](https://substack.com/redirect/c4c56f44-b6fd-4ec0-96a0-669cff3fbfaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with a whimper as a useless speculative asset, as **[Michael Saylor's company grapples with quadrupled dividend obligations](https://substack.com/redirect/4b7ca56a-92e7-4df4-814d-201bbb9f87da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid ongoing price declines below sixty thousand dollars.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Grantham Slams No Utility:** The GMO co-founder argued bitcoin lacks intrinsic value and real world use for trades or supermarket purchases while enabling crooks to move money and failing to outperform in bull markets unlike gold.
* **Repeated Crash History:** Bitcoin has dropped at least 70% from every cycle peak and is now fifty two percent off its October high hovering below $60,000 dollars with the current slump likely to drag on.
* **Dividend Obligations Quadrupled:** Strategy now faces $1.2 billion dollars annually on preferred shares after rapid growth including 11.5% yield on its Stretch version as prices fell sharply.
* **Cash Rebuild Dilemma:** The firm holds enough reserves for roughly ten months of payments but needs nearly $2.8 billion dollars for preferred recovery while selling bitcoin risks eroding confidence according to analysts.

# [Mark Cuban fires warning: AI giants must choose creators over A-list celebs](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Billionaire Mark Cuban **[advised AI companies and data center builders to win public support](https://substack.com/redirect/f66e62d4-cc10-4f5a-9a2f-eb4087f8b181?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by directly helping artists, writers and unions rather than hiring celebrity endorsers or engaging music and film firms amid growing backlash over job impacts.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Put People First Strategy:** Cuban said the fight against data centers proxies hate toward AI wealth concentration and urged firms to connect with creators across cities to protect their work and provide financial support.
* **Avoid Celeb Endorsements:** The entrepreneur warned against paying famous people to back the technology calling it dumb and stressed not approaching music or film companies to avoid worsening tensions.
* **Acknowledge Job Risks:** Cuban noted AI threatens entry level white collar roles in customer service software development and data analysis but believes towns facing losses should receive billions in support from major LLMs as a cost of business.
* **" Kiss Working Asses" Advice:** With massive power needs for data centers he emphasized engaging everyday workers trying to pay bills to secure capacity otherwise the business will fall far short.

# [OpenAI and Anthropic slammed by brutal spend crunch as efficiency wars rage](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI and Anthropic may see slowing growth **[as enterprises rein in AI costs by switching to cheaper open source models](https://substack.com/redirect/da3a647e-9319-47e8-9cc9-fc67c700fe0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** capping token spend and demanding clear ROI ahead of their planned IPOs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Tokenmaxxing Era Ends:** Founders like Lindy CEO switched fully to cheaper alternatives like DeepSeek saving millions as costs previously ballooned into billions since ChatGPT launch with AI coding tools driving heavy usage.
**Enterprise Caps Implemented:** Uber set monthly AI spending tiers starting at fifteen hundred dollars and blew through annual budget in four months while clients pull back until proving return on investment.
**Growth Rates Peaking:** Anthropic annualized run rate hit $47 billion dollars up from $10 billion last year and OpenAI near $25 billion prompting urgency to list before rationalizing spend hits.
**Model Routing Rises:** Companies turn to routing tasks to appropriate cheaper models as 95% still use frontier ones for simple jobs which will become untenable long term per executives.

# [Fed Chair Warsh makes bold move: Hands key roles to internal economists](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh **[appointed economists Daniel Covitz and Eric Engstrom as advisors to reshape economic and monetary policy](https://substack.com/redirect/7b4ba8fb-6187-40dc-999c-518218397863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** views relying on decades of internal expertise following announcement of five operational task forces.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Internal Appointments Made:** Warsh selected Covitz as Deputy Director in Research Statistics and Engstrom as Associate Director in Monetary Affairs both retaining division roles on rotating advisory basis.
* **Task Forces Launched:** Moves follow creation of groups focused on communication data inflation technology and balance sheet to re examine key metrics with resources deployed inside and outside the institution.
* **Heavy Internal Reliance:** Despite broad changes planned the latest picks indicate reliance on Fed experts while earlier external selections included Project 2025 architect Paul Winfree and Stanford's Daniel Heil.
* **Remaking Approach Confirmed:** Appointments confirmed by people familiar aim to tackle projects as Warsh charts new course after press conference on operational structure updates.

# [Hidden force behind S&P stall: Options gamma explains this week's flat market](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The S&P 500 ended almost unchanged despite big moves from Micron earnings positive data and Apple decline possibly **[due to long gamma positioning by market makers stabilizing the index](https://substack.com/redirect/7fe4e7da-2e54-4ffd-b51a-accf48dd47d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a narrow range ahead of monthly options expiry.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48f5449d-0e46-4dc6-af3e-c3c0e07abe32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Wild Ride To Nowhere:** Traders faded overnight rally then bought dip sending Nasdaq futures swing three percent yet index closed three quarters percent up after starting flat near prior close.
* **Long Gamma Stabilizing:** Dealers owning options that pay on volatility buy back puts on dips and sell calls on rips keeping stocks ranged with focus around 7200 to 7400 levels.
* **Expiry Influence Noted:** June thirtieth monthly options expiry Tuesday prompts comfort with cheaper out of the money bets as blow up risks remain from AI repricing or higher rates seen.
* **Bonds Stay Calm:** Treasury ETF TLT moved only three basis points despite GDP at two point one percent and PCE inflation at four point one five percent highest since April twenty twenty three.

Fellow American,I just wanted to take a moment to say thank you. Your unwavering support means the world to me.
Because of your dedication, I can keep fighting for our shared values in the Senate. Whether it is advocating for sensible economic policies, defending our national security, or ensuring Maine's interests are always front and center, your backing gives me the strength to do what is right for our state and our country.
We have important work ahead of us. There are critical issues facing our communities, and we must remain focused on delivering real results. Knowing I have you in my corner gives me absolute confidence that we can tackle these challenges head-on.
I have written a special, short note just for you to express my gratitude and outline our next steps.

Fellow American - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill.

Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did.

After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake.

The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today.

And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it.

I won't stand for it. _Not for a second._

clean_body: I was the first in my family to go to college. | Fellow American - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington. I grew up in the back of a bar. Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did. I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13. I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb. That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way. After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves. That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake. The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today. And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it. I won't stand for it. Not for a second. We are in a fight for the future of this country, and it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. I didn't come from money. I came from a bar in South Carolina, a mother who worked hard, and a faith that hard work still means something in America. It still does. Thank you for standing with me. God bless you, and God bless South Carolina. name: Autism Health
subject: A Message From Autism Health: Standing With the Families of Venezuela
body:
Dear Friends and Supporters,

I am writing to you today with something urgent on my heart, and a direct ask for your assistance.

Many of you know my husband, Steve Slepcevic, as the Co-Founder of Autism Health Inc. What you may not know is that Steve is also the CEO and Founder of Strategic Response Partners, an organization that deploys trained rescue and medical teams into the hardest-hit disaster zones in the world. The same heart that helped build Autism Health, the drive to show up for families in their most difficult moments, is the heart now leading rescue teams toward one of the worst disasters we have seen in years.

On June 24, two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela less than a minute apart near the coast west of Caracas. Entire apartment buildings collapsed. Hospitals were damaged. Right now, families are waiting for word about loved ones trapped beneath the rubble. The death toll has climbed into the hundreds and continues to rise, with thousands injured and many more displaced, sleeping in the streets, afraid to return to what is left of their homes.

Autism Health Inc. is standing alongside Strategic Response Partners to support this lifesaving mission, and today I am asking our community to stand with us.

** Why We Are Stepping In
------------------------------------------------------------

At Autism Health, our mission has always been about families. We exist because we believe no family should face their hardest moments alone, and that conviction does not stop at the edge of our usual work. A disaster of this scale touches everyone, and it touches the most vulnerable hardest of all.

Among the thousands of families affected are children and adults with autism and other disabilities, who are among the most at risk in any emergency. Displacement, the loss of routine, the loss of medical care, the chaos and noise and fear of a collapsed community, these things fall heaviest on those who are least equipped to absorb them. When we support this mission, we are helping reach the very families our organization was founded to serve, in a moment when they have almost nothing left.

** What the Teams Are Doing on the Ground
------------------------------------------------------------

Strategic Response Partners is deploying Urban Search and Rescue paramedic teams to assist with critical lifesaving operations. These teams are fully equipped, highly trained, certified, and actively responding right now. The work includes:
* Urban Search and Rescue
* Emergency Medical Assistance
* Emergency Shelter and Essential Supplies
* Heavy Equipment and Logistics Support
* Humanitarian Relief for Affected Families

These are not abstract categories. They are the difference between a family reunited and a family left waiting. They are clean water for people who have lost everything, medical care for the injured, and a trained rescuer reaching someone before time runs out.

The teams are already in motion. But the need is growing faster than the resources to meet it, and that is where our community comes in.

** How You Can Help
------------------------------------------------------------

In a disaster of this scale, the first hours and days are everything. Survival often comes down to how quickly trained rescuers and medical personnel can reach people who are trapped, injured, or stranded. Every team that can be deployed, every load of supplies that can be moved, expands how many lives can be reached while it still matters.

Every donation directly funds the deployment of trained rescue personnel, specialized equipment, medical supplies, food, clean water, fuel, transportation, emergency shelter, and other lifesaving resources for the people impacted by this disaster.
To support the rescue and relief mission directly, please give through the Strategic Response Partners GiveSendGo campaign:
DONATE HERE (https://www.givesendgo.com/Venezuela?utm_source=share&mc_cid=ccba0d18aa&mc_eid=UNIQID)

To support Autism Health as we continue serving families impacted by autism, including those caught in moments of crisis like this one, you can also give at www.autismhealth.com (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/links.givebutter.com%2Fengage%2Fo504%2FngmBM9w/b43o/x0zGAQ/AQ/e004ece7-6de3-4465-b03a-a5a3a708e50c/3/u8s8ctu2bj?mc_cid=ccba0d18aa&mc_eid=UNIQID) .

If you are not able to give, you can still help by sharing this message with people in your life who can. In moments like this, awareness moves resources, and resources save lives.

** A Final Word
------------------------------------------------------------

This is where ordinary people get the chance to do something extraordinary. Your generosity becomes hope for a family waiting to be rescued, comfort for those who have lost everything, and strength for the first responders working around the clock to bring people home.

I am deeply proud of the work Steve and his teams are doing, and I am grateful beyond words for a community like ours, one that has never been afraid to show up for families in their hardest moments. clean_body: Dear Friends and Supporters, I am writing to you today with something urgent on my heart, and a direct ask for your assistance. Many of you know my husband, Steve Slepcevic, as the Co-Founder of Autism Health Inc. What you may not know is that Steve is also the CEO and Founder of Strategic Response Partners, an organization that deploys trained rescue and medical teams into the hardest-hit disaster zones in the world. The same heart that helped build Autism Health, the drive to show up for families in their most difficult moments, is the heart now leading rescue teams toward one of the worst disasters we have seen in years. On June 24, two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela less than a minute apart near the coast west of Caracas. Entire apartment buildings collapsed. Hospitals were damaged. Right now, families are waiting for word about loved ones trapped beneath the rubble. The death toll has climbed into the hundreds and continues to rise, with thousands injured and many more displaced, sleeping in the streets, afraid to return to what is left of their homes. Autism Health Inc. is standing alongside Strategic Response Partners to support this lifesaving mission, and today I am asking our community to stand with us. Why We Are Stepping In At Autism Health, our mission has always been about families. We exist because we believe no family should face their hardest moments alone, and that conviction does not stop at the edge of our usual work. A disaster of this scale touches everyone, and it touches the most vulnerable hardest of all. Among the thousands of families affected are children and adults with autism and other disabilities, who are among the most at risk in any emergency. Displacement, the loss of routine, the loss of medical care, the chaos and noise and fear of a collapsed community, these things fall heaviest on those who are least equipped to absorb them. When we support this mission, we are helping reach the very families our organization was founded to serve, in a moment when they have almost nothing left. What the Teams Are Doing on the Ground Strategic Response Partners is deploying Urban Search and Rescue paramedic teams to assist with critical lifesaving operations. These teams are fully equipped, highly trained, certified, and actively responding right now. The work includes: Urban Search and Rescue Emergency Medical Assistance Emergency Shelter and Essential Supplies Heavy Equipment and Logistics Support Humanitarian Relief for Affected Families These are not abstract categories. They are the difference between a family reunited and a family left waiting. They are clean water for people who have lost everything, medical care for the injured, and a trained rescuer reaching someone before time runs out. The teams are already in motion. But the need is growing faster than the resources to meet it, and that is where our community comes in. How You Can Help In a disaster of this scale, the first hours and days are everything. Survival often comes down to how quickly trained rescuers and medical personnel can reach people who are trapped, injured, or stranded. Every team that can be deployed, every load of supplies that can be moved, expands how many lives can be reached while it still matters. Every donation directly funds the deployment of trained rescue personnel, specialized equipment, medical supplies, food, clean water, fuel, transportation, emergency shelter, and other lifesaving resources for the people impacted by this disaster. To support the rescue and relief mission directly, please give through the Strategic Response Partners GiveSendGo campaign: DONATE HERE () To support Autism Health as we continue serving families impacted by autism, including those caught in moments of crisis like this one, you can also give at www.autismhealth.com () .
