Dear friends,As our campaign approaches its first finance reporting deadline, we wanted to provide a brief update on where we stand and where we’re headed.
We’re not building a campaign around endless fundraising emails, text messages, phone calls, or stacks of mail asking for money. We’d rather spend our time talking about Alaska’s future. But if you believe experience, integrity, and practical solutions matter, a [**$26 Vote of Confidence for 2026**](https://us.list-manage.com/WXayvy9gI2r?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612) would send a powerful message that Alaskans are behind this campaign.
Over the past several weeks, we’ve begun laying out a vision for Alaska built on something increasingly rare in politics: real solutions to real problems.
* **Energy Security:** Southcentral Alaska faces a looming natural gas shortage, and too many politicians continue to talk around the issue rather than solve it. Bill and Randy have the experience and relationships to move Alaska toward [long-term energy security](https://us.list-manage.com/114SrhKgW6j?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612).
* **Responsible Resource Development:** We’ve [proposed reforms](https://us.list-manage.com/TSfm7IBWHb1?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612) that put the State in the lead on pre-permitting project areas while maintaining Alaska’s high environmental standards.
* **An Honest Fiscal Conversation:** We’ve begun a candid discussion about Alaska’s fiscal future with a proposal - not a mandate. We recognize it has generated both support and criticism. We’re listening carefully, and we’ll continue to listen. Nothing would change without broad based support from the public and legislature.

Not everyone will agree with every proposal, and that’s okay. Politics today often revolves around slogans, talking points, and promises that sound good but never get implemented. **We believe Alaska deserves better**. We believe leadership means identifying problems, offering workable solutions, listening to Alaskans, and making those solutions stronger through public discussion.
If you’d like to learn more about the ideas we’ve released so far, please visit [WalkerHoffbeck.com](https://us.list-manage.com/mh1yByP4mUe?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612).
And if you believe this is the kind of leadership Alaska needs, we would be honored if you would make a [$26 Vote of Confidence in Alaska’s Future](https://us.list-manage.com/NQUMYeNZ1IZ?e=b6cf32d1c2&c2id=bccaf449ed2960725e09a7036fc7e612).
With gratitude,**Bill Walker** \- Candidate for Governor**Randy Hoffbeck** \- Candidate for Lieutenant Governor
Integrity. Experience. Solutions.

name: Matias, United We Dream
subject: Making sense of the Supreme Court’s latest TPS decision
body:
You’re invited to our community call on Tues, 6/30! | | | Peter, Yesterday, the Supreme Court handed down a devastating ruling to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti and Syria. **We’re currently witnessing the largest delegalization effort in recent U.S. history.** For months, this administration has tried to dismantle programs that our families have relied on for generations, from TPS to DACA to asylum protections. Since taking office, the administration has terminated TPS for 14 protected countries, putting the future of nearly 1.3 million people on the line. Peter, they’re trying to redefine who gets to belong here, but we know that no one in our community is disposable. TPS holders have never been temporary in our communities. They’re our neighbors next door, our co-workers, and working people who our country has openly depended on for their labor, care, and contributions for decades. Now, it’s our turn to have their backs and call on Congress to put an end to these delegalization efforts. clean_body: You’re invited to our community call on Tues, 6/30! | | | Peter, Yesterday, the Supreme Court handed down a devastating ruling to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti and Syria. We’re currently witnessing the largest delegalization effort in recent U.S. history. For months, this administration has tried to dismantle programs that our families have relied on for generations, from TPS to DACA to asylum protections. Since taking office, the administration has terminated TPS for 14 protected countries, putting the future of nearly 1.3 million people on the line. Peter, they’re trying to redefine who gets to belong here, but we know that no one in our community is disposable. TPS holders have never been temporary in our communities. They’re our neighbors next door, our co-workers, and working people who our country has openly depended on for their labor, care, and contributions for decades. Now, it’s our turn to have their backs and call on Congress to put an end to these delegalization efforts. Will we continue down the path of mass deportation and delegalization, or will we build a future where our families can live with dignity and stability? ✍️ We’re making sense of this moment together. clean_body: | Three weeks from today, Tennesseans head to the ballot box for the August primary. This weekend will mark120 in-person stops in Jerri Green's ongoing tour across the state. Everywhere we go, people are telling us the same thing:the financial pressure isn't letting up, it's getting worse. = For o ver fifteen years , the status-quo servants in the statehouse have protected the wealthy few while everyday people are forced to choose between buying groceries or putting gas in the tank. The politicians who rubber-stamp these corporate handouts are banking on working families staying home on election day. They want us to believe Tennessee is a permanently red state, but the truth is it’s an under-registered, under-represented state. When we all c ome together, we win. That's why we've been so focused on building a movement driven by the people who actually keep Tennessee running. We are nurses working to keep our rural clinics functioning, teachers buying their own classroom supplies, gig workers piling on shifts and barely scraping by , families making things work on a minimum wage that hasn't budged in over a decade. We don’t need piles of corporate cash to win this race —we need ordinary Tennesseans,just like you , to refuse to be priced out of their own state to break their entrenched power and elect a governor who answers to families, not billionaire donors. We have exactly 21 days left to build the field operations capable of reaching voters we know are ready for change. Within 24 hours of the House and the Senate passing a historic and effective bipartisan bill to tackle housing affordability, Donald Trump canceled the bill’s signing ceremony and announced that he’s refusing to sign it until Congress passes his massive voter suppression bill, the “SAVE America Act.”
We could have gotten private equity out of buying big tracts of land and driving up prices. We could have lowered rental prices. We could have gotten first-time homebuyer grants all across the country. Instead, we sat in a room full of empty chairs in a canceled press conference. Womp womp.
This was one more painfully clear proof point: we cannot take two more years of the GOP having a trifecta of power in Washington. We absolutely have to take back the House this November.
Our fight to reclaim power is facing a big test next week with our June 30th FEC deadline, and we’re working towards a $10,000 online fundraising goal. name: The Turning Point USA Team
subject: How JD Vance found his way back to faith
body:
Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance

| | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance | | | | | | | Peter, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. subject: We Can Flip Virginia's 10th Congressional District
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julie Perry for Congress
body:
You don't want to miss this.
| | | | |
---
I'm not a career politician. I'm a classroom teacher, a wife, and someone who has spent my life helping others find their voice. Growing up with a learning disability, I learned early on how to face challenges head-on. That experience shaped who I am and led me to the classroom, where I now work with students, especially those who struggle with speech and learning, to build confidence and succeed. Now I'm stepping forward to serve Virginia's 10th District because our families deserve leadership that understands what they're going through. I'm focused on stronger schools, a more affordable cost of living, safe communities, and leadership rooted in integrity. subject: Six Candidates. Two Chambers. One Movement.

body:
Meet the newest slate of Forward's 2026 endorsees.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
The Forward Party has officially endorsed six independent candidates running for federal office — four for the U.S. Senate and two for the U.S. House. Their elections could fundamentally change how Congress works. **Six Candidates. Two Chambers. One Argument.** The Forward Party has announced the most expansive independent federal endorsement slate by any political organization in the 2026 election cycle. Four U.S. Senate candidates across Idaho, Colorado, South Dakota, and Montana, plus two U.S. House candidates in Iowa are being added to our growing list of endorsed candidates. They are veterans, business leaders, and public servants, all running without a party. |
## **U.S. Senate Endorsements**
Idaho • Colorado • South Dakota • Montana
---
**Idaho**
**Todd Achilles**
**U.S. Senate | Independent | Challenging Sen. Jim Risch (R)**
Todd Achilles is an Army veteran, former Idaho State Representative, technology executive, and public policy instructor from Boise. He has the military record, the legislative experience, the private-sector track record, and the classroom credibility that most Senate candidates would dream of — and he's running without a party label against a three-term incumbent who has held Idaho office since nearly 1970.
In Idaho, unaffiliated voters now outnumber registered Democrats two to one. Achilles' campaign polling shows him **trailing Risch by 14 points among uninformed voters — and leading by 3 among voters who know both candidates.** That gap shows this race gets better every time a voter hears the argument.
He is also a founder and board member of Veterans for Idaho Voters, and a member of the American Federation of Teachers union and Idaho Business for Education — the kind of cross-constituency coalition that can actually win a Senate race in a state that's ready for something different.
**Colorado**
**Bob Chew**
**U.S. Senate | Forward Party | Challenging Sen. John Hickenlooper (D)**
Bob Chew served as an officer on a nuclear submarine during the Cold War, then spent 30 years building a global company from four employees to 700. He knows how to build something real and work hard for it.
He's running on the Forward Party line in Colorado because he believes both parties have spent decades refusing to have the hard conversations: the national debt, Social Security solvency, immigration, and energy. He is self-funding his candidacy and has pledged to invest whatever it takes because conviction, not calculation, is what got him into this race.
The forward argument isn't always about which race is easiest to win. Sometimes it's about challenging a system that has gone unchallenged. Chew’s opponent Sen. John Hickenlooper is an incumbent in a state where one party has been unchallenged for too long.
**South Dakota**
**Brian Bengs**
**U.S. Senate | Independent | Challenging Sen. Mike Rounds (R)**
Brian Bengs is a U.S. Navy and Air Force JAG Corps veteran, former instructor at the Air Force Academy and NATO School, law professor at Northern State University, and Wind Cave National Park Ranger. He has spent his life in service — in uniform, in the classroom, and in his community — and now he's channeling that same ethic into a Senate campaign built on a simple foundational argument: big money in politics is the root cause of nearly every policy failure South Dakotans are living with.
He's been a member of the American Legion, the VFW, and Veterans for All Voters as a state leader. In 2023, he led a citizen-driven constitutional amendment effort to protect voter-passed ballot measures from legislative override. He's done this before — organized from scratch, built a coalition, fought the system.
**Montana**
**Seth Bodnar**
**U.S. Senate | Independent | Open Seat**
****
Seth Bodnar graduated first in his class at West Point, served as a Green Beret with multiple overseas deployments, built a career in business, and spent eight years as president of the University of Montana.
The story of how he got into this race tells you something about the problem he's running to fix. Two-term incumbent Sen. Steve Daines withdrew from the race **eight minutes before the filing deadline** and simultaneously endorsed his chosen successor, Kurt Alme — without a primary, without voter input, without asking Montana if that's what they wanted. Numerous elected Montana Republicans have gone on record expressing their frustration with the move. It is exactly the kind of insider self-dealing that Bodnar's campaign is built to challenge.
He has outraised every other candidate in the race — Democrat and Republican. Montana showed up for him before a single vote was cast.
## **U.S. House Endorsements**
Iowa's 1st District • Iowa's 2nd District
---
Iowa is **a state with a sizable unaffiliated electorate and is about to have independent candidates in two competitive congressional districts at the same time.** Both are candidates who did the strenuous door-to-door work to earn their place on the November ballot.
**Michael Bridgford**
**U.S. House, IA-01 | Independent | Challenging Mariette Miller-Meeks (R)**
****
Michael Bridgford is running in one of the most-watched congressional districts in the country. Cook Political Report rates Iowa's 1st District a toss-up. Roughly one-third of voters in the district aren't registered with either major party.
His district's general election will be a three-way race — and this is the third consecutive cycle in which the same two major-party candidates, incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R) and Democrat Christina Bohannon, will face off. Iowa's 1st District voters know exactly what they're getting from both parties. Bridgford is offering them something they haven't had: a choice. "I think 2026 is a big year for an independent movement across the country," he has said. He's not wrong.
**Dave Bushaw**
**U.S. House IA-02 | Independent | Open Seat**
****
Dave Bushaw is a squash farmer in West Union, a labor unionist, and a folk musician who has played at union strikes across the country. "Both parties walked away from the people who built this country," he has said. That conviction drove him to do something Iowa's legislature tried to prevent: qualify for the November ballot as an independent after the state raised the signature threshold mid-campaign.
He knocked on more than 7,000 doors in northeast Iowa. 88% of the people who answered signed his petition. He officially filed his signatures on June 2nd — primary day itself — achieving **200% of the required number in every single county in Iowa's 2nd District.** That is not just ballot access. That is a grassroots mandate. The general election will be a three-way race against Democrat Lindsay James and Trump-backed Republican Joe Mitchell, in a district Cook now describes as "increasingly competitive."
## **How These Candidates Could Change Everything**
Here's the argument both parties hope you never think about too hard.
The Senate and the House both operate on razor-thin margins right now. Whichever party holds the majority controls the committee chairs, the legislative calendar, and every procedural lever that determines what bills ever reach a vote. The minority party can obstruct. That's it. And that majority can be as thin as one or two seats before everything changes. Independent senators and representatives are not required to caucus with either major party. That means a small enough bloc — even two or three seats in the Senate — could deny either party an outright working majority, and in exchange for agreeing to organize the chamber, demand real structural changes
Forward Party candidates are accountable to the voters. They will focus on solutions, not partisan fighting, in order to serve their constituents. In these six campaigns, it's a description of what they've already done before a single November vote is cast.

He has the military record, the legislative experience, the private-sector track record, and the classroom credibility that most Senate candidates would dream of — and he's running without a party label against a three-term incumbent who has held Idaho office since nearly 1970. In Idaho, unaffiliated voters now outnumber registered Democrats two to one. Achilles' campaign polling shows him trailing Risch by 14 points among uninformed voters — and leading by 3 among voters who know both candidates. That gap shows this race gets better every time a voter hears the argument. He is also a founder and board member of Veterans for Idaho Voters, and a member of the American Federation of Teachers union and Idaho Business for Education — the kind of cross-constituency coalition that can actually win a Senate race in a state that's ready for something different. Colorado Bob Chew U.S. Senate | Forward Party | Challenging Sen. John Hickenlooper (D) Bob Chew served as an officer on a nuclear submarine during the Cold War, then spent 30 years building a global company from four employees to 700. He knows how to build something real and work hard for it. He's running on the Forward Party line in Colorado because he believes both parties have spent decades refusing to have the hard conversations: the national debt, Social Security solvency, immigration, and energy. He is self-funding his candidacy and has pledged to invest whatever it takes because conviction, not calculation, is what got him into this race. The forward argument isn't always about which race is easiest to win. Sometimes it's about challenging a system that has gone unchallenged. Chew’s opponent Sen. John Hickenlooper is an incumbent in a state where one party has been unchallenged for too long. South Dakota Brian Bengs U.S. Senate | Independent | Challenging Sen. Mike Rounds (R) Brian Bengs is a U.S. Navy and Air Force JAG Corps veteran, former instructor at the Air Force Academy and NATO School, law professor at Northern State University, and Wind Cave National Park Ranger. He has spent his life in service — in uniform, in the classroom, and in his community — and now he's channeling that same ethic into a Senate campaign built on a simple foundational argument: big money in politics is the root cause of nearly every policy failure South Dakotans are living with. He's been a member of the American Legion, the VFW, and Veterans for All Voters as a state leader. In 2023, he led a citizen-driven constitutional amendment effort to protect voter-passed ballot measures from legislative override. He's done this before — organized from scratch, built a coalition, fought the system. Montana Seth Bodnar U.S. Senate | Independent | Open Seat ** Seth Bodnar graduated first in his class at West Point, served as a Green Beret with multiple overseas deployments, built a career in business, and spent eight years as president of the University of Montana. The story of how he got into this race tells you something about the problem he's running to fix. Two-term incumbent Sen. Steve Daines withdrew from the race eight minutes before the filing deadline and simultaneously endorsed his chosen successor, Kurt Alme — without a primary, without voter input, without asking Montana if that's what they wanted. Numerous elected Montana Republicans have gone on record expressing their frustration with the move. It is exactly the kind of insider self-dealing that Bodnar's campaign is built to challenge. He has outraised every other candidate in the race — Democrat and Republican. Montana showed up for him before a single vote was cast. U.S. House Endorsements Iowa's 1st District • Iowa's 2nd District Iowa is a state with a sizable unaffiliated electorate and is about to have independent candidates in two competitive congressional districts at the same time. Both are candidates who did the strenuous door-to-door work to earn their place on the November ballot. Michael Bridgford U.S. House, IA-01 | Independent | Challenging Mariette Miller-Meeks (R) Michael Bridgford is running in one of the most-watched congressional districts in the country. Cook Political Report rates Iowa's 1st District a toss-up. Roughly one-third of voters in the district aren't registered with either major party. His district's general election will be a three-way race — and this is the third consecutive cycle in which the same two major-party candidates, incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R) and Democrat Christina Bohannon, will face off. Iowa's 1st District voters know exactly what they're getting from both parties. Bridgford is offering them something they haven't had: a choice. "I think 2026 is a big year for an independent movement across the country," he has said. He's not wrong. Dave Bushaw U.S. House IA-02 | Independent | Open Seat Dave Bushaw is a squash farmer in West Union, a labor unionist, and a folk musician who has played at union strikes across the country. "Both parties walked away from the people who built this country," he has said. That conviction drove him to do something Iowa's legislature tried to prevent: qualify for the November ballot as an independent after the state raised the signature threshold mid-campaign. He knocked on more than 7,000 doors in northeast Iowa. 88% of the people who answered signed his petition. He officially filed his signatures on June 2nd — primary day itself — achieving 200% of the required number in every single county in Iowa's 2nd District. That is not just ballot access. That is a grassroots mandate. The general election will be a three-way race against Democrat Lindsay James and Trump-backed Republican Joe Mitchell, in a district Cook now describes as "increasingly competitive." How These Candidates Could Change Everything Here's the argument both parties hope you never think about too hard. The Senate and the House both operate on razor-thin margins right now. Whichever party holds the majority controls the committee chairs, the legislative calendar, and every procedural lever that determines what bills ever reach a vote. The minority party can obstruct. That's it. And that majority can be as thin as one or two seats before everything changes. Independent senators and representatives are not required to caucus with either major party. That means a small enough bloc — even two or three seats in the Senate — could deny either party an outright working majority, and in exchange for agreeing to organize the chamber, demand real structural changes Forward Party candidates are accountable to the voters. They will focus on solutions, not partisan fighting, in order to serve their constituents. **I served 20 years in the Air Force and I need you to understand the depth of the dishonor here.** Our military is 250 years old. It began with a ragtag band of minutemen who grabbed their rifles to throw off the yoke of a king, and every generation since has paid in blood to make it a little fairer and a little stronger than the one before. Each wave of Americans who were once told they did not belong, the immigrants, the Black soldiers, the women, fought their way in and made the whole institution better for having them. **That is the story of the uniform: a long slow march toward the idea that what matters is whether you can do the job.** And now it has been handed over to a megalomaniac with the temperament and maturity of a teenager. A man who looks at the women who fly combat missions and command troops and gather intelligence and bleed for this country and is apparently threatened by them. **There 's no other explanation.** [**Help us send a combat veteran to Congress who will fight to restore the honor Hegseth is stripping from this institution piece by piece.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt809HxUuAuqc2LHuu7N7Dlj7Voj5hIyI8agLOlZ6C1tpxpgn3rZB8Lw2qtpbSp-sFttkW-CqhQ_Ci-uV4iFh0MxJaQ63vxegCdHUFNwCOlDvj981rkoTu7LaQAXTzUwfa9Ky5hUvNJ8kMwGVbP8zT_D9VR86SImiG6YtcbFlu43-IpM3JONQ0EeiURXCdRQ2E0WG56dnSO36O5mZ_1oAqT6rjwLtPpk0DdOVorn841KIUNvQ1bxjv-8shl3CVjgoK4hieWZ6Ptg6xDU36x_pyiKNR0ef_LrAGezQM9p-3y4wVpc4M-MxvivOPqRlea8neyQ/4rt/4aVlWkYFRzidpvXYKZ0BdA/h3/h001.S5-d-lulnWfq5sRsYk-01SBlZuiXVNAcLzLGL9CqyOE) I served alongside women who were as fine a group of officers as this country has ever produced. Their courage was no less than any man's and their sacrifice was every bit as great.

The idea that our country cannot even lay a wreath in their memory without it being branded a political controversy is one of the most shameful moments I have witnessed in my lifetime of service. **Pete Hegseth is a disgrace to every person who has ever worn the uniform and he should be removed from office. ** And Keith Self, a man who wore the uniform himself and knows exactly what this costs in morale and readiness and basic human decency, is standing right there beside him saying nothing. | The political establishment talking heads on cable news are desperately trying to spin what happened in New York this week as a fluke.
That is what the establishment always does when the people who don't do things their way beat them. They call it a fluke, a one-off, a weird "local" race, a candidate-specific upset, anything but what it actually is.
A movement.
But here in Denver, they are not acting like New York was a fluke. They're pouring millions into our race because they're terrified that it could happen again.
A dark-money Super PAC with hidden funders just announced another $1,000,000 in spending to stop us before Tuesday's election. Reporting has linked this network to AIPAC-aligned groups and shell PACs, which means Denver voters may not know who is really paying for these attacks until after the ballots are counted.
They saw anti-corporate PAC, anti-AIPAC progressives win in New York, and voters reject the idea that Democrats should campaign on democracy while protecting corporate power, defending blank checks for war, and telling working people to wait their turn.
And now they are looking at Denver.
They know we're a city where rent is out of control, health care is still too expensive, young people are watching the pathway to a stable life disappear, and voters are tired of being represented by a leader who has had THREE decades to deliver and still asks for another term.
I'm the candidate who will fight for Medicare for All, universal child care, housing as a human right, publicly financed elections, abolishing ICE, and an arms embargo to stop U.S. weapons from fueling genocide in Gaza.
I will NEVER accept AIPAC money or corporate PAC checks from the same industries making life harder for families.
What our campaign has is thousands of doors knocked on, volunteers giving up their nights and weekends, neighbors talking to neighbors, and a campaign that has never once had to pretend this system is working.
But in a race this close, we cannot let a $1,000,000 smear campaign be the last thing voters hear before Election Day.
We do not need to match them dollar for dollar. We need enough to keep our ads running, keep organizers in the field, send the texts, make the calls, print the lit, and reach the Denver voters who can still decide this race.

subject: ICYMI: $540 Million Secured for California Water Infrastructure
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vince Fong for Congress
body:
If you didn't see the news a few weeks ago, we wanted to share that we are making real progress of the issue of water infrastructure. | | |
---
| |
# In Case You Missed It: $540 Million Secured for California Water Infrastructure
---
| Dear Friend, We are making real progress of the issue of water infrastructure in the Central Valley—and we have results to show for it. For the past several months, I have been working alongside my colleagues and federal partners to help secure federal funding to modernize and strengthen our state’s critical water infrastructure. Thanks in part to our efforts, and the leadership of President Trump, that critical funding was included in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act that Congress passed last year. Earlier this year, the Department of the interior finally announced the deployment of $540 million for water infrastructure projects here in California. **_This is one of the most significant water investments the Central Valley has seen in decades._** As you know, Central Valley families, farmers, and communities depend on reliable water every single day. We grow nearly three-quarters of the nation’s fresh fruits and nuts and half of its vegetables, yet for far too long we’ve been forced to rely on outdated infrastructure that cannot keep up with today’s demands. Gavin Newsom and the California Democrats have pushed a radical environmental agenda that has stood in the way of numerous needed projects. Voters approved Prop 1 over 12 years ago, promising new dams and expanded reservoirs, yet the state has nothing to show for it. We can no longer wait for California Democrats to do their jobs. We are taking action and delivering results. These new investments will go directly toward repairing and upgrading the systems that move water across our state — including the Friant-Kern Canal, Delta-Mendota Canal, San Luis Canal, and Tehama-Colusa Canal, along with important work to expand water storage at Shasta Dam. Many of these systems have been severely impacted by decades of wear and groundwater overuse, causing land subsidence that has reduced water delivery capacity by as much as 60% in some areas. This new federal funding will help restore that lost capacity, improve efficiency, and ensure that water can be delivered reliably to the communities, farms, and businesses that depend on it. A stronger, more reliable water system means greater agricultural stability, stronger local economies, and a more secure food supply for our entire country. While this is a significant step forward, our work is not done. We will continue to advance policies that allow for expanded water storage, improved conveyance, and bringing California’s water management into the 21st century. Thank you for your continued support and for standing with me in the fight to secure a stronger future for the Central Valley. Sincerely

Congressman Vince Fong

subject: The NHGOP Victory Report - 6/26/26
body:
The NHGOP Victory Report - 6/26/26

| | | | | | |
Dear Friend,
**A Note from the Chairman**
Well, here it is; an event 250 years in the making! I remember in 1976 for the bicentennial was such a big deal. The Freedom Train was traveling around the country. I even won two tickets although I couldn’t go. My trivia question was how many lamps did Paul Revere put in the old North Church.
New Hampshire was never really center stage the way Virginia and Massachusetts was, but New Hampshire played a far larger role in the American Revolution than many people realize. Despite being one of the smallest colonies, it was among the first to actively resist British authority, the first colony to establish an independent government, and a significant source of soldiers, supplies, and naval support.
On December 14–15, 1774, months before the famous battles at Lexington and Concord, New Hampshire patriots captured British patriots seized gunpowder, muskets, and cannon at the Raid on Fort William and Mary in what is now New Castle. Many historians consider this one of the first overt acts of rebellion in the colonies.
In 2026, the next generation of patriots are taking up the cause to preserve the liberty that they presented to us. Approximately 450 people filed to run for various offices around the state. Still others have chosen to step aside. Whether it was one term or many, I thank them for their service to our state.
As we celebrate our 250th birthday, our nation’s brightest days are ahead of us. I am very optimistic that Republicans will rise to the challenge and we will win back the U.S. Senate and House seats. It won’t be easy, but it will be worth it. Revolutionary Granite Staters like John Sullivan, John Langdon, Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, and Matthew Thornton each risked everything they had to help us have the country we do today. Let us be worthy of their legacy.
**Election Integrity Workers Needed**
Over two-thirds of Republicans believe that the 2020 election was stolen. The legislature and Governor have worked to improve the integrity of New Hampshire elections in recent years, but there still are concerns out there.
Safe and secure elections require good laws, but also good people to monitor polling locations. In 2026 we need approximately 2,000 people to help maintain the integrity of our elections serving as either inspector of the elections or poll challengers. The description of these jobs is below. Please use the link provided to indicate your interest. Inspector of Elections is our #1 priority as they have to be appointed by July 15th.
**Inspector of Elections**
An Inspector of Elections is an election official appointed to assist in the administration of Election Day operations. Inspectors help verify voter checklists, process voters, maintain accurate election records, assist with ballot handling, and ensure election procedures are conducted fairly, accurately, and in accordance with New Hampshire law. They serve as part of the team responsible for the integrity and smooth operation of the polling place.
**Poll Challenger**
A Poll Challenger is a designated representative of a political party or candidate who observes the voting process and may raise concerns regarding a voter's eligibility when there is a legitimate basis to do so. Poll Challengers help promote transparency and confidence in elections by monitoring compliance with election laws while respecting voters' rights and maintaining order at the polling place.
**Social Media**
Be sure to follow us on social media so you can keep up to date on all the exciting things the party has to offer! We encourage you to share our posts so that we can continue to reach more people!

**Facebook:** [New Hampshire Republican State Committee](https://gop.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6abc8216f2c93cdbede56dda3&id=af3fd190f9&e=f3aa6419cd)

**YouTube:** [https://www.youtube.com/@NH_GOP](https://gop.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6abc8216f2c93cdbede56dda3&id=89ded04148&e=f3aa6419cd) (NH_GOP)

Become a Grassroots Giver today!With $10/month or $120/year you help us:

* Send 1500 texts to targeted voters to Get Out The Vote
* Send 325 mail pieces targeting vulnerable State House Democrats

Our goal is to have 1,000 Grassroots Givers. Won't you join us in investing in YOUR New Hampshire Republican Party? [https://secure.winred.com/new-hampshire-gop/grassroots-givers](https://gop.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6abc8216f2c93cdbede56dda3&id=4312f9a791&e=f3aa6419cd)

Scott MaltzieChairman

Peter,
Right now, rumors are swirling in the nation's capital.
In smoky backrooms across the city, conservative political operatives are whispering among themselves. They see the writing on the wall--the Senate is in serious jeopardy of falling to Democrats this November, perhaps even inevitable.
With only 7 months left of guaranteed control of the chamber necessary to confirm Trump's next picks for the Supreme Court, there's a growing push to force MAGA Justices Samuel Alito (age 76), Clarence Thomas (age 77), and John Roberts (age 71) to retire.
This would hand Trump three more Supreme Court Justice appointments and enshrine MAGA control over the Supreme Court for at least the next 40 years:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0013Dcv6aztupdO2mRFTslJ7enui8lVAlbrzlO9fF2MmMaB3xt7gjNRc3rv247lOf9BnuTgUo0ZIoQk1EiL3jUGqZllFNVegf2m80FkxpomQymL-fKJc8ZW_iZwPOUhIvrM8_sOFxQ5O7s85PIqLIA7lK-ehZ-e1ztiaXFLFAmB1uZAg0eAqNemoS90iUiQxpFC7YQF33qYPQWcc6ZwSLko2ayPhtOZRGwUDloOjxdmDpo=&c=nIXJLlYDO-Y1XKUdPmFYPzUU6Q2OfsidI_Ps_65sLKyZdUV7FkY7Aw==&ch=0ebo_KaK5pXEMq6sA2t1avt5sgPf3MPuju1VeTWHoqZqSqTVP-QRAw==)

To accomplish this, MAGA would use the so-called "nuclear option"--a change of Senate rules that allows the appointment of Supreme Court justices via a simple majority vote rather than the 60 vote threshold historically used to confirm justices.
Mitch McConnell used the nuclear option for Trump's appointments of Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Coney Barrett. Prior to that, the nuclear option had never been used before in American history for a Supreme Court Justice confirmation. We have seen and felt the consequences of those actions: Roe v. Wade overturned. The Voting Rights Act gutted. Trump handed criminal immunity. The Clean Air and Water Acts gutted.
We cannot endure the hell of another 40 years of a MAGA controlled Supreme Court. We cannot allow Donald Trump, a president who has won both of his elections by historically slim margins, to single-handedly pack this court and dictate the next 4 decades of American history.
That's why we're pushing for Democrats to use a nuclear option of their own--to reform and rebalance the Supreme Court by expanding the amount of justices on the court. This is the only way for Democrats to stop the hell to come. The Constitution gives us that power. Congress has changed the number of justices seven times. No amendment is required.
But for this to become a reality, Democrats need our help. We need to win back control of the House, Senate, and White House by 2028. That's why Defend Our Courts will be fighting for Democrats across the map in hotly contested House and Senate races this November.
This fight is necessary. Unpacking the court is non-negotiable. body:
Things have slowed down. We don’t know why.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2316%2E791427%2ErabBnP)
Friend — some bad news, and some good news.
**The bad:** We are just four days away from perhaps the most important FEC fundraising deadline of the entire election year, and our fundraising is still just way, way behind where we hoped it would be.
Things have slowed down. We don’t know why. We’re less than two months from Primary Election Day, and we’ve been non-stop organizing to oppose Trump’s harmful agenda in our district. We need resources to keep it up.
**The good:** No matter how far behind we are, four days is more than enough time to turn that around. We could even do it in a matter of hours.
That’s because we don’t suck up to billionaires and corporate lobbyists to raise money. We have thousands, if not millions, of like-minded folks out there who understand the stakes of this year’s elections and believe in what Ilhan stands for.
We’ve said it before, and we’ll say it again: If everyone reading this email chipped in $10 right now, we would hit our FEC fundraising goals four days before the deadline. **We just need people like you to step up.**
[**Please: make your first contribution to Ilhan Omar’s campaign for reelection today. Let’s smash this FEC goal, reelect Ilhan, and begin the hard work of cleaning up the mess that Trump’s administration has made.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260626-2-180&t=2&akid=2316%2E791427%2ErabBnP)

| | Peter, as we face our first Federal Election Commission (FEC) deadline of the general election, I still refuse to let this campaign distract me from fighting for my constituents.

From working to address our affordability crisis to securing disaster assistance and hundreds of millions of dollars for flood protection, I always strive to deliver results for our communities.

subject: Wanted to check back in
body:
It’s a small act, but when you’re running a people-powered campaign, every single signature counts.
| | | | | Hi there, Peter. I just wanted to check back in with you on this email I sent about our Make Stuff Cost Less campaign tour.
---
Sadly, we came up a few hundred folks short of our 25,000-endorsement goal – so I’m extending the deadline to **11:59 p.m. tonight.**
**If you’re with me in the fight to flip North Carolina blue, would you take 30 seconds now to add your name? It’s a small act, but when you’re running a people-powered campaign, every single signature counts. Here’s the best link for you:[_https:/act.roycooper.com/priorities_](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/mscl-endorse-cooper-0626-email?source=email_su_pros_jtk705&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=&askdif=&t=6&akid=1894%2E124072%2EBLCKPP)**
Thank you so much.
Roy
\---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: **Roy Cooper (via Cooper Victory Fund)** Date: Jun 25, 2026
Subject: Will you endorse my Senate campaign?
| |
| | |
---
[](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/mscl-endorse-cooper-0626-email?source=email_su_pros_jtk705&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=&askdif=&t=7&akid=1894%2E124072%2EBLCKPP)
[](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/mscl-endorse-cooper-0626-email?source=email_su_pros_jtk705&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=&askdif=&t=8&akid=1894%2E124072%2EBLCKPP)
Peter, I’ve been crisscrossing the state on my Make Stuff Cost Less campaign tour, talking with and listening to North Carolinians directly, and I keep hearing versions of the same thing:
🚨 Everything from gas to groceries is getting unaffordable.

🏠 Buying a house and planning for the future seems unthinkable.

🇺🇲 The American Dream feels unattainable.
**Stuff costs too much, and nobody in Washington DC seems to care.**
When I hear things like this, I know it’s time to get to work. That’s why I’m in this fight. As North Carolina’s next U.S. Senator, I will put the people before power, party and politics – as I did for eight years as Governor:
✅ We expanded Medicaid for hundreds of thousands of working North Carolinians.

✅ We added hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs.

✅ We increased teacher pay and expanded paid parental leave.
**Now, I’m ready to bring this North Carolina common sense to the U.S. Senate – but I need your help. The GOP is going all in to defeat me, and only by building a powerful grassroots team can I fight back and win.**
[Peter, will you add your name now to personally endorse my campaign for Senate? I’m aiming to gather 25,000 signatures before the end of the day, and it would mean a lot to have you with me in this fight.](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/mscl-endorse-cooper-0626-email?source=email_su_pros_jtk705&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=&askdif=&t=9&akid=1894%2E124072%2EBLCKPP)

---
Thank you,

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

body:
Here’s how we bring the Zohran coalition to every corner of the country.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260626-1&t=1&akid=3651%2E587540%2EhHs5IH)
Peter,
Young people across the country are looking to New York as a point of inspiration, and there’s a big reason why.
_Mayor Zohran Mamdani._
He’s the most exciting mayor this country has seen in a generation, hands down. The hope and electricity he’s created in New York City is palpable.
But Zohran knows as well as I do, he can’t carry out his working class agenda alone. Making campaign promises like free and fast buses a reality requires a fierce coalition of allies ready to back him up in Albany and Washington.
**That's exactly where Leaders We Deserve comes in — we’ve already helped build that coalition.**
**Claire Valdez** just won her primary for Congress in NY-07, and **Aber Kawas** just won hers for State Senate in Queens. Two more fearless fighters who will help carry Zohran's vision beyond City Hall.
**The eyes of the country are on young progressives right now, and this is our chance to prove not just that we can win — we __deliver__ on our promises.**
Part of why people trust Zohran is because he doesn't answer to special interests. He says what he believes and follows through. Unlike corporate Dems, his decisions are driven by principle, not by who's funding him. **Imagine what's possible if we had more people like that at every level of government.**
That’s why we’re not stopping at New York City.
Young voters across the country are seeing proof in real time that a better future is possible. We’re going to bring that same winning blueprint to state legislatures and Congress in every corner of the country.
But none of this happens without resources. Our work isn’t powered by special interests or corporate PACs. We do it all with the support of folks like you.
**[Will you pitch in $5 or whatever you can today to help us keep building this movement and elect the next generation of courageous young leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260626_1_coalition.-wHngH&refcode=em20260626-3651&amount=5&t=2&akid=3651%2E587540%2EhHs5IH)**

David Hogg

name: Alex Kelloff

body:
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
A Letter from Alex
For 14 months, I’ve traveled across every corner of our district, stretching from the Roaring Fork Valley to the San Juan mountains, and from Pueblo to Grand Junction. Then starting on May 7th we launched our By The People Tour, which lasted until June 14th. Our primary objective during this tour was listening directly to constituents’ concerns. We held 17 community workshops and received over 100 online submissions. We asked three foundational questions:
* What is working well and what do you love about living in your community?
* What have we lost under Donald Trump and Jeff Hurd, and what needs to be restored?
* What does the next Congress need to get done?
What we heard across the district was clear. People possess immense pride in their resilient communities, their public lands, and their unique rural values. We also heard how deeply frustrated people are by a broken system in Washington, as evidenced by skyrocketing cost of living, attacks on fundamental civil liberties, and an economy structured to favor the wealthy at the expense of working families.
This is The By The People Plan : a community-driven, locally sourced policy roadmap built to instruct the next member of Congress exactly how to fight for us, directly sourced from and by the people.
The Strategic Pillars of Our Plan
1. Eradicating Corruption & Restoring Government Integrity
Washington is failing because it has been captured by big money. In our tour workshops, our community overwhelmingly demanded an end to corporate political control.
The Legislative Directive: We will fight to overturn Citizens United, pass ironclad campaign finance reforms, implement mandatory term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court, oppose the SAVE Act, implement a national ban on partisan gerrymandering to ensure equitable representation and fair elections, and ban sitting politicians from insider stock trading and participation in financial prediction markets.
2. Protecting Our Public Lands, Water, & Climate Identity
Our public lands are central to our economy and our way of life. In places like Mesa County, where public lands make up 70% of the county, constituents made it clear that federal budget cuts have left our natural resources exposed.
The Legislative Directive: The plan fully restores funding and staffing to the U.S. Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management. We will legally help pass a new Colorado River Compact, protect critical local assets like Lake Nighthorse and the Crystal Reservoir, and restore withheld FEMA funds for aggressive local wildfire mitigation.
3. Stabilizing Rural Healthcare & Protecting the Safety Net
Cuts to Medicaid have pushed our rural medical infrastructure to the brink, leaving independent community institutions facing potential closure.
The Legislative Directive: We will protect local medical facilities by halting devastating cuts, investing in rural hospitals, and introducing a universal healthcare infrastructure in which everyone gets public health insurance with the individual option to opt out in favor of private insurance. Furthermore, we will codify reproductive freedom as a federal law and defend Social Security, Medicare, and Veterans benefits from political attacks.
4. Building a Rural Economy for the Working Class
From local housing constraints to rising grocery prices across the district, families are being squeezed out of their own hometowns.
The Legislative Directive: This plan tackles inflation and cost of living by working with affordable housing groups and non-profits to streamline federal regulations. We will eliminate tax loopholes for billionaires, deliver robust federal funding for rural physical infrastructure including roads, bridges, water treatment, and broadband access, and institute a Center of Excellence within the government to provide proven project blueprints for municipalities. We will aggressively enforce federal anti-monopoly laws against private equity firms buying up our mobile home parks, single-family neighborhoods, and RV parks.
5. Defending Human Rights & the Rule of Law
We are a district defined by neighbors who watch out for one another. The community expressed profound opposition to federal overreach and discriminatory practices that tear apart local families.
The Legislative Directive: We will champion comprehensive immigration reform that provides permanent protections for DACA recipients, an investment into our immigration court system, and a clear, functional pathway to citizenship, while reforming ICE operations to guarantee complete constitutional compliance.
— Alex
June Recap
June marked the successful conclusion of our By the People Tour, an initiative that took Alex to communities across Colorado's 3rd District to listen, learn, and build a campaign rooted in the priorities of the people.
The final stops of the tour brought Alex to Pueblo, Alamosa, Gunnison, and Grand Junction, where the tour concluded on June 14th. Throughout the tour, thousands of conversations with residents, local leaders, business owners, farmers, ranchers, healthcare providers, educators, and advocates reinforced the issues we heard time and again: affordability, healthcare, protecting public lands and water, strengthening rural economies, and restoring trust in government.
While the tour may have concluded, the work it inspired is just beginning. Our team has compiled what we heard from communities across all 27 counties into the By the People Plan — a roadmap shaped by the voices of the people of Colorado's 3rd District that will continue to guide Alex's priorities throughout this campaign and, if elected, in Congress.
The campaign also continued connecting with communities through events across the district. On June 13th, we joined supporters at the Mesa County Democrats' Spring Fling in Grand Junction, where we had the opportunity to visit with residents and discuss the future of Colorado's 3rd District.
On June 19th, Alex hosted a meet-and-greet at Gunbarrel Square in Rifle. After the event, he visited several of the small businesses in the building, hearing directly from owners about the opportunities and challenges they face. We are grateful to everyone who joined us for thoughtful conversations about the issues that matter most to Western Colorado.
The following day, Alex participated in a candidate forum in Durango, continuing his commitment to engaging directly with voters and answering their questions. At the same time, members of our campaign proudly represented Alex at the Strawberry Days Parade in Glenwood Springs, connecting with residents and celebrating one of the region's longest-standing community traditions.
On June 21st, Alex spent Father's Day in Durango attending a breakfast hosted by the La Plata County Democrats. It was another meaningful opportunity to connect with community members, discuss the issues facing Southern Colorado, and hear directly from voters about the priorities they want their next representative in Congress to champion. We are grateful to the La Plata County Democrats for their warm welcome and to everyone who took time to join the conversation.
As we move into the next phase of the campaign, our commitment remains unchanged. We will continue showing up, listening, and working every day to earn the trust of the people of Colorado's 3rd District. The By the People Tour may have come to an end for the moment, but the conversations, and our commitment to putting the people of this district first, will continue throughout this campaign.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/1_6.jpg]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/2_6.jpg]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/3_4.jpg]
We are also proud to announce that Alex earned the endorsement of Nurses for America. In their endorsement, they shared:
“Your commitment to Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, protecting our environment, gun safety, voting rights, comprehensive reproductive health services, LGBTQ+ rights, gender affirming care, affordable access to health care, disability rights, and public broadcasting matches our NFA mission.”
We are honored to have the support of Nurses for America and grateful for their recognition of Alex's commitment to expanding access to affordable healthcare, protecting essential public services, and advocating for the well-being of communities across Colorado's 3rd District.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/118157/images/nurse.jpg]
Holding Hurd Accountable
Zero Influence When it Counts
Jeff Hurd and Dark Money Groups are spending a fortune on ads trying to convince us that he has an inside track in Washington, but his actual record shows he has zero influence where it counts. When the administration issued its final denial of over $41 million in federal disaster funding for Colorado, Hurd completely failed to deliver for his district. clean_body: [] A Letter from Alex For 14 months, I’ve traveled across every corner of our district, stretching from the Roaring Fork Valley to the San Juan mountains, and from Pueblo to Grand Junction. Then starting on May 7th we launched our By The People Tour, which lasted until June 14th. Our primary objective during this tour was listening directly to constituents’ concerns. We held 17 community workshops and received over 100 online submissions. We asked three foundational questions: What is working well and what do you love about living in your community? What have we lost under Donald Trump and Jeff Hurd, and what needs to be restored? * What does the next Congress need to get done? What we heard across the district was clear. People possess immense pride in their resilient communities, their public lands, and their unique rural values. We also heard how deeply frustrated people are by a broken system in Washington, as evidenced by skyrocketing cost of living, attacks on fundamental civil liberties, and an economy structured to favor the wealthy at the expense of working families. This is The By The People Plan : a community-driven, locally sourced policy roadmap built to instruct the next member of Congress exactly how to fight for us, directly sourced from and by the people. The Strategic Pillars of Our Plan 1. Eradicating Corruption & Restoring Government Integrity Washington is failing because it has been captured by big money. In our tour workshops, our community overwhelmingly demanded an end to corporate political control. The Legislative Directive: We will fight to overturn Citizens United, pass ironclad campaign finance reforms, implement mandatory term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court, oppose the SAVE Act, implement a national ban on partisan gerrymandering to ensure equitable representation and fair elections, and ban sitting politicians from insider stock trading and participation in financial prediction markets. 2. Protecting Our Public Lands, Water, & Climate Identity Our public lands are central to our economy and our way of life. In places like Mesa County, where public lands make up 70% of the county, constituents made it clear that federal budget cuts have left our natural resources exposed. The Legislative Directive: The plan fully restores funding and staffing to the U.S. Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management. We will legally help pass a new Colorado River Compact, protect critical local assets like Lake Nighthorse and the Crystal Reservoir, and restore withheld FEMA funds for aggressive local wildfire mitigation. 3. Stabilizing Rural Healthcare & Protecting the Safety Net Cuts to Medicaid have pushed our rural medical infrastructure to the brink, leaving independent community institutions facing potential closure. The Legislative Directive: We will protect local medical facilities by halting devastating cuts, investing in rural hospitals, and introducing a universal healthcare infrastructure in which everyone gets public health insurance with the individual option to opt out in favor of private insurance. Furthermore, we will codify reproductive freedom as a federal law and defend Social Security, Medicare, and Veterans benefits from political attacks. 4. Building a Rural Economy for the Working Class From local housing constraints to rising grocery prices across the district, families are being squeezed out of their own hometowns. The Legislative Directive: This plan tackles inflation and cost of living by working with affordable housing groups and non-profits to streamline federal regulations. We will eliminate tax loopholes for billionaires, deliver robust federal funding for rural physical infrastructure including roads, bridges, water treatment, and broadband access, and institute a Center of Excellence within the government to provide proven project blueprints for municipalities. We will aggressively enforce federal anti-monopoly laws against private equity firms buying up our mobile home parks, single-family neighborhoods, and RV parks. 5. Defending Human Rights & the Rule of Law We are a district defined by neighbors who watch out for one another. The community expressed profound opposition to federal overreach and discriminatory practices that tear apart local families. The Legislative Directive: We will champion comprehensive immigration reform that provides permanent protections for DACA recipients, an investment into our immigration court system, and a clear, functional pathway to citizenship, while reforming ICE operations to guarantee complete constitutional compliance. — Alex June Recap June marked the successful conclusion of our By the People Tour, an initiative that took Alex to communities across Colorado's 3rd District to listen, learn, and build a campaign rooted in the priorities of the people. The final stops of the tour brought Alex to Pueblo, Alamosa, Gunnison, and Grand Junction, where the tour concluded on June 14th. Throughout the tour, thousands of conversations with residents, local leaders, business owners, farmers, ranchers, healthcare providers, educators, and advocates reinforced the issues we heard time and again: affordability, healthcare, protecting public lands and water, strengthening rural economies, and restoring trust in government. While the tour may have concluded, the work it inspired is just beginning. Our team has compiled what we heard from communities across all 27 counties into the By the People Plan — a roadmap shaped by the voices of the people of Colorado's 3rd District that will continue to guide Alex's priorities throughout this campaign and, if elected, in Congress. The campaign also continued connecting with communities through events across the district. On June 13th, we joined supporters at the Mesa County Democrats' Spring Fling in Grand Junction, where we had the opportunity to visit with residents and discuss the future of Colorado's 3rd District. After the event, he visited several of the small businesses in the building, hearing directly from owners about the opportunities and challenges they face. We are grateful to everyone who joined us for thoughtful conversations about the issues that matter most to Western Colorado. The following day, Alex participated in a candidate forum in Durango, continuing his commitment to engaging directly with voters and answering their questions. At the same time, members of our campaign proudly represented Alex at the Strawberry Days Parade in Glenwood Springs, connecting with residents and celebrating one of the region's longest-standing community traditions. On June 21st, Alex spent Father's Day in Durango attending a breakfast hosted by the La Plata County Democrats. It was another meaningful opportunity to connect with community members, discuss the issues facing Southern Colorado, and hear directly from voters about the priorities they want their next representative in Congress to champion. We are grateful to the La Plata County Democrats for their warm welcome and to everyone who took time to join the conversation. Hi friend, I’m going to get a little insider baseball on you. Please stick with me through it. **In four days, we are going to have to publicly file our financial records with the state.** ICYMI, this means that everyone from my opponents and their teams, the media, and the deep-pocketed special interests will be able to see everything I have in the bank and make assumptions about my momentum. [**I’m sure I don’t need to explain why this is such a critical moment for my campaign. You’re smart and get it. But I truly need you to dig deep if you can and contribute before this filing. Can I count on you?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/8lC0N03O692R) **This isn’t our first public filing, but it is the last one that makes a material difference before the primary** – _can you believe the primary is less than 3 months away_ 🤯? I trust you, really, so I want to share exactly what we learned during our last public filing:
---
| | **Q1 PUBLIC FILING INSIGHTS
TEAM ANDERBOIS INTERNAL MEMO**
* More Rhode Islanders contributed to our campaign than to any other campaign in this race!

* BUT we are running behind in total raised and total cash on hand.

* Our average contribution is significantly lower than that of my opponents. **This means this campaign belongs to real people. Not PACs. Not insiders. Not a handful of wealthy donors writing huge checks.**

**I am so proud of the grassroots support — _This is a good thing, but it makes it hard to compete dollar-for-dollar._**
| From what we saw in our opponents’ reports, it’s safe to say there’s only one candidate with the momentum to win the primary that has the resources, support, and infrastructure to win in the general election.

**That candidate is Sue AnderBois.**

**However, the cash on hand is the biggest weakness we face. It is imperative that we post strong numbers for the filing that closes on June 30th.**
---

**[Please, if you are able, contribute now and help this campaign have the strongest showing possible.](https://sue4ri.com/l/ohDxY6XRP6s6)**
| [ **DONATE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/B2b1TWOaV66S)
---
We’ve taken the time to track my opponents’ spending patterns and project what we need to effectively compete. We have an audacious goal of raising an additional $25,000 before my public filing on June 30th. If we hit that goal, we can execute a smart outreach strategy — _even if one of our opponents has more money in the bank than we do._ Every campaign is currently making decisions about final mailer budgets, digital advertising spends from now until Primary Day, placing final print orders for organizing resources, etc. **The winner will not be the one who has the highest amount of dollars raised. The winner will be the candidate who is executing a campaign that is the most efficient, nimble, and strategic to increase their name recognition before voting starts.** That’s why this deadline matters so much to our campaign. This is the last meaningful public filing before the primary. It's the last one where we can look at the numbers, make adjustments based on our opponents' raise and spending (they are going to do the same with us), and build the kind of campaign that can win the primary and compete all the way through Election Day. **If you've been waiting for the right time to give for the first time or give again, this is it.** [**Will you help us chase down this goal of $25,000 more raised from grassroots donors before midnight on June 30?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/d3yH00b8uhqi)

clean_body: The end of June isn't just the end of another month, Peter. It's also the end of our second fundraising quarter of this election year. But before we ask you to = we want to explain what an end-of-quarter fundraising goal actually is, and why it's so important to our campaign: Every year is divided into four fundraising quarters. At the end of each quarter, campaigns (like this one) are required to publicly report how much money they've raised. And those numbers don't stay private. When a campaign reports its quarterly fundraising, they're reviewed by political strategists, outside groups, the media, and especially opponents. The fundraising reports filed at the end of this month will help determine where money gets spent, which races receive attention, and which campaigns are viewed as having the resources needed to win. With our primary election getting closer, Wesley is working every day to reach voters across St. Louis and share his vision for our communities, and build the campaign infrastructure needed to win. But none of that happens without grassroots supporters stepping up. We're working to raise $15,000 before our end-of-quarter deadline so we can continue reaching voters, growing our campaign, and showing that this campaign has the strength to compete and re-elect https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
It’s clear what they want to do — incite someone to hurt me or my family.
I’m Christian Urrutia, the Democrat running for Congress in NH-01, America's most vulnerable open blue seat. I'm an economic populist and a first-generation Mexican-American son of immigrants. An Army officer. And someone who still believes in this country enough to fight for it.
To the far-right someone like me attaining elected office is an existential threat.
These type of extremists showed up to an event I spoke at waving Nazi flags trying to stop me from speaking (I gave my speech anyways). They send me messages telling me that my life may “abruptly come to an end.” They send me pictures of nooses.
Because they hate me, they hate us, and they hate our vision.
This isn’t just about me. It’s about whether we let hate and political violence take root here in America. Or whether we stand up and say no. You know where I stand. But I can’t do this alone.
If you can, please make a donation to help us beef up security for my staff and I so we can continue rolling with the punches. Whether it's $50, $20, or even just $10 it will have an outsized impact. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]

body:
| | | | | [|

|
---
| |
# Nationwide Stuff Costs Too Much Weekend of Action With More Than 200 On-The-Ground Events Taking Place in Communities Throughout the Country
---
| | **Associated Press:** [DNC plans weekend of events to focus on affordability concerns](https://us.list-manage.com/pBjwZkSYaMG?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
---
| |
_While focusing on affordability and holding Republicans accountable for making life more expensive, thousands of Democrats will spend the weekend participating in canvasses, community meetings, voter registration drives, volunteer trainings, phone banks, and service events that reach, engage, and mobilize working families_ Today, the DNC [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/bC83j5KHiDn?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the launch of a nationwide _Stuff Costs Too Much Weekend of Action_ that will **train 150 new organizers, engage thousands of volunteers, and include more than 200 on-the-ground events** throughout the country today, Saturday, and Sunday. Democratic volunteers, organizers, and campaign staff will spend the weekend having nearly 10,000 conversations with working families during door-to-door canvases, innovative voter registration drives, neighborhood meetings, Know Your Rights trainings, service events, and phone banks. While holding Republicans accountable for jacking up costs, the weekend will also focus on the work Democrats are doing to make life more affordable.
---
| [SOCIAL TOOLKIT](https://us.list-manage.com/Wggs6ryEitm?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
---
| |
_In response to the launch of the Stuff Costs Too Much Weekend of Action,**DNC Chair Ken Martin released the following statement:**_ “From groceries and gas to healthcare, childcare, rent, and utilities, everything costs too damn much under Donald Trump and the Republicans. And to stop these skyrocketing prices that are crushing working families, we have to stop the Republicans in November. That’s why Democrats are launching this nationwide weekend of action to reach, engage, register, and mobilize voters who will make the difference in races up and down the ballot. By organizing early and organizing everywhere, Democrats will win these midterms and get to work making life more affordable.” The nationwide weekend of action will feature affordability-focused events with elected officials and partner organizations. That includes:
* **An organizer bootcamp featuring Gov. Lujan Grisham.** The bootcamp will train 150 new organizers to join campaigns this cycle.
* **A voter registration drive targeting shift workers and gig workers.** When We Count fellows will be registering voters at cost-salient locations such as grocery stores, laundromats, thrift stores, gas stations, discount stores, transit stops, dollar stores, food courts, check-cashing areas. This is in addition to targeting shift workers at airport rideshare waiting lots, popular food delivery pickup corridors, and stadium staff entrances.
* **Door knocking and block walking in critical and overlooked areas throughout the country.** This includes canvassing in all four of Nevada’s Congressional Districts with the following special guests: Democratic nominee for governor Aaron Ford, Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor Sandra Jauregui, Democratic nominee for attorney general Nicole Cannizzaro, and Democratic nominee for the Second Congressional District Teresa Benitez-Thompson. Canvasses also include door knocking in Flagstaff, Tucson, Scottsdale, Phoenix, Philadelphia, Scranton, Reading, Erie, Pittsburgh, State College, Racine, Eau Claire, Oshkosh, Green Bay, Milwaukee, Sheboygan, Madison, and many other communities.
* **Phonebanking in communities throughout the country.** This includes talking to voters in NY-22 and OH-01 about how the affordability crisis has been affecting their daily lives. Both of these districts have seen gas prices rise to levels that are higher than the national average, with the price per gallon seeing over a 40% increase since the start of Trump’s unnecessary war with Iran.
* **Service events in battleground states.** This includes a North Las Vegas community food drive with the Nevada Coordinated Campaign that mobilizes volunteers to meet, engage, listen to, and serve voters where they are. There will also be a park cleanup event in Nevada where volunteers will listen to families about their concerns around rising costs and share Democratic efforts to make life more affordable. Additionally, the Wisconsin Coordinated Campaign and the Kenosha County Democratic Party are collecting and distributing school supplies to families in need. This is an opportunity to meet, listen to, connect with, and serve voters.
* **A national activation call focused on the impact of Trump’s failing economy on Black workers.** The call will feature Cleveland Mayor Justin Bibb, Collective PAC Founder and President Quentin James, the Black Men Vote Executive Director Michael Bland, and the Maricopa Area Labor Federation.

The _Stuff Costs Too Much Weekend of Action_ builds on the DNC’s work to reach people where they are, engage communities, register voters, sign up volunteers, and invest in year-round, on-the-ground organizing. In the spring, the DNC held a [National Voter Registration Week of Action](https://us.list-manage.com/fLxDKaoJyry?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) — with more than 100 events — and published [The Playbook](https://us.list-manage.com/fTn2bYR49XU?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), an actionable guide to help build winning campaigns that includes best practices, case studies, and innovations in organizing. Earlier this year, the DNC launched [When We Count](https://us.list-manage.com/bIEY1sT_U4D?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), the largest-ever campaign to register and mobilize the next generation of Democratic voters ahead of the midterms. The DNC also launched the [NextWave Regional Bootcamp](https://us.list-manage.com/eTaNoWqtG6P?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), the largest-ever in-person campaign training program. Additionally, the DNC spearheaded [Local Listeners](https://us.list-manage.com/dicg1dyjDFA?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), a new voter contact initiative to engage over one million infrequent voters across key congressional districts and states. As Republicans have gutted healthcare and Trump has [bragged](https://us.list-manage.com/dN6bw2IyVJf?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) that “I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation,” costs for just about everything have continued to skyrocket and inflation has [surged](https://us.list-manage.com/18PZ1NcNtjR?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) to its highest rate in years. The average household has already had to [spend](https://us.list-manage.com/8nBTWb8uHvR?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) at least $3,100 more under Republicans. That [includes](https://us.list-manage.com/OjwQn32lCv3?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) $310 more on groceries including from their reckless tariffs, $372 more on gas thanks to their war of choice in Iran, $110 more on electricity, and $622 more on housing. This rise in prices is in addition to healthcare premiums [jumping](https://us.list-manage.com/Nhggr3O7Rhz?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) by an average of 58% after Republicans repeatedly refused to extend the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.
