## Christmas Sweater Kid Charms World Cup Fans
A young Mexico fan named Santi didn't have an official jersey for [Mexico's World Cup opener](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTSN0a9FIi9QoVadS9tCkFWlxKdPgjkGvTvn3gFLlAysEAg8H363v9Nj74tP80kWa3u5VdXhO1GoiZyrodxVeOptZGhqn89jbkJwWzokAFQgGq1Rof3uvQ29kRIcme5quecBSDVNf-mOnmblrJaXKDRBy13Ual6AuNVtPt63rr_fxZEwoVCqHE9aL0ZqdpdEY70nJ03SDIes7lcs8-8UEuvPOTymXLsQ_zwXzWTv7ocOlwaa1dLL2ocP70HS6UmAobnyIl7nDxn5yI4aBwVnjnR9oh0stvGZxJsBPDnUqlNxjHVKCRKT7t8I8D7o94UgGXC7RcgoXtcUI0vB0gpR7VKDtc-jLbs_kQfFW6G8QejQ9_P_N_Yz9n_BMAAP__wWiZNA) against South Africa in Mexico City, so he improvised with a green Christmas sweater featuring Santa Claus, white shorts, and red boots. His mother said he chose the outfit because he wanted to represent the colors of the Mexican flag. Photos and video of Santi quickly went viral, prompting broadcaster Claro Sports to ask viewers for [help identifying him](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQAL8GOpBZjDGFi2vocu2VyMHreC9LHNkrUP7-lPuF149mpPlz226emF6P3_5AFx9xk5i3F16VUQTLtqdCVQ5f64VesDwpcD6R_QYKTKdMB2YLnviz6Ta4iAg4tuiG2cKk9GiGNjlQJkC8x9FabTRO8b7AMiu_W6uXyfqW3NemDBhQyqihN_MerJ2inyPO4xQbrTCQ5NL_zfSShJE_-cTS7_lo2SWRd23GXw2sDaz1nYvU_uNTzl-ggdUXoZ2xNrDKlbsnhdqdVDx3h39iTRSlu3Lh0A0LWK3Gce6THNwWF94XMVM1c6PV4_DE_6Py41ung38BAAD__6sPgNI). The story resonated with fans around the world, who shared their own memories of finding creative ways to support their teams when money was tight. After Santi was located, Mexico forward Santiago Gimenez sent him a personalized national team jersey and a video message. "_We have the same name,_ " [Santiago told him](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu5CAURb8Gd7bwsw12QbGNu9l2S_QEjzEbDCNghszfR5NE-YHUV7r3nvPvoi_og4_Xv3iSclenq0s6UiuBaqWszZF9qSeW0ggr5TdvQ3pQQA0cRM9FD0Jb9OGp584qRwQ0daRGucLC50mM3aHsZuW8oRATGjQr2WUbxSZpnGBETnPn1auNCxDAueDjIKSx67o4lI7ktDg2c7K-pjz8Tz7Wg1x4pgflwaSzC-qo9VbY9IfBzmBvrQ1HCvgKGez3wmCnWClX9PGkWBnsX3uj3Ljc5o3B_gPaf5P2J717k3qHsW8pB9ub-43B3mVlb82H4IuQbObXE334_FF_LfCh4CMAAP__wBWGWA). "_I just wanted to send you a big hug, many blessings, and I hope you like the gift_."
## Learning Sign Language for Love

A children's vocabulary book first published in 1985 has become an [Amazon bestseller](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2urCAUhZ9GOwyDgkxBcRu7ue0tyUY2yp2tTIDRzNufeHLe4JQrK1k_37-HfUCkuC9_YUMTlmBrSHbHsxDWitnOa46lblDKiVAxP6OndCCBFVwoxhUTynqI9LFD601AFNi3aG6jFpIPvbq1q5EguZ6VHJ2SUoDX994NGpzvuVbufm-judK4EkpwrvitU-PstZYBxoBjL0MzcPSxptz9T3GvKwb6pANzN6etJbPW-ipN_6cRUyOm8zw7j_uBebz8RkzXoUZMlGYg9iNcepPHzOBd15QLGzj7IGSWyLNn9IW5lJ7M4Zw2LOwq2-OyVuawVFaQCHObjX-dkSgWNTYDXzaI9D2p_prlYcRXAAAA__-7Loy9) more than four decades after its authors gave up on ever making money from it. _The Weighty Word Book_ , co-authored by Elissa Guralnick, Paul Levitt, and the late Douglas Burger, teaches advanced vocabulary through puns and illustrations. **Donald Trump just said the quiet part out loud, friend.**
He abruptly canceled an event focused on lowering housing costs and announced that he would not move forward until Congress passed the SAVE Act — the voter suppression bill that would require millions of Americans to produce documentary proof of citizenship just to register to vote.
Instead of focusing on lowering costs for working families, Trump demanded that Republicans prioritize legislation that would make it harder for eligible Americans to vote.
We now know he privately pressured Republican senators to pass the SAVE Act because he believes Republicans won’t win the 2026 midterms without it.
**The quiet part is no longer quiet. That is why Democratic Secretaries of State have fought so hard against the SAVE Act.**
They understand that election security and voter suppression are not the same thing, and they refuse to let Washington politicians rewrite the rules simply because they fear the outcome of an election.

Their desire for fewer restrictions on firearms officially outweighed American families’ desire for a safe country in the eyes of the captured, corrupt Supreme Court.** [**The Supreme Court is supposed to rule on behalf of We the People, not wealthy extremists. Hawaii’s law had banned people from carrying concealed handguns on any private property open to the public without receiving the owner’s express permission—think grocery stores, hotels, friend’s houses. The Supreme Court overturned it. Most Americans already know that guns don't belong in grocery stores, concert venues, restaurants, and their neighbors' homes unless someone explicitly says otherwise. That is not a radical position. That is common sense. And it is what Hawaii's law reflected. **But common sense doesn't matter to a Court that answers to the gun lobby and the dark money interests that spent decades engineering its majority.** This is the same Court that has called the Second Amendment a 'disfavored right,' expanded gun rights far beyond anything the framers contemplated, and consistently made it harder for states to protect their own residents. **Today's ruling is not a surprise. It is a pattern.** [**Congress cannot allow the Supreme Court to keep acting against the interests of the American people. We must demand that they make a plan and take action to rein in the Supreme Court and unrig our system.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOax_Tb2bOJVOyFl36_-dfzE82mSDDG_VK0ftS9ZBBaT7JNTskSLiKSJsfuTK408JLQYRpHtG5H74bKY_eiHVxqJnYihDdQYNZ261snDhOnv9doQAL_K1vlk3TD5T0zxszT-7tpsr601DSTZJyONNn8cHqSmhR20Pcvy6IF9lYiudy7Oz6C7-nx_xp5jZLLb7Vuxum-asb5UmaZk9fVzri4inR82mQe4bRqdHLJojUEwHrQst8RSDqHL4-iqK7GdJmHSA9EY3KZvMswnx4TTjRsU_kfrDXGcNVRUr0pmHu9HEpKqQqsMB_BE0gGBY85Tgvn51RdH2Py_uAPKnhcGCg83WRZ3R9ybTyErSkc2bC5R5AVN6E1PG65c8AoxNZ3uZDFokKBUYnZVOuuZYECmaiQ8jA/4rt/0BntR2KxRPie1b7PGHYzFg/h1/h001.BBO59dnWt19tq4KCyQCQmR_XF6AbjYQG3E5XMDktCzk) [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOax_Tb2bOJVOyFl36_-dfzE82mSDDG_VK0ftS9ZBBaT7JNTskSLiKSJsfuTK408JLQYRpHtG5H74bKY_eiHVxqJnYihDdQYNZ261snDhOnv9doQAL_K1vlk3TD5T0zxszT-7tpsr601DSTZJyONNn8cHqSmhR20Pcvy6IF9lYiudy7Oz6C7-nx_xp5jZLLb7VuxBPOI807kIM4XXR5OBHRxptFMUNX1-ushR403qAjAlKnsDis7zqjesJcX2oACC-qhMQAC48sO2sLtfNLtAZcH2tOtBNe9E5GwHhF2KsV1Q22zfWvz-FR4WplNeTzALJG5w0okvIFRmp7yu5ZDOtBaV_SJcca7vqvprQ_kJ9MrTxmOEUsjUqgeNHLGrn1UMOghPOVaZsevsLXDiIKzZk8hTQ/4rt/0BntR2KxRPie1b7PGHYzFg/h2/h001.GBxqdBYZW1yUhxIcpFZP5Z9ZBlmOeCUK3VuVWQ5FxxA) **This is what a captured Court looks like in practice.** It is not an abstract threat to democratic norms. ## PUBLIC DENIED THE RIGHT TO VOTE - CODY JOINS LAWSUIT AGAINST UNELECTED JUDGES
---
Cody shares another exclusive investigation that is shocking residents across Skagit County. According to public records Cody reveals in his most recent video, the public has been denied the constitutional right to vote for Skagit County Superior Court judges. Although the Constitution of the State of Washington requires at least one elected judge in each county, not a single vote was cast for any of the judges declaring to be serving in the current term. of the Skagit County Superior Court. According to Cody, "We are a Constitutional Republic that requires elections. We are not a monarchy, and we do not recognize these four Judges as Royalty who are ordained to rule over us" Cody Hart for Government Accountability

[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/d85aaba9-da55-4cf1-8784-94a75a0ddd5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**Lawrence O 'Donnell: **Governor, what is the biggest difference between this campaign and your last winning campaign for Governor? How have the issues changed?_
_**Roy Cooper:** Well, right now, Lawrence, people are getting crushed by higher prices from food to utilities to rent to health care. And the people in Washington, the politicians there, are forgetting about the people. They're paying more attention to their own power. And you can see it in all of these bad policies that are being passed that are championed by my opponent Michael Whatley, like tariffs on farmers. Pender in Wilson County is getting killed with his fertilizer and equipment costs. Veterans like Tim worried about his VA benefits. Moms like Meredith who's afraid of health care cuts because her daughter has cerebral palsy and is on Medicaid, and we know how Washington is attacking health care right now. We just can't have this. We need change. I'm excited about running for office. The people will always be my focus. I will never forget them like the politicians who are there now. We got to change. You can see my policy proposals at roycooper.com. You can also contribute. You can also volunteer to help us. We need your help because we've got to take this seat in North Carolina in order to take back the Senate majority in Washington._
_**Lawrence O 'Donnell:** So Donald Trump was scheduled to sign a bipartisan bill for trying to help with the costs of housing. An affordability bill supported by Elizabeth Warren on the Democratic side, supported by most of the Republicans in the Senate, 85 votes in the Senate. Donald Trump refused to sign it because he was mad at the Republicans in the Senate about something unrelated to that bill at all. And so that bill is sitting there unsigned tonight. And Donald Trump reportedly said he doesn't give a crap. He said, "I don't give a crap," and I'm cleaning that up a bit, "I don't give a crap about the affordability of housing."_
_**Roy Cooper:** And Congress is going home. It's pretty clear that Washington is broken right now. And I will get there and work across the aisle to make sure that we address the cost of living for people. This bill was a good one. It didn't do everything that we wanted, but it certainly helped with rent. It helped make more housing available to people. Clearly we've got an administration in Washington that's not paying attention to the people of North Carolina. We got to stop it. You're seeing what they will do in order to be able to keep their power. They're spending hundreds of millions of dollars here in North Carolina to try to keep me from being elected. We've got to fight back. That's going to happen in every swing state. We can't take anything for granted here. If we're going to take back the legislative branch of government so that we can take back the constitutional authority that the framers intended, we've got to make sure that we get people out to vote and we win these races._
_**Lawrence O 'Donnell:** So, new reporting in the New York Times shows that the latest inflation data shows a surge in inflation because of Donald Trump's war and the increase in gasoline prices and diesel fuel prices. But, the bad news is that underneath all of that, the underlying inflationary trend was also increasing and that is not going to come down when the price of oil comes down. Are voters expecting in North Carolina a sudden relief for their economic problems if oil starts to flow through the Strait of Hormuz?_
_**Roy Cooper:** No, I think they recognize that there's going to be a long time before they get any benefit from this. My opponent Michael Whatley is trying to convince people that prices are down and that we have defeated inflation because he has to continue to ingratiate himself to this President. At the end of the day, the people of North Carolina are not going to buy that. I heard Congressman Raskin talking about Republicans in Congress now aren't supporting the slush fund. Well, I got somebody who's supporting it here in North Carolina, and that's Michael Whatley because he knows he has to. We don't need a Senator in North Carolina who's going to do and say whatever this President tells him to do and say. We need a Senator who is going to be independent and who's going to put the total focus on the people. And that's what I'm going to do when I get elected._

We’re almost there! Just four more sleeps until election night. Many people turn in their ballots at the last minute and we would love your help connecting with them. | | | | _**FROM THE DESK OF NEWT GINGRICH**_
---
Peter, I have been studying American elections for over fifty years. I helped engineer the 1994 Republican Revolution that gave us our first House majority in decades. I know what a warning sign looks like. And I am writing to you today because **what is happening in Texas right now is one of the most serious warning signs I have seen in a generation**.

_Let me give you the facts._

A new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research shows Democrat James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47 to 44 percent in the Texas Senate race. Cook Political Report downgraded the race from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. And Talarico has raised over $40 million for this race, including $27 million in a single quarter, the largest first-quarter fundraising haul ever recorded by a Senate candidate in American history.

Now let me give you the history, because this is where it gets alarming.

**The party that has Majority control almost always loses ground in midterm elections.** It happened to Franklin Roosevelt in 1938. It happened to Lyndon Johnson in 1966. It happened to Bill Clinton in 1994. It happened to Barack Obama in 2010. And frankly, it happened to us in 2018. The American electorate has a long and consistent pattern of using the midterm election to push back against the party in power, and anyone who tells you 2026 will be different is not being honest with you.

The Democrats know this history better than anyone. They are running and fully supporting James Talarico in Texas because they have looked at the historical map, seen the midterm pattern, calculated the fundraising numbers, and decided that Texas is winnable. And right now, the polling and the money say they may be correct.

Here is what makes this moment even more critical. Talarico had no runoff. He spent three months doing nothing but raising money and organizing for the general election. He started the general election campaign with a three-month head start, a 3-point lead, and a $38 million fundraising advantage.

**_I have seen what happens when Republicans ignore these early warning signs. I have also seen what happens when we take them seriously and fight back._**

In 1994 we took them seriously. We organized. We raised the money. We delivered a message that resonated with the American people. And we won.

**Ken Paxton can win this race.** President Trump has already called James Talarico the worst Texas candidate he has ever seen and pledged to campaign across the state for Ken. But presidential rallies do not close a $38 million fundraising gap. Only grassroots conservatives like you can do that.

[**I am asking you today, as someone who has spent five decades fighting for this country and this party, to make an urgent contribution to Ken Paxton's campaign. clean_body: You need to take this seriously This is a warning sign. You need to take this seriously | | | | FROM THE DESK OF NEWT GINGRICH Peter, I have been studying American elections for over fifty years. I helped engineer the 1994 Republican Revolution that gave us our first House majority in decades. I know what a warning sign looks like. And I am writing to you today because what is happening in Texas right now is one of the most serious warning signs I have seen in a generation. Let me give you the facts. A new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research shows Democrat James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47 to 44 percent in the Texas Senate race. Cook Political Report downgraded the race from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. And Talarico has raised over $40 million for this race, including $27 million in a single quarter, the largest first-quarter fundraising haul ever recorded by a Senate candidate in American history. Now let me give you the history, because this is where it gets alarming. The party that has Majority control almost always loses ground in midterm elections. It happened to Franklin Roosevelt in 1938. It happened to Lyndon Johnson in 1966. It happened to Bill Clinton in 1994. It happened to Barack Obama in 2010. And frankly, it happened to us in 2018. The American electorate has a long and consistent pattern of using the midterm election to push back against the party in power, and anyone who tells you 2026 will be different is not being honest with you. The Democrats know this history better than anyone. They are running and fully supporting James Talarico in Texas because they have looked at the historical map, seen the midterm pattern, calculated the fundraising numbers, and decided that Texas is winnable. And right now, the polling and the money say they may be correct. Here is what makes this moment even more critical. Talarico had no runoff. He spent three months doing nothing but raising money and organizing for the general election. He started the general election campaign with a three-month head start, a 3-point lead, and a $38 million fundraising advantage. I have seen what happens when Republicans ignore these early warning signs. I have also seen what happens when we take them seriously and fight back. In 1994 we took them seriously. We organized. We raised the money. We delivered a message that resonated with the American people. And we won. Ken Paxton can win this race. President Trump has already called James Talarico the worst Texas candidate he has ever seen and pledged to campaign across the state for Ken. But presidential rallies do not close a $38 million fundraising gap. Only grassroots conservatives like you can do that. Texas is not going to flip because the Democrats got lucky. It will only flip if we let them. Do not let them flip Texas! Thanks, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House P.S. | | | Paid for by Ken Paxton for Senate | | PO BOX 3476 MCKINNEY, TX 75070 | | |

**Under Trump, New Mexicans’ annual electricity bills are up _8% per family_. ** When you work hard in America, that should mean something. At the very least, it should mean you aren’t forced to make tradeoffs between your health care, rent, and energy bills. But President Trump’s war on affordable, American-made energy and his massive tariff-taxes are making things worse, not better. Every hardworking person in New Mexico deserves stability and financial security. Period. I am fighting to bring costs down so this can be a reality. One of the ways we can do that is by helping homeowners and renters upgrade to modern, energy-efficient appliances that reduce monthly utility bills and make homes more comfortable year-round. That’s exactly what I intended when I created the federal home energy rebate program. My program helps families cover the upfront costs of buying efficient electric appliances and making home upgrades that will deliver years of savings. **But now, the Trump administration is actively undermining it,** proposing to make it harder for families to use these rebates and restricting how families can get these savings. I refuse to sit idly by as Donald Trump attacks clean, affordable American-made energy and drives up costs for New Mexicans. And I will continue to fight for lower costs and American energy independence. **Today, I’m asking for your help.** [**Friend, will you add your name to my efforts calling on the Department of Energy to restore this program?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134091502/630077280/1928956311?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260626_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0OTMzZWYyMC1hMjcxLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O4KngV1esWQlms3Q4wPAK855MZ6eNV0DdN9sE5_M4JE=&emci=4233ef20-a271-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=4933ef20-a271-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=252045) | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134091505/630077282/1928956311?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260626_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0OTMzZWYyMC1hMjcxLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=O4KngV1esWQlms3Q4wPAK855MZ6eNV0DdN9sE5_M4JE=&emci=4233ef20-a271-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=4933ef20-a271-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=252045)

clean_body: Washington should be helping people save money—not creating new obstacles. Under Trump, New Mexicans’ annual electricity bills are up 8% per family. When you work hard in America, that should mean something. At the very least, it should mean you aren’t forced to make tradeoffs between your health care, rent, and energy bills. But President Trump’s war on affordable, American-made energy and his massive tariff-taxes are making things worse, not better. Every hardworking person in New Mexico deserves stability and financial security. Period. I am fighting to bring costs down so this can be a reality. One of the ways we can do that is by helping homeowners and renters upgrade to modern, energy-efficient appliances that reduce monthly utility bills and make homes more comfortable year-round. That’s exactly what I intended when I created the federal home energy rebate program. My program helps families cover the upfront costs of buying efficient electric appliances and making home upgrades that will deliver years of savings. But now, the Trump administration is actively undermining it, proposing to make it harder for families to use these rebates and restricting how families can get these savings. I refuse to sit idly by as Donald Trump attacks clean, affordable American-made energy and drives up costs for New Mexicans. And I will continue to fight for lower costs and American energy independence. Today, I’m asking for your help. | Help send a clear message that New Mexico families deserve lower energy costs, more consumer choice, and policies that put working people first. name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: The President needs you today
body:
He stopped the housing bill cold. Now he needs us to back the veto.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/EYfBTp-C9PiZzjrusxNVJbt3Ix229pLDEC3XQXJPcps=452)Patriot–On Wednesday, President Trump was supposed to walk into the Capitol and sign a housing bill. He did not. Two hours before the ceremony, he canceled it.Here is what he said:
> _Today's Housing News Conference and Signing is hereby cancelled until such time as we pass the desperately needed SAVE AMERICA ACT, which I consider to be a National Emergency._
I want you to understand exactly what just happened. The President refused to sign a bill that both parties wanted, and he did it to force Washington to finally act on election integrity.The SAVE America Act is simple. Prove you are a citizen before you register to vote. Show a photo ID when you cast your ballot. The House has passed it. The Senate has buried it.The President just used his leverage to drag it back into the light.Here is the part that matters. A veto sends this bill back to Congress and forces another vote. This time, every member knows exactly where the President stands. That is how you move a stuck Senate. Now he needs us behind him.**Here is what I need you to do today:**
1. Call the White House at **202-456-1111** or message them at [_**whitehouse.gov/contact**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.whitehouse.gov%2Fcontact%2F/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/HPljYzbrAbRGvf56JEQHLgzEnUc807GaF2VdHSNXSis=452). Tell them: _"President Trump, please veto the housing bill and send it back to Congress. Do not sign it until they pass the SAVE America Act and protect our elections."_
2. Post on social media and tag the President. Tell him publicly to veto it.
* Truth Social: [_**@realDonaldTrump**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftruthsocial.com%2F@realDonaldTrump/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/eaRY5cdJ3DDI4ieonLysxgWvtlLnbx8UQrckPKumOcQ=452)
* X: [_**@realDonaldTrump**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fx.com%2FrealDonaldTrump/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/fpVZ85G3jRrOqJOUbq5N--kEgaKqVs6q_-qaqtlflQE=452), [_**@POTUS**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fx.com%2FPOTUS/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/BOWiL_esndBsgC0qfd0aon9krZxD4wFNyYhOsgRT0Lk=452), [_**@WhiteHouse**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fx.com%2FWhiteHouse/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/NaP9rfUse709OY3uOa98YxolqH-9-XzyduW7M-wLXJA=452)
* Facebook: [_**@DonaldTrump**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2FDonaldTrump/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/vxNkfCHB-rdeZGb21X69texMrGi3j_xGViRynRoo1Ag=452)
* Instagram: [_**@realdonaldtrump**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Frealdonaldtrump/1/0100019f05c81074-ef1fcdfc-e766-44d2-b86e-b280a1cc68c2-000000/_3SlS3sAyn0gJs5pTFDYLRSN6uqLe3idr6aTCvbsL14=452)

This is how grassroots pressure works. Not one call. Not one post. Thousands of us, at the same time, refusing to let Washington look away.The President drew the line last week. Let's give him the backing to veto this bill and finish the job.In liberty,Jenny Beth Martin

The GOP is out here talking about gutting Social Security – so there's a lot at stake.

---
Hardworking people in Pennsylvania and across this country have paid into Social Security their entire lives.
They've earned this benefit, so it's only right they see those checks come through after they retire – it's their money!
The current administration is already throwing things into chaos by closing Social Security Administration offices, cutting staff, and making it harder for seniors to get help over the phone.

John

After Chris and Karen Harrington learned Clinton lacks a local food sovereignty ordinance, they began gathering signatures to force a special town meeting. Their plan is to give away sourdough and baked goods, collect donations for local causes and keep the farm stand alive while pushing the town to protect other small farms from state interference.

Hello Peter,
We have just finished our second week of town halls - visiting and holding events in 7 of the 8 counties in District 13. (Don’t worry, Johnston County ...we’ll be there in just a few days!) It was great to see so many folks across the district.
All this driving has meant I have had to stop to refuel a lot! While gas prices seem to be coming down, that’s not enough to ease the financial pressures everyone is feeling right now.
I’ve heard it across the district - from neighbors and friends old and new - that prices across the board are out of hand, and that we need representation focused on taking the right steps to lower those costs. It’s not just gas and groceries; it's housing, it’s healthcare, and all the small parts of life that add up to one huge financial burden on families across the nation.
It’s about time we start working to change that. Fixing our country will require doing what we can to ensure people show up, make their voices heard, and choose new representation – and to do that, I need your help. There is a huge campaign finance deadline in just a few days, and I’m relying on your grassroots support to make sure we stay on track and flip this seat.
Will you please make a contribution of any amount today to help us meet our goal and elect a representative who will fight for you, not the billionaires and corporate interests? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260626bdy]

| A Patriotic opening ceremony to kick off the Great American State Fair (a 16-day national exposition running June 25 - July 10, 2026, on the National Mall from the U.S. Capitol to the Washington Monument). It celebrated America's 250th birthday with showcases from all 56 states and territories.
Why You Should Visit the Great American State Fair:
The Great American State Fair on the National Mall (June 25-July 10, 2026) is a once-in-a-generation celebration of America's 250th birthday that brings the spirit of a classic state fair to the heart of our nation's capital. With pavilions from all 56 states and territories, visitors can taste regional foods, experience unique cultures, and discover what makes each corner of America special - all in one unforgettable location between the Capitol and the Washington Monument. Families will love the carnival rides (including a giant Ferris wheel), live music, rodeo shows, military tributes, daily themed programming, and hands-on exhibits celebrating innovation, history, agriculture, and American ingenuity. It's free to attend, packed with patriotism, and offers a joyful, unifying way to honor our shared heritage during this historic milestone. Whether you're a proud local, a tourist, or just love celebrating what makes America great, this is an event you don't want to miss!

| Valley Link
---
| |
---
I had breakfast with a wonderful constituent, Lorrane of Louisa County, where we discussed several topics but front and foremost for her was the proposed and highly unpopular Valley Link project. Even though I've been told this is not a federal issue, I've shared Valley Link concerns with Dominion and PJM in the district and in my D.C. office over the last few months. I asked them, can you bury the lines, they said no. I asked them, can you reroute the lines, they said very little room for change due to restrictions. I asked why does it go through Appomattox County, Buckingham County, Louisa County, and others instead of in a straight line from Campbell County to Culpepper County? On this question, I get a mixed bag of answers. Unfortunately, the General Assembly in Richmond gave SCC authority over energy lines and infrastructure in Virginia, but I've been told the Governor could stop this project if she wanted to. Your local board of supervisors has influence on projects like this as well. The good news is the project is in the planning stages so maybe something can be done. I think the answer is invest in small modular reactors at the location where you need the energy instead of massive power lines across people's personal property and across multiple counties.

| | Dear Friend,

**We did it!**
Because of your support, encouragement, and vote, I am honored to officially be the **Republican nominee for Comptroller of Maryland.**
**More than 134,000 Marylanders** placed their trust in our campaign. Thank you. This victory belongs to every volunteer, donor, supporter, and voter who believes Maryland deserves better.
But make no mistake—the real race begins now.
Over the next four months, we'll take our message to every corner of Maryland—from **every Shore to every Mountain, every Bay to every Beltway** and everywhere in between.
I'm not running because I wanted a career in politics. I'm running because Maryland deserves responsible financial leadership.
Our state faces a growing structural deficit, declining fiscal discipline, and the first credit rating downgrade in more than 50 years. The Comptroller must be an **independent watchdog** who protects taxpayer dollars, increases transparency, strengthens oversight, and tells Marylanders the truth.
**Now, I need you on our team.**
Whether you want to stay informed, volunteer, attend an event, or simply follow along as we travel across Maryland, I'd love to stay connected with you and help us build a movement for accountability - true accountability.
**Click below and join our campaign community today.**
[**JOIN THE TEAM**](https://votesonyadunn.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c4b8ca5ed46d57f82b50c73a6&id=9de542de7e&e=d8ca418081)
Together, we'll restore trust, protect taxpayers, and bring common-sense financial leadership back to Maryland.
**Let's get it Dunn!**

**Sonya Dunn**
Republican Nominee Comptroller of Maryland

body:
These are a big deal
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260626-2963)
Peter,
Big news: This week, our campaign just earned the endorsement of Our Revolution, one of the largest progressive grassroots organizations in the country.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260626.vSM0c2&refcode=em20260626-2963&t=1&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)
And that comes right after earning an endorsement from BLOC, one of Wisconsin’s most powerful organizations for year-round, multiracial, community-based organizing.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260626.vSM0c2&refcode=em20260626-2963&t=2&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)
True electability is about building a coalition broad enough, strong enough, and organized enough to win.
That means young people and seniors. Black, brown, Indigenous, AAPI, and white working-class communities. Rural towns, small cities, suburbs, and urban neighborhoods. Union members, renters, homeowners, students, parents, caregivers, service workers, educators, small business owners, and everyone who is tired of politics that protects the powerful while leaving the rest of us behind.
That is the coalition Fran is building.
Fran is running to make Wisconsin affordable for working families by taxing the rich, lowering property taxes, fully funding our public schools, delivering universal childcare, protecting workers, and taking on the corporate power driving up our bills.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260626.vSM0c2&refcode=em20260626-2963&t=3&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)
And now, with Our Revolution and BLOC standing with us, we have even more momentum.
But endorsements alone won’t win this race. People power will.
We need the resources to organize in every corner of Wisconsin, reach voters who are ready for something different, and build the grassroots campaign it will take to win.
**[Can you contribute $10, or whatever you can to help us win?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260626.vSM0c2&refcode=em20260626-2963&t=4&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)**
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260626.vSM0c2&amount=10&refcode=em20260626-2963&t=7&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)**
Thank you for being part of this,
Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260626-2963&t=8&refcode2=2963_105371_6e4sFl&akid=2963%2E105371%2E6e4sFl)**
---
Email us: [info@francescahong.com](mailto:info@francescahong.com)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is one of the most powerful tools that grassroots campaigns like ours have to reach everyday people across Wisconsin and beyond, so thank you for reading to the end.
The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.francescahong.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/)

# [Peace Abroad, War Next Door: Pakistani Airstrikes Devastate Afghan Civilians](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2510348&post_id=203717112&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAzNzE3MTEyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODI1MTE3NTgsImV4cCI6MTc4NTEwMzc1OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI1MTAzNDgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ILG7EenOeqFBgyIGVI-tfcKtYaKzfx2y_bsYJ9HEB80)
### While Pakistan presents itself as a mediator between Iran and the United States its attacks on Afghan civilians are ravaging border villages.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ae56cda0-dc6b-4599-8b04-cb2becafd535?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Funeral for civilian victims of Pakistani airstrikes held in Khost on June 11. Photo: Mohammad Zaman Nazari.
In the village of Mana, located in Afghanistan's Khost province, close to the Pakistani border, men who normally pass their days farming instead spent the morning of June 10 digging fresh graves for their murdered relatives and neighbors.
The night before, shortly after midnight, Pakistani drones and fighter jets flattened the neighboring homes of two brothers, Siraj and Babri. Nine members of a single family were killed, most of them women and children.
The two brothers' homes stood beside one another in Mana. Neighbors worked through the night dragging the dead and the wounded out of the debris. Across the two households, ten more people were wounded, several of them in critical condition. The survivors were rushed first to a small district hospital, before being transferred to the largest provincial hospital in Khost.
A doctor at the hospital, who asked not to be named because medical staff have been warned against speaking to journalists, told Drop Site that 11 bodies were brought in after the strike, including women, children, and men--every one of them a civilian. Among the wounded survivors were three children.
These are not isolated tragedies--they are the latest episodes in a campaign that Drop Site has been documenting along the border since the winter, one in which Pakistan, while presenting itself to Washington and Tehran as an indispensable peacemaker, has bombed Afghan villages, hospitals, schools and markets, emptied entire districts along the border, and blockaded roads until clinics ran out of medicine.
By the United Nations' own conservative count, Pakistani operations had already killed hundreds of Afghan civilians this year before the June 10 strikes. What plays in Islamabad's conference halls as "counterterrorism operations," appears, from Khost and Paktika, like indiscriminate punishment of Afghans living along the border demarcation line.
By April 1, the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) had verified at least 372 civilian deaths from Pakistani operations in Afghanistan, though the actual death toll in an area largely sealed off to independent monitors is likely higher.
The attack on Mana was not the only deadly incident in the region that night. Pakistani aircraft also struck a series of buildings in neighboring Paktika province. Taken together, the bombardment of Khost and Paktika killed or wounded at least 23 civilians in a matter of hours, locals said.
By the following morning in Mana the bodies had been washed, wrapped, and carried into the open for a mass funeral. At the ceremony, hundreds gathered under chants of "Allahu Akbar," as they prepared to bury the victims, the majority of whom were children and women.
The crowd was furious. Mourners called for international human rights organizations to open an impartial investigation into the killings and demanded that those responsible be brought to justice.
Noor Badshah Khan, a tribal elder from the area, addressed the crowd and blasted Pakistan for waging a merciless campaign against ordinary Afghans.
"When will these crimes stop? When will they stop slaughtering the children of this soil?" he asked.
The attack on Paktika killed three more children: 10-year-old Nazam Khan, his younger sister Khadeja, and their cousin Mozdalafa.
The three had spent the evening counting the stars and bickering over the number before they drifted off to sleep in the open air, family members told Drop Site.
The blast destroyed the house, killed the family's livestock, and hurled the children's father, Sher Mast, some 60 feet through the air. He and his wife survived the attack that killed their children, though both were badly wounded.
A neighbor who reached the wreckage within half an hour gathered what remained of the three children by torchlight. The next day they were lowered into three small graves dug side by side, the eldest boy's shroud still wet with blood.

## **The War After the War**
Along this stretch of border, the drones that fly overhead day and night have their own nickname. Villagers call them "bangana," the Pashto word for a buzzing wasp. For the children of Khost and Paktika, that sound is now woven into their daily lives.
War has become a tragic constant of life in the region. The same valleys were bombed during the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan during the 1980s, and again during the two-decade long U.S.-led war and occupation. Now, the hostile aircraft overhead are operated by a Pakistani regime that enjoys close ties with Washington.
The drones inflict a particular type of psychological torment on residents of the region. Locals describe a feeling of helplessness--they can hear the machines, but never reach them, and their own government has no capacity to to stop them.
The grief inflicted by the recent attacks in Khost and Paktika has eroded long-standing cultural traditions in the area. By custom, after a death, neighbors cook for a bereaved family for three days. This time, villagers said, no one could bring themselves to eat after the massacres.
Without a responsive government, or the attention of international media, many Afghans have turned to social media in a desperate attempt to inform the world of their plight and demand accountability.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe6345c-73e9-45d1-b018-eaf096862400?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Afghans in Khost prepare to bury victims of Pakistani strikes on June 10. Photo: Mohammad Zaman Nazari.
In the hours after the strikes, Afghans filled online platforms with appeals to the United Nations and the international community to hold the Pakistani military to account, describing the bombardment as a direct assault on Afghanistan's national sovereignty.
While Pakistan has justified its attacks as a response to terrorist attacks on its soil blamed on the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), locals say that the justifications are an attempt to mask the real motives for the ongoing attacks on a border zone that has long been disputed between the two countries.
"This is indeed a continuation of the War on Terror in Afghanistan," said Mohammad Zaher, a local from Khost. "It was clear that it would not stop after the first drones reappeared after the U.S. withdrawal."
## **" Precise and Calibrated"**
Islamabad tells a different story about its attacks. Pakistan's information minister, Attaullah Tarar, [described the operation](https://substack.com/redirect/1ec796d8-f349-4264-9cad-b250a4e08aa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as "precise and calibrated," claiming the Air Force had destroyed four militant targets and killed 26 TTP fighters. The gulf between the reported casualty figures, with Kabul recording 13 civilian dead, and Pakistan claims that double that number were killed, all terrorists, has by now become a familiar feature of the information war that accompanies the armed conflict.
Residents from the region who spoke to Drop Site rejected the Pakistani account of the strikes, stating that none of the victims had any ties to armed groups.
Pakistan's escalating attacks on its neighbor come as the country is embracing a new international identity as a peacemaker mediating the war between Iran and the United States. Field Marshall Asim Munir, the Pakistani military's chief of staff, has emerged as a close ally of President Donald Trump, who has praised Munir as an "exceptional human being," while ignoring his brutal crackdowns on dissent inside Pakistan, as well as his escalating killings of Afghan civilians.
Trump's praise for Munir as a mediator stands in stark contrast to the brutal reality of Pakistan's military campaign against its neighbor.
Islamabad declared "open war" on the Afghan Taliban government in February after a suicide attack on a Shia mosque in Islamabad blamed on the TTP. Since that time, Pakistani airstrikes have shifted from rural areas on the border to attacks on Kabul itself, including the [bombing](https://substack.com/redirect/0da83c66-50b6-442d-b82a-c77f5f10b12a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a rehabilitation clinic in the heart of the capital that killed hundreds in March.
Residents described the attacks on roads and local transport infrastructure as a de facto siege--depriving markets and clinics of basic goods like flour and medicine. Locals from the region told Drop Site they believed the aim of Pakistani operations was to depopulate the frontier and carve out a buffer zone, with the terror wrought by the recent bombings in Khost and Paktika helping achieve the same goal by encouraging flight from the area.
While the newest phase of the war between the two neighbors has been justified as a counterterrorism operation, Afghans note that Pakistani animosity towards Kabul has continued across many different regimes over the decades--with nationalist, communist, democratic, and Islamist governments all targeted by Islamabad in a bid to ensure that its neighbor remains too weak and unstable to assert its own territorial claims.
"This is an endless cycle and you don't need any educated analyst, military expert or historian to understand it," said Ali Khan, a resident of Kabul and former soldier of the U.S.-backed Afghan army that collapsed in 2021. "You just need to talk to the people who have been affected by these policies for decades."
Pakistan's confrontation with Afghans is increasingly taking place on both sides of the border. After years of hosting a large refugee population, hundreds of thousands of Afghans have recently been deported from Pakistan back to Afghanistan--in many cases placing them back in the same border villages and provinces that are currently under attack by Pakistani drones and aircraft.
"Afghans are a population to be managed, leveraged, and disposed of, never quite people", said Ali Khan. Because of his own affiliation to the former army of the Afghan Republic, he himself fled to Pakistan, and then Iran during the last four years, before he ultimately returned home to Kabul earlier this year.
"It's better for me to hide in Kabul, see my family and live with some level of dignity instead of being beaten and deported by our neighboring countries," he said.
_Afghanistan-based journalists Fazelminallah Qazizai and Mohammad Zaman Nazari contributed to this report._

What plays in Islamabad's conference halls as "counterterrorism operations," appears, from Khost and Paktika, like indiscriminate punishment of Afghans living along the border demarcation line. By April 1, the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) had verified at least 372 civilian deaths from Pakistani operations in Afghanistan, though the actual death toll in an area largely sealed off to independent monitors is likely higher. The attack on Mana was not the only deadly incident in the region that night. Pakistani aircraft also struck a series of buildings in neighboring Paktika province. Taken together, the bombardment of Khost and Paktika killed or wounded at least 23 civilians in a matter of hours, locals said. By the following morning in Mana the bodies had been washed, wrapped, and carried into the open for a mass funeral. At the ceremony, hundreds gathered under chants of "Allahu Akbar," as they prepared to bury the victims, the majority of whom were children and women. The crowd was furious. Mourners called for international human rights organizations to open an impartial investigation into the killings and demanded that those responsible be brought to justice. Noor Badshah Khan, a tribal elder from the area, addressed the crowd and blasted Pakistan for waging a merciless campaign against ordinary Afghans. "When will these crimes stop? When will they stop slaughtering the children of this soil?" he asked. The attack on Paktika killed three more children: 10-year-old Nazam Khan, his younger sister Khadeja, and their cousin Mozdalafa. The three had spent the evening counting the stars and bickering over the number before they drifted off to sleep in the open air, family members told Drop Site. The blast destroyed the house, killed the family's livestock, and hurled the children's father, Sher Mast, some 60 feet through the air. He and his wife survived the attack that killed their children, though both were badly wounded. A neighbor who reached the wreckage within half an hour gathered what remained of the three children by torchlight. The next day they were lowered into three small graves dug side by side, the eldest boy's shroud still wet with blood. The War After the War Along this stretch of border, the drones that fly overhead day and night have their own nickname. Villagers call them "bangana," the Pashto word for a buzzing wasp. For the children of Khost and Paktika, that sound is now woven into their daily lives. War has become a tragic constant of life in the region. The same valleys were bombed during the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan during the 1980s, and again during the two-decade long U.S.-led war and occupation. Now, the hostile aircraft overhead are operated by a Pakistani regime that enjoys close ties with Washington. The drones inflict a particular type of psychological torment on residents of the region. Locals describe a feeling of helplessness--they can hear the machines, but never reach them, and their own government has no capacity to to stop them. The grief inflicted by the recent attacks in Khost and Paktika has eroded long-standing cultural traditions in the area. By custom, after a death, neighbors cook for a bereaved family for three days. This time, villagers said, no one could bring themselves to eat after the massacres. Without a responsive government, or the attention of international media, many Afghans have turned to social media in a desperate attempt to inform the world of their plight and demand accountability. | | ---|---|--- Afghans in Khost prepare to bury victims of Pakistani strikes on June 10. Photo: Mohammad Zaman Nazari. In the hours after the strikes, Afghans filled online platforms with appeals to the United Nations and the international community to hold the Pakistani military to account, describing the bombardment as a direct assault on Afghanistan's national sovereignty. While Pakistan has justified its attacks as a response to terrorist attacks on its soil blamed on the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), locals say that the justifications are an attempt to mask the real motives for the ongoing attacks on a border zone that has long been disputed between the two countries. "This is indeed a continuation of the War on Terror in Afghanistan," said Mohammad Zaher, a local from Khost. "It was clear that it would not stop after the first drones reappeared after the U.S. withdrawal." " Precise and Calibrated" Islamabad tells a different story about its attacks. Pakistan's information minister, Attaullah Tarar, as "precise and calibrated," claiming the Air Force had destroyed four militant targets and killed 26 TTP fighters. The gulf between the reported casualty figures, with Kabul recording 13 civilian dead, and Pakistan claims that double that number were killed, all terrorists, has by now become a familiar feature of the information war that accompanies the armed conflict. Residents from the region who spoke to Drop Site rejected the Pakistani account of the strikes, stating that none of the victims had any ties to armed groups. Pakistan's escalating attacks on its neighbor come as the country is embracing a new international identity as a peacemaker mediating the war between Iran and the United States. Field Marshall Asim Munir, the Pakistani military's chief of staff, has emerged as a close ally of President Donald Trump, who has praised Munir as an "exceptional human being," while ignoring his brutal crackdowns on dissent inside Pakistan, as well as his escalating killings of Afghan civilians. Trump's praise for Munir as a mediator stands in stark contrast to the brutal reality of Pakistan's military campaign against its neighbor. Islamabad declared "open war" on the Afghan Taliban government in February after a suicide attack on a Shia mosque in Islamabad blamed on the TTP. Since that time, Pakistani airstrikes have shifted from rural areas on the border to attacks on Kabul itself, including the of a rehabilitation clinic in the heart of the capital that killed hundreds in March. Residents described the attacks on roads and local transport infrastructure as a de facto siege--depriving markets and clinics of basic goods like flour and medicine. Locals from the region told Drop Site they believed the aim of Pakistani operations was to depopulate the frontier and carve out a buffer zone, with the terror wrought by the recent bombings in Khost and Paktika helping achieve the same goal by encouraging flight from the area. While the newest phase of the war between the two neighbors has been justified as a counterterrorism operation, Afghans note that Pakistani animosity towards Kabul has continued across many different regimes over the decades--with nationalist, communist, democratic, and Islamist governments all targeted by Islamabad in a bid to ensure that its neighbor remains too weak and unstable to assert its own territorial claims. "This is an endless cycle and you don't need any educated analyst, military expert or historian to understand it," said Ali Khan, a resident of Kabul and former soldier of the U.S.-backed Afghan army that collapsed in 2021. "You just need to talk to the people who have been affected by these policies for decades." Pakistan's confrontation with Afghans is increasingly taking place on both sides of the border. After years of hosting a large refugee population, hundreds of thousands of Afghans have recently been deported from Pakistan back to Afghanistan--in many cases placing them back in the same border villages and provinces that are currently under attack by Pakistani drones and aircraft. "Afghans are a population to be managed, leveraged, and disposed of, never quite people", said Ali Khan. Because of his own affiliation to the former army of the Afghan Republic, he himself fled to Pakistan, and then Iran during the last four years, before he ultimately returned home to Kabul earlier this year. "It's better for me to hide in Kabul, see my family and live with some level of dignity instead of being beaten and deported by our neighboring countries," he said. DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin **[fired right back at crazed Democrat Rosa DeLauro](https://substack.com/redirect/aa7c8eb9-80d0-4dcb-b69c-abcc8c2ee25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after she screamed in his face, telling her to stop lying about President Trump's immigration enforcement and calling her out for neglecting to acknowledge the 450,000 children who went missing crossing Biden's open border.

A proposed **[one-time 5% emergency tax on Californians with assets exceeding $1 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6f62d3-a8d0-42b0-8800-8c8540988641?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has been officially added to the state's November ballot, despite strong opposition from Governor Gavin Newsom. The measure, backed by the Service Employees International Union and endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, aims to fund healthcare, education, and food assistance programs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6f62d3-a8d0-42b0-8800-8c8540988641?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

The state has already lost prominent figures including Elon Musk, Larry Page, and Larry Ellison. Newsom instead called for a federal billionaire tax, arguing wealth inequality should be addressed nationally rather than state by state.
* **Critics accuse Newsom of opposing the measure to protect potential 2028 presidential donors.** Supporters counter that public opinion favors the tax and that opposing it prioritizes billionaires over millions of Californians facing medical bankruptcy.

It’s Lauren Underwood, Congresswoman for Illinois’ 14th Congressional District and Red-to-Blue co-chair.
I know what’s coming.
Between now and Election Day, Republicans are going to flood the zone. They’re going to throw everything they have at us — distractions, attacks, misinformation — and hope that we get overwhelmed and shut down.
It’s a strategy. And it works — if we let it.
I’ve been in Congress long enough to know that the moments when it feels hardest to fight are exactly the moments when fighting matters most. When the noise is loudest, when the stakes feel impossibly high, when it would be so easy to freeze.
We cannot freeze.
Our democracy — the health care families depend on, the schools our kids attend, the rights we’ve fought for — is on the line. And the only way we protect it is by staying in the fight, even when it’s hard.
That’s what I’m doing every day in Congress. And I need you with me.
Will you split a contribution between Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign today and help make sure we don’t back down? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/underwoodrrr]

In the waning months before the 2020 presidential election, the Biden-Harris regime and its cheerleaders in the media breathlessly hyped a sensational “domestic terrorism” plot: a ragtag group of disgruntled Michigan militia types allegedly scheming to kidnap Democratic Governor Gretchen Whitmer from her vacation home, blow up a bridge, and spark chaos. The FBI swooped in with fanfare on October 8, 2020, arresting 13 men and touting it as a major victory against right-wing extremism. Bill and Mike Null, and Eric Molitor were all found “Not Guilty” of material support to terrorism in Michigan state court. Now they tell their story.

name: Voto Latino
subject: Here’s what VL On-Campus student leaders accomplished in the spring semester
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
This past spring semester, our student leaders truly stepped up to lead the charge.
#
Peter,
Young Latino voters will shape the future of this country — but only if we meet them where they are and help them feel comfortable and prepared to participate.
That’s why we launched VL On-Campus. Through this year-round initiative, we partner with student-led organizations and Latino Greek life nationwide to drive peer-to-peer conversations, register voters, and build lasting civic power right where community is already strongest.
This past spring semester, our student leaders truly stepped up to lead the charge. Here are just a few incredible highlights from campus:
**George Mason University**
**The Hispanic Latine Leadership Alliance** contacted 20,000 voters ahead of Virginia’s April 21 redistricting election. Students held a nonpartisan GOTV text bank, sending **20,000 texts across the Commonwealth of Virginia** , urging voters to make a plan to vote.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260626-1._JzkBo&amount=3&%3Brefcode=em20260626-313&t=1&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)
**University of Michigan**
**The Beta Omicron Chapter of Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Inc. engaged students ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.** The sisters invited students on campus to learn about the issues impacting Latinos, register to vote, and paint "affirmation jars" to remind one another of their collective power.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260626-1._JzkBo&amount=3&%3Brefcode=em20260626-313&t=2&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)
**Duke University**
We are incredibly proud to highlight **Sofia Cava, a recent public policy graduate from Duke University.** Throughout all four years of college, Sofia was active in Beyond Borders, an immigrant rights organization, working to expand its reach. When VL On-Campus created a chapter at Duke, the organization held multiple voter registration drives. Sofia shared with us that the lessons she learned inspired her to continue contributing to her community, noting, _"Let’s always remember how we got here and build a career that helps our communities."_
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260626-1._JzkBo&amount=3&%3Bamp%3Brefcode=em20260626-313&t=3&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)
Despite systemic attacks on the Latino community, _**our students persevered.** _Which is why we have endless gratitude for our VL On-Campus leaders who created safer spaces for youth to gather, engage in conversations about the issues that impact us, and register youth to vote.
Sustained voter registration and engagement require real resources. We do this by showing up consistently, keeping students engaged, and reaching newly eligible voters to ensure they turn out in important elections.
**[So, will you chip in today to power VL On-Campus and help us continue to reach young Latino voters from now through November?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260626-1._JzkBo&amount=3&refcode=em20260626-313&t=4&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)**
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260626-1._JzkBo&amount=3&refcode=20260626-313&t=23&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)**
Thank you for supporting these student leaders and helping engage young voters on campuses across the nation.
Voto Latino

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-voto-footer?refcode=em20260626-313-&t=24&refcode2=313_1366028_lyk3G4&akid=313%2E1366028%2Elyk3G4)**
---
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) secured $4 million in road funding through the Fiscal Year 2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act, directing federal dollars to the gateway connecting Interstate 65 to Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base. Britt, who chairs the Subcommittee on Homeland Security Appropriations, said the money will support the Maxwell Capital Gateway Project, the primary route serving thousands of military personnel, civilian employees, students, contractors, and visitors at the base. The funding targets roadway and bridge improvements to Washington Ferry Road from US-31 to the rear access gate at Maxwell.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.), Chair of the Subcommittee on Homeland Security Appropriations, recently directly secured $1.25 million for the City of Atmore in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act. This funding will support the repair and improvement of Atmore’s storm drainage system. In total, Senator Britt directly secured more than $14.97 million for Alabama in FY26 Homeland Security appropriations funding. “I’m proud to deliver $1.25 million in funding for the City of Atmore to upgrade its stormwater infrastructure,” said Senator Britt. “As a member of the Appropriations Committee, I’m committed to returning taxpayer dollars right back to our communities. This critical funding will address longstanding drainage issues, reduce flooding risks, and better protect homes, businesses, and public safety. I’m eager to see the lasting impact this project will have in strengthening Atmore’s resilience for years to come.

body:
| | | |
---
**Boysko Bulletin: Hearing the Concerns that Working Families Have Expressed, Our General Assembly Passed a State Budget That Offers Financial Relief for Virginians**
---
Dear Peter, On Monday, the General Assembly passed a fiscally responsible balanced biennial budget. We await the Governor’s action - she can sign it as-is, recommend changes or veto line items. The General Assembly returns to Richmond next Monday to vote on her actions. This budget affords Virginians immediate financial relief including an increase in childcare funding, an increase in the state tax personal deductions, and funding to subsidize healthcare exchange premiums on the Virginia exchange. The voters asked us to hear the concerns of working families who are struggling and we listened. Among the budget items which I am most proud of is a 4% raise for teachers for each of the two years of the biennial budget, funds to cover SNAP nutrition benefits that the federal government cut, and the subsidies for healthcare exchange premiums. As passed by the General Assembly, here are a few of the items the budget will provide.
* Help schools better meet the needs of students by investing $148 million to more than double the flexible add-on for students with disabilities and $29 million for K-12 students from low-income families
* Provide the state share of 4% raises each year for teachers and school staff ($388 million above the former Governor’s introduced budget) and 3.5% raises each year for state employees and state-supported local employees ($311 million above the introduced budget proposal)
* Help lower ACA health insurance premiums in 2027 for people with low and moderate incomes (138% to 250% of the poverty line) by investing $150 million.
* Support access to care by investing $15 million in free clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers to address increased demand
* Preserve access to care during pregnancy by restoring FAMIS prenatal funding
* Protect access to food assistance by providing $135 million to cover federal cuts and $3 million for work supports for people subject to new SNAP and Medicaid work reporting requirements
* Help Virginia respond to federal funding uncertainty and changing Medicaid estimates, reduce future state health care costs, and monitor environmental conditions through $969 million in one-time spending, while investing an additional $577 million in general fund money for capital projects
* Cutting taxes by increasing the standard deduction by nearly $500 per person to $9,200 for single filers and $18,400 for joint filers
* Establishing Virginia’s Paid Family and Medical Leave insurance program to expand access to paid leave for nearly 3.5 million Virginians
* Boosting housing development through increased investments in the Virginia Housing Trust Fund
* Expanding access to affordable childcare, including the creation of a new Employee Child Care Assistance Program to help working parents gain access to quality care

Many of you have written to me with concerns regarding our data centers. I’ve also heard from our environmental advocates that the budget does not go far enough to address the impacts of data centers on our communities. Ensuring that data centers pay their fair share of taxes and do not impact our communities negatively is important. The budget passed by the General Assembly calls for a fee on data centers based on their energy consumption, which is expected to generate a maximum of $600 million each year. It does not include the Senate’s proposal to end the sales tax exemption. This is just the start - the budget also includes a data center study. The Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy shall study the data center sales and use tax exemption and other data center impacts during the 2026 interim. The Joint Subcommittee shall meet at least two times with the following goals and objectives: (i) reviewing Virginia's data center sales and use tax exemption; (ii) examining the impact of the existing and any potential future exemption or incentives; (iii) approaches taken in other states related to the data center industry including tax preferences, incentives, environmental standards and mitigation, moratoriums on incentives or location of new facilities, and sustainable development requirements; (iv) reviewing methods related to data center investment in nonurbanized areas of the Commonwealth; (v) reviewing the recommendations and options in the 2024 JLARC study on Data Centers in Virginia; (vi) reviewing the estimated direct and indirect economic benefits of data center investment in Virginia; (vii) reviewing the direct or indirect impacts on the environment and quality of life related to data center location and siting; (viii) evaluating the impact of Artificial Intelligence on employment; (ix) reviewing the State Corporation Commission reported data on electric service agreements, water usage, permitted generators; and (x) recommended mechanisms to provide direct revenue to the state from the data center industry. The Joint Subcommittee shall report recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2026. You are invited to join Delegate Sullivan and me for a Town Hall to present commendations and memorial resolutions at the McLean Community Center on June 30 at 6:30 pm.
---
---
I hope that you are enjoying your summer. Happy Fourth of July! Kindest regards,
---
---
Jennifer B. Property owners can register their security cameras for free with Connect Fairfax County. Once registered, the FCPD will be aware of the camera’s location. In the event of a crime or suspicious activity in your area, FCPD may contact you to see if your camera contains relevant footage. clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin: Hearing the Concerns that Working Families Have Expressed, Our General Assembly Passed a State Budget That Offers Financial Relief for Virginians Dear Peter, On Monday, the General Assembly passed a fiscally responsible balanced biennial budget. We await the Governor’s action - she can sign it as-is, recommend changes or veto line items. The General Assembly returns to Richmond next Monday to vote on her actions. This budget affords Virginians immediate financial relief including an increase in childcare funding, an increase in the state tax personal deductions, and funding to subsidize healthcare exchange premiums on the Virginia exchange. The voters asked us to hear the concerns of working families who are struggling and we listened. Among the budget items which I am most proud of is a 4% raise for teachers for each of the two years of the biennial budget, funds to cover SNAP nutrition benefits that the federal government cut, and the subsidies for healthcare exchange premiums. As passed by the General Assembly, here are a few of the items the budget will provide. Help schools better meet the needs of students by investing $148 million to more than double the flexible add-on for students with disabilities and $29 million for K-12 students from low-income families Provide the state share of 4% raises each year for teachers and school staff ($388 million above the former Governor’s introduced budget) and 3.5% raises each year for state employees and state-supported local employees ($311 million above the introduced budget proposal) Help lower ACA health insurance premiums in 2027 for people with low and moderate incomes (138% to 250% of the poverty line) by investing $150 million. Support access to care by investing $15 million in free clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers to address increased demand Preserve access to care during pregnancy by restoring FAMIS prenatal funding Protect access to food assistance by providing $135 million to cover federal cuts and $3 million for work supports for people subject to new SNAP and Medicaid work reporting requirements Help Virginia respond to federal funding uncertainty and changing Medicaid estimates, reduce future state health care costs, and monitor environmental conditions through $969 million in one-time spending, while investing an additional $577 million in general fund money for capital projects Cutting taxes by increasing the standard deduction by nearly $500 per person to $9,200 for single filers and $18,400 for joint filers Establishing Virginia’s Paid Family and Medical Leave insurance program to expand access to paid leave for nearly 3.5 million Virginians Boosting housing development through increased investments in the Virginia Housing Trust Fund Expanding access to affordable childcare, including the creation of a new Employee Child Care Assistance Program to help working parents gain access to quality care Many of you have written to me with concerns regarding our data centers. I’ve also heard from our environmental advocates that the budget does not go far enough to address the impacts of data centers on our communities. Ensuring that data centers pay their fair share of taxes and do not impact our communities negatively is important. The budget passed by the General Assembly calls for a fee on data centers based on their energy consumption, which is expected to generate a maximum of $600 million each year. It does not include the Senate’s proposal to end the sales tax exemption. This is just the start - the budget also includes a data center study. The Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy shall study the data center sales and use tax exemption and other data center impacts during the 2026 interim. The Joint Subcommittee shall meet at least two times with the following goals and objectives: (i) reviewing Virginia's data center sales and use tax exemption; (ii) examining the impact of the existing and any potential future exemption or incentives; (iii) approaches taken in other states related to the data center industry including tax preferences, incentives, environmental standards and mitigation, moratoriums on incentives or location of new facilities, and sustainable development requirements; (iv) reviewing methods related to data center investment in nonurbanized areas of the Commonwealth; (v) reviewing the recommendations and options in the 2024 JLARC study on Data Centers in Virginia; (vi) reviewing the estimated direct and indirect economic benefits of data center investment in Virginia; (vii) reviewing the direct or indirect impacts on the environment and quality of life related to data center location and siting; (viii) evaluating the impact of Artificial Intelligence on employment; (ix) reviewing the State Corporation Commission reported data on electric service agreements, water usage, permitted generators; and (x) recommended mechanisms to provide direct revenue to the state from the data center industry. The Joint Subcommittee shall report recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2026. Property owners can register their security cameras for free with Connect Fairfax County. Once registered, the FCPD will be aware of the camera’s location. name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: Why we're not in Corpus Christi
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240920%2E444211%2EtcAMPe)
The Texas Democratic Convention is taking place this week and we wish everyone there good luck and good times!
We’re excited for all the great work Democrats are doing, excited for what we know are going to be great speeches by the candidates. But we’re skipping the convention this year. There’s important work for us to do across Texas right now.
Just over this past week Powered by People volunteers added over 800 new voters to our network (registering 247 of them to vote). We’ve held 45 voter registration events across 19 cities at concerts, during student orientations, at pride events, Juneteenth events, ice cream shops, and more. We also activated 267 volunteers across the state who are personally following up with each new voter we add to our network.
I spent yesterday with our volunteers at El Paso Community College, talking with, registering and committing to staying in touch with the new voters who will make the difference in November. It was great to actually talk with -- and listen to -- young people who hold the outcome of this election in their hands. Even better to get them registered and make a personal connection that I can follow up on over the next 4 months.
In addition to EPCC this week we are on Texas Southern University’s campus engaging students at freshman orientation. Also at University of Houston Downtown, registering incoming students at freshman orientation this Saturday... catching UT San Antonio students during summer school... and we'll be at San Antonio’s Pride Festival, El Paso’s Sun City Pride, and Houston's Sober & Proud Zero-Proof Pub Crawl and Pride Happy Hour at Play in Houston as well.
Y ademas... We'll be at Axelrad in Houston for Cumbia Libre night, Emerald City Dispensary + Lounge in Fort Worth, and Amy’s Ice Cream at the Arboretum in Austin... Resilient Mini Flea Market in Houston and supporting an event with Revival Run Club... and lots more.
Best wishes to all our friends at the state convention, we’ll be missing you! But know that we’re excited to join you in supporting James, Gina and the amazing people running alongside them. And the best way we can think of doing that is being out there right now, reaching, registering and turning out the margin of victory in November.
[**Please consider donating to keep our volunteers in the field with the voters who are the key to making James Talarico the next Senator and Gina Hinojosa the next Governor of the great state of Texas!**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260626.15qM52&refcode=ema20260626-240920&t=3&akid=240920%2E444211%2EtcAMPe)
Beto

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

data centers, giving them a free pass to spew toxic pollution that causes
