Maine's Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Graham Platner staged a press event in Portland Thursday to accuse Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins of profiting from her office.
Platner's allegation was based on a bizarre leftist conspiracy theory that claims Collins funneled money to her husband's consulting firm with a piece of legislation that passed the Senate unanimously five years before Collins was married.
Platner's allegations of corruption drew a sharp response from Sen. Collins' campaign.
"Today, a man I have never met held a press conference and accused me of criminal conduct," Collins said on X.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..3k5xh8_0SA3ztQpG6nN8Qu9wDjs9Udr6gCNYa2KtA-w?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203720867)
"That is outrageous and false," she said. "If Graham Platner wants to debate policy, I look forward to that conversation. But making reckless and defamatory accusations because you cannot defend your own record is beneath the people of Maine."
Like any EdgeLord shitposter, Platner was giddy to have elicited a response from Collins. So he jumped on X to double-down on his allegations that Collins has committed crimes (while simultaneously denying that he was alleging she's engaged in criminal conduct).
"She got incredibly wealthy, funneling taxpayer money to her husband & profiting off stock trading while in office (violating the STOCK Act 25 times)," he said. "In a reasonable society, that would be criminal."
For the first-ever Robinson Report Fact-Check, I rate Graham Platner's claim Four Portapotties on the Platner Lie-o-Meter.
Subscribe to The Robinson Report for future Portapottie Reports on the Platner v. Collins campaign...
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..3k5xh8_0SA3ztQpG6nN8Qu9wDjs9Udr6gCNYa2KtA-w?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=203720867)
##### So let's dig into Platner's allegation that Collins has used her office to self-enrich
Every U.S. Senator has to file financial disclosures that allow the public to get a basic picture of their net worth, their assets, their liabilities, and, nowadays, their stock trading activity (or the activity of their family members). Collins was elected to the U.S. Senate in 1997, but the first financial disclosures available online date to 2012 and cover the financial year beginning in 2011. This was just before she married her husband.
In that first financial disclosure, Collins disclosed assets of $110,005 to $300,000 and liabilities of $365,003 to $800,000. In other words, after two full terms in the U.S. Senate, Collins showed a negative net worth of between -$689,995 and -$65,003. Not exactly the portfolio of someone who has leveraged their office in Washington, D.C., to pad their bank account.
_(Note: Congressional financial disclosures require members to disclose dollar value ranges for assets and liabilities, so any analysis of congressional net worth is necessarily a minimum/maximum assessment.)_
The details of Collins' 2012 disclosed assets are even more boring, almost raising the question of why she wasn't taking a little more risk with bets on tech start-ups or blue-chip technology companies. She reported between $15,000 and $50,000 saved in a deferred compensation plan, a Fidelity IRA, a U.S. FCU savings account, and a Bangor Savings Bank account. Collins, then 59, reported an additional $50,000 to $100,000 in a separate Fidelity Asset Manager IRA. On the liabilities side, Collins reported two mortgages -- her home in Maine and another house (likely in the D.C. area) -- as well as a home equity line of credit.
That's it. If there's any mystery or intrigue around Collins' financial disclosure, the question is why she was one of the poorest member of Congress. Here are the images of the oldest available disclosure for Collins.
Susan Collins 2012 Financial Disclosure (Source: US Senate Clerk)
However...
After 2012, Collins' financial life rockets into the multi-millionaire stratosphere, a sure sign that she'd started trading stocks like the Wolf of Wall Street or, even worse, Nancy Pelosi and Ro Khanna... right? Right?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c98797a-52c1-4cfb-86ab-06b2f6918f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Well, no.
To understand this sudden spike in Collins' net worth, you have to hop in the news archive time machine and travel back to 2012-2013 -- the same time period in which Graham Platner wrote on Reddit, "Luttrell didn't write the damn book, it was ghost written by a limey, and is war porn at its worst," in reference to the story of Navy Cross and Purple Heart recipient Marcus Luttrell, the U.S. Navy SEAL who inspired the hit movie _Lone Survivor_.
Back to Collins: In 2012, she married Thomas A. Daffron at a small ceremony in her hometown of Caribou. (My invite must have gotten lost in the mail...) Prior to marrying Collins, Daffron had a diverse and lucrative career. He'd worked as chief of staff to several prominent senators, including former Defense Secretary William S. Cohen, and he'd served as the vice president and chief operating officer for the Baltimore Orioles. In 2006, he joined Jefferson Consulting Group, where he worked until 2016.
Under U.S. Senate rules, members are required to include their spouses in their financial disclosures. The jump in net worth visible on Collins' financial disclosures is almost entirely assets and income that Daffron brought to the marriage. (No word on whether he asked for a pre-nup.) Unlike Collins, Daffron's disclosed finances show a man with a little more interest in taking risks and making savvy investments. In the 2013 disclosure, Collins reports basically the same asset and liability profile, along with a joint checking account ($50,000-$100,000) and a joint savings account ($15,000-$50,000). Every other asset and income stream on Collins' disclosure -- every single one -- is reported as belonging to "Spouse," a.k.a. Daffron.
Well... not every source of income. Collins did report receiving a grill, dishes and silverware, a painting, a vase, and a picnic basket -- all as wedding gifts and all with values reported under $700. You can find the whole 2013 financial disclosure here:
| Susan Collins 2013 Report4.27MB ∙ PDF file
---|---
| [Download](https://substack.com/redirect/b9553232-d736-4c8e-8cd9-0b9b5e44ade1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
As anyone can see from the 2013 disclosure, Mr. Susan Collins came to the marriage with a high net worth and a diverse array of investments, including some five-to-six-figure investments in popular ETFs and mutual funds. His reported net worth is anywhere from $1.2 million to $5.3 million -- and that doesn't include his annual income from his full-time job. When it comes to individual stocks, Daffron held modest ($1,000-$15,000) positions in dozens of popular publicly traded companies, including Chevron, Comcast, ConocoPhillips, DuPont, GE, General Mills, Heinz, Intel, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Amazon, Apple, and Google.
Now, you can hardly expect a communist to have a sophisticated understanding of high finance. Especially when their retirement strategy is designed around collecting a full military disability while waiting for Dad to die so you can inherit all the money Granddad made selling chairs. Compound interest, EBITDA, and the New York Stock Exchange might be a little hard for an "oysterman" like Graham Platner to wrap his brain around. But since 2012, the value of shares in those companies, especially the technology giants, has increased significantly. The appreciation of those stock prices, along with Daffron continuing to invest money in what appears to be the same way he'd been investing pre-2012, explains Collins' entire increase in net worth.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..3k5xh8_0SA3ztQpG6nN8Qu9wDjs9Udr6gCNYa2KtA-w?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203720867)
To suggest Collins has corruptly profited from congressional insider trading, as Platner did Thursday, also elides her role in co-authoring the STOCK Act, which enhanced disclosures around congressional stock trading and prohibited certain kinds of trades. Indeed, it's only because of the STOCK Act provisions that Collins supported that politicians are now required to promptly disclose stock market transactions made by them or related parties, as opposed to disclosing them once per year. These disclosures allow websites like Unusual Whales to closely monitor, almost in real time, the stock portfolios of politicians. So thanks to legislation backed by Susan Collins, we can see that her and her husband's most recent year in the stock market has basically tracked the S&P 500 average. (The purple line is the Collins financial disclosure, while the tan line is the benchmark average.)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/daa1370b-4387-4440-b96e-65bcc1d940b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For comparison's sake, here's Nancy Pelosi's lifetime trading against the S&P500...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd27f39a-6500-46fc-8edb-ea1b8a74506c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Unusual Whales is also the website that [produced](https://substack.com/redirect/9ac16fd9-b7b5-4d6f-9613-1e9da9c533a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the 2024 congressional trading report that found the value of Collins' portfolio grew by 77.5 percent from Dec. 29, 2023, to Dec. 30, 2024 -- an eyebrow-raising number that beat not only the S&P 500 benchmark but also Nancy Pelosi! However, as Unusual Whales discloses, the methodology is based on a simple percentage change in portfolio valuation. It doesn't look at what individual stock performances may have driven the change. When you look at the individual stock performance, Collins' (a.k.a. Daffron's) strong performance is explained by the spectacular growth in valuations of large tech companies -- the kind of tech companies that any member of the public could invest in.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=203720867&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAzNzIwODY3LCJpYXQiOjE3ODI1MTM5NzEsImV4cCI6MTc4NTEwNTk3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.meOxjPu1tlyegJAp3Ieh5UKHL1vuSxklwk5d8BkbCRM)

For example, Daffron owned shares in Google, Amazon, and Apple, which saw their share prices climb by, respectively, +37.4%, +45.6%, and +31.6%. Similarly, Daffron owned Amphenol (+41.1%) and Raytheon (+40.2%). However, the real winning horse in the Collins-Daffron portfolio was NVIDIA, which has been an international stock market phenomenon, rising by 177.7% during the reporting period. However, the Unusual Whales data shows Daffron's last purchase of NVDA stock was Jan. 6, 2022. In other words, the Collins-Daffron stock portfolio is basically what you would expect from a reasonably intelligent dude who has been a working professional most of his life and invested his money wisely.
Which brings us to Graham Platner, a guy whose finances resemble those of a man who blew his U.S. military paycheck on drugs and hookers in Bangkok. In his speech Thursday, Platner made a series of insinuated allegations -- allegations that, if true, would amount to ethical violations or even crimes.
Here's a look at some pieces from El Platner's speech transcript:
_" We must pass the Collins rule. Senators should not be able to funnel money to their spouses."_
First of all, you would have to be a real idiot with zero understanding of how Congress runs to think that anyone in Washington, D.C., is going to call something "The Collins Rule" unless the rule is that you're not allowed to miss votes. But the important point is this: There is no evidence that Collins has funneled any money to Daffron.
_" We have anti-nepotism laws, which prohibits members from putting family members on their payroll, but it says nothing about a spouse's firm being enriched through winning contracts by agencies that that senator or congressperson oversees."_
Talk of nepotism is rich coming from a guy whose fake oyster business (it's a hobby) has disclosed just $5,000 in sales, all of which comes from his birthing parent. The same guy is just counting down the hours until dear old Dad kicks the bucket (the same dad who bought his house for him) and he can inherit the family fortune. But if you really want to talk about nepotism, how about Platner putting his wife on the campaign payroll despite her only job experience being as a live-in nanny in Camden (ask her how that ended...) and an alleged teacher.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60b98dd6-fcf0-4da1-a1bc-a80b272df9bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Platner's actual criticism, to the extent there is some truth within the speech his DSA comrades wrote for him, pertains to a bill Collins co-authored with ex-Sen. Joe Lieberman (I-Conn.) in 2007.
The so-called "Accountability in Government Contracting Act" aimed to make small firms more competitive when bidding for federal contracts. It also added some oversight provisions and made changes to the inspectors general offices. The bill passed the Senate unanimously. That is, two of the most moderate senators in U.S. history introduced the bill, and every single Democrat and every single Republican voted for it.
That's the true version of the bill. The Platner version of the bill is that Collins was so greedy that she introduced this bill and convinced every single senator to vote for it because she also could predict the future and predicted that one day she would be married to a man who would benefit from the bill. Seriously. That's Platner's claim. Platner is claiming that Collins only introduced this bill because it would benefit Jefferson Consulting Group, where her husband (five years into the future) worked.
The attack is so preposterous it could only have originated with someone who is, to borrow one of Platner's favorite phrases, retarded. And, of course, it did: the original claim came from [Salon](https://substack.com/redirect/8a203552-9347-487f-8682-321a7e077967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but it's been regurgitated by Platnerista groupies like [Maine AFL-CIO leader Andy O'Brien](https://substack.com/redirect/7f3c2b99-c744-4750-85cb-7bdfe373de86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There's never been any evidence to suggest that Collins played any role whatsoever in directing contracts to the Jefferson Consulting Group. Moreover, while Daffron was working at Jefferson, Collins' income disclosures show a more or less stable growth in net worth -- not some massive spike in income or assets.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..qEtEUoAiMIuMz-O98lu-PoowIp5Nd8AiVNgjiAd10k8?)
##### If Susan Collins can see into the future, as Graham Platner seems to believe, then you'd think her portfolio would perform a little better -- maybe as good as Nancy Pelosi's or Ro Khanna's!
Platner is lying about Collins' finances, but he's correct to point out that Members of Congress have been found to trade on insider congressional knowledge, earning themselves millions of dollars. But if Platner wants to root out this corruption, he should start with Rep. Ro Khanna, who has endorsed Platner and is all over social media defending him and singing his praises.
Khanna, a California Democrat since 2017, doesn't personally trade stocks -- just like Collins. But the Khanna clan are busy little day traders with a knack for beating the market. He entered Congress with an estimated net worth of $45.8 million and now, by some estimates, is worth more than $200 million. Not bad on that $170,000 congressional salary... According to Quiver Quantitative, the Khanna clan has made 38,666 stock trades since he took office (total volume: $630.9 million). That's earned them an impressive 112.1% over the S&P 500. Many of those trades have been connected to activity involving congressional committees on which Khanna sits.
A 2022 _[New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/55ce895b-3a38-43b7-90a7-7f332fd3c71f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ investigation found, for example, that the Khanna family traded stocks in 897 companies, 149 of which had potential conflicts with Khanna's work as a congressman. An ethics complaint published this year notes that he (or his family) made 624 late filings to notify the proper authorities when his family is engaged in trading.
##### In other words, one of Graham Platner's biggest cheerleaders in Congress is a habitual violator of the ethics law that Collins helped write.

Republican Sen. Susan Collins responded to far left Democrat Graham Platner's allegations of criminal conduct in a statement posted to X on Friday. Jun 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Maine's Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Graham Platner staged a press event in Portland Thursday to accuse Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins of profiting from her office. Platner's allegation was based on a bizarre leftist conspiracy theory that claims Collins funneled money to her husband's consulting firm with a piece of legislation that passed the Senate unanimously five years before Collins was married. Platner's allegations of corruption drew a sharp response from Sen. Collins' campaign. "Today, a man I have never met held a press conference and accused me of criminal conduct," Collins said on X. "That is outrageous and false," she said. "If Graham Platner wants to debate policy, I look forward to that conversation. But making reckless and defamatory accusations because you cannot defend your own record is beneath the people of Maine." Like any EdgeLord shitposter, Platner was giddy to have elicited a response from Collins. So he jumped on X to double-down on his allegations that Collins has committed crimes (while simultaneously denying that he was alleging she's engaged in criminal conduct). "She got incredibly wealthy, funneling taxpayer money to her husband & profiting off stock trading while in office (violating the STOCK Act 25 times)," he said. "In a reasonable society, that would be criminal." For the first-ever Robinson Report Fact-Check, I rate Graham Platner's claim Four Portapotties on the Platner Lie-o-Meter. Subscribe to The Robinson Report for future Portapottie Reports on the Platner v. Collins campaign... So let's dig into Platner's allegation that Collins has used her office to self-enrich Every U.S. Senator has to file financial disclosures that allow the public to get a basic picture of their net worth, their assets, their liabilities, and, nowadays, their stock trading activity (or the activity of their family members). Collins was elected to the U.S. Senate in 1997, but the first financial disclosures available online date to 2012 and cover the financial year beginning in 2011. This was just before she married her husband. In that first financial disclosure, Collins disclosed assets of $110,005 to $300,000 and liabilities of $365,003 to $800,000. In other words, after two full terms in the U.S. Senate, Collins showed a negative net worth of between -$689,995 and -$65,003. Not exactly the portfolio of someone who has leveraged their office in Washington, D.C., to pad their bank account. (Note: Congressional financial disclosures require members to disclose dollar value ranges for assets and liabilities, so any analysis of congressional net worth is necessarily a minimum/maximum assessment.) The details of Collins' 2012 disclosed assets are even more boring, almost raising the question of why she wasn't taking a little more risk with bets on tech start-ups or blue-chip technology companies. She reported between $15,000 and $50,000 saved in a deferred compensation plan, a Fidelity IRA, a U.S. FCU savings account, and a Bangor Savings Bank account. Collins, then 59, reported an additional $50,000 to $100,000 in a separate Fidelity Asset Manager IRA. On the liabilities side, Collins reported two mortgages -- her home in Maine and another house (likely in the D.C. area) -- as well as a home equity line of credit. That's it. If there's any mystery or intrigue around Collins' financial disclosure, the question is why she was one of the poorest member of Congress. Here are the images of the oldest available disclosure for Collins. Susan Collins 2012 Financial Disclosure (Source: US Senate Clerk) However... After 2012, Collins' financial life rockets into the multi-millionaire stratosphere, a sure sign that she'd started trading stocks like the Wolf of Wall Street or, even worse, Nancy Pelosi and Ro Khanna... right? Right? | | ---|---|--- Well, no. To understand this sudden spike in Collins' net worth, you have to hop in the news archive time machine and travel back to 2012-2013 -- the same time period in which Graham Platner wrote on Reddit, "Luttrell didn't write the damn book, it was ghost written by a limey, and is war porn at its worst," in reference to the story of Navy Cross and Purple Heart recipient Marcus Luttrell, the U.S. Navy SEAL who inspired the hit movie Lone Survivor. Back to Collins: In 2012, she married Thomas A. Daffron at a small ceremony in her hometown of Caribou. (My invite must have gotten lost in the mail...) Prior to marrying Collins, Daffron had a diverse and lucrative career. He'd worked as chief of staff to several prominent senators, including former Defense Secretary William S. Cohen, and he'd served as the vice president and chief operating officer for the Baltimore Orioles. In 2006, he joined Jefferson Consulting Group, where he worked until 2016. Under U.S. Senate rules, members are required to include their spouses in their financial disclosures. The jump in net worth visible on Collins' financial disclosures is almost entirely assets and income that Daffron brought to the marriage. (No word on whether he asked for a pre-nup.) Unlike Collins, Daffron's disclosed finances show a man with a little more interest in taking risks and making savvy investments. In the 2013 disclosure, Collins reports basically the same asset and liability profile, along with a joint checking account ($50,000-$100,000) and a joint savings account ($15,000-$50,000). Every other asset and income stream on Collins' disclosure -- every single one -- is reported as belonging to "Spouse," a.k.a. Daffron. Well... not every source of income. Collins did report receiving a grill, dishes and silverware, a painting, a vase, and a picnic basket -- all as wedding gifts and all with values reported under $700. You can find the whole 2013 financial disclosure here: | Susan Collins 2013 Report4.27MB ∙ PDF file ---|--- | As anyone can see from the 2013 disclosure, Mr. Susan Collins came to the marriage with a high net worth and a diverse array of investments, including some five-to-six-figure investments in popular ETFs and mutual funds. His reported net worth is anywhere from $1.2 million to $5.3 million -- and that doesn't include his annual income from his full-time job. When it comes to individual stocks, Daffron held modest ($1,000-$15,000) positions in dozens of popular publicly traded companies, including Chevron, Comcast, ConocoPhillips, DuPont, GE, General Mills, Heinz, Intel, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Amazon, Apple, and Google. Now, you can hardly expect a communist to have a sophisticated understanding of high finance. Especially when their retirement strategy is designed around collecting a full military disability while waiting for Dad to die so you can inherit all the money Granddad made selling chairs. Compound interest, EBITDA, and the New York Stock Exchange might be a little hard for an "oysterman" like Graham Platner to wrap his brain around. But since 2012, the value of shares in those companies, especially the technology giants, has increased significantly. The appreciation of those stock prices, along with Daffron continuing to invest money in what appears to be the same way he'd been investing pre-2012, explains Collins' entire increase in net worth. To suggest Collins has corruptly profited from congressional insider trading, as Platner did Thursday, also elides her role in co-authoring the STOCK Act, which enhanced disclosures around congressional stock trading and prohibited certain kinds of trades. Indeed, it's only because of the STOCK Act provisions that Collins supported that politicians are now required to promptly disclose stock market transactions made by them or related parties, as opposed to disclosing them once per year. These disclosures allow websites like Unusual Whales to closely monitor, almost in real time, the stock portfolios of politicians. So thanks to legislation backed by Susan Collins, we can see that her and her husband's most recent year in the stock market has basically tracked the S&P 500 average. (The purple line is the Collins financial disclosure, while the tan line is the benchmark average.) | | ---|---|--- For comparison's sake, here's Nancy Pelosi's lifetime trading against the S&P500... | | ---|---|--- Unusual Whales is also the website that the 2024 congressional trading report that found the value of Collins' portfolio grew by 77.5 percent from Dec. 29, 2023, to Dec. 30, 2024 -- an eyebrow-raising number that beat not only the S&P 500 benchmark but also Nancy Pelosi! However, as Unusual Whales discloses, the methodology is based on a simple percentage change in portfolio valuation. It doesn't look at what individual stock performances may have driven the change. When you look at the individual stock performance, Collins' (a.k.a. Daffron's) strong performance is explained by the spectacular growth in valuations of large tech companies -- the kind of tech companies that any member of the public could invest in. For example, Daffron owned shares in Google, Amazon, and Apple, which saw their share prices climb by, respectively, +37.4%, +45.6%, and +31.6%. Similarly, Daffron owned Amphenol (+41.1%) and Raytheon (+40.2%). However, the real winning horse in the Collins-Daffron portfolio was NVIDIA, which has been an international stock market phenomenon, rising by 177.7% during the reporting period. However, the Unusual Whales data shows Daffron's last purchase of NVDA stock was Jan. 6, 2022. In other words, the Collins-Daffron stock portfolio is basically what you would expect from a reasonably intelligent dude who has been a working professional most of his life and invested his money wisely. Which brings us to Graham Platner, a guy whose finances resemble those of a man who blew his U.S. military paycheck on drugs and hookers in Bangkok. In his speech Thursday, Platner made a series of insinuated allegations -- allegations that, if true, would amount to ethical violations or even crimes. Here's a look at some pieces from El Platner's speech transcript: " We must pass the Collins rule. Senators should not be able to funnel money to their spouses." First of all, you would have to be a real idiot with zero understanding of how Congress runs to think that anyone in Washington, D.C., is going to call something "The Collins Rule" unless the rule is that you're not allowed to miss votes. But the important point is this: There is no evidence that Collins has funneled any money to Daffron. " We have anti-nepotism laws, which prohibits members from putting family members on their payroll, but it says nothing about a spouse's firm being enriched through winning contracts by agencies that that senator or congressperson oversees." Talk of nepotism is rich coming from a guy whose fake oyster business (it's a hobby) has disclosed just $5,000 in sales, all of which comes from his birthing parent. The same guy is just counting down the hours until dear old Dad kicks the bucket (the same dad who bought his house for him) and he can inherit the family fortune. But if you really want to talk about nepotism, how about Platner putting his wife on the campaign payroll despite her only job experience being as a live-in nanny in Camden (ask her how that ended...) and an alleged teacher. | | ---|---|--- Platner's actual criticism, to the extent there is some truth within the speech his DSA comrades wrote for him, pertains to a bill Collins co-authored with ex-Sen. Joe Lieberman (I-Conn.) in 2007. The so-called "Accountability in Government Contracting Act" aimed to make small firms more competitive when bidding for federal contracts. It also added some oversight provisions and made changes to the inspectors general offices. The bill passed the Senate unanimously. That is, two of the most moderate senators in U.S. history introduced the bill, and every single Democrat and every single Republican voted for it. That's the true version of the bill. The Platner version of the bill is that Collins was so greedy that she introduced this bill and convinced every single senator to vote for it because she also could predict the future and predicted that one day she would be married to a man who would benefit from the bill. Seriously. That's Platner's claim. Platner is claiming that Collins only introduced this bill because it would benefit Jefferson Consulting Group, where her husband (five years into the future) worked. The attack is so preposterous it could only have originated with someone who is, to borrow one of Platner's favorite phrases, retarded. And, of course, it did: the original claim came from , but it's been regurgitated by Platnerista groupies like . There's never been any evidence to suggest that Collins played any role whatsoever in directing contracts to the Jefferson Consulting Group. Moreover, while Daffron was working at Jefferson, Collins' income disclosures show a more or less stable growth in net worth -- not some massive spike in income or assets. ? If Susan Collins can see into the future, as Graham Platner seems to believe, then you'd think her portfolio would perform a little better -- maybe as good as Nancy Pelosi's or Ro Khanna's! Platner is lying about Collins' finances, but he's correct to point out that Members of Congress have been found to trade on insider congressional knowledge, earning themselves millions of dollars. But if Platner wants to root out this corruption, he should start with Rep. Ro Khanna, who has endorsed Platner and is all over social media defending him and singing his praises. Khanna, a California Democrat since 2017, doesn't personally trade stocks -- just like Collins. But the Khanna clan are busy little day traders with a knack for beating the market. He entered Congress with an estimated net worth of $45.8 million and now, by some estimates, is worth more than $200 million. Not bad on that $170,000 congressional salary... According to Quiver Quantitative, the Khanna clan has made 38,666 stock trades since he took office (total volume: $630.9 million). That's earned them an impressive 112.1% over the S&P 500. Many of those trades have been connected to activity involving congressional committees on which Khanna sits. A 2022 investigation found, for example, that the Khanna family traded stocks in 897 companies, 149 of which had potential conflicts with Khanna's work as a congressman. An ethics complaint published this year notes that he (or his family) made 624 late filings to notify the proper authorities when his family is engaged in trading. In other words, one of Graham Platner's biggest cheerleaders in Congress is a habitual violator of the ethics law that Collins helped write. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

Thank you. Thank you for caring about children you may never meet. Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold. Because that is exactly what is happening. Every day. God's children are not for sale. And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth. When you make your first gift to the Sound of Freedom Foundation today, we'll send you a FREE white "God's Children Are Not For Sale" t-shirt as our thank-you. | | | | | | | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. You can't buy it online. It was created exclusively for supporters of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: "No more." Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity. And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself. A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold. Families were being torn apart. Lives were being destroyed. I couldn't forget it. I couldn't stay silent. I kept asking myself one question: "What if it were my child?" That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom. Not for fame. Not for awards. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed. Studios walked away. People told us to give up. But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option. And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Our mission is simple: To stop the sale of God's children. Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, "Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14) Every child is precious in God's eyes. Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth. And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them When you make your first gift today, you help: Prevent exploitation by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children. # Jo’s first TV ads are hitting the air!
---
| | This week, Jo’s first TV ads are officially on a screen near you! The campaign released “Never Expires” and “Heat”, which will air in English and Spanish across broadcast, cable, and streaming throughout Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.
“Never Expires” features eight military veterans, including Jo, reflecting on their oath of service to the United States. The ad ends by thanking “all who swore the oath for 250 years,” referring to America’s 250th birthday this July 4th. The spot echoes this [campaign’s theme](https://us.list-manage.com/GqJGMNIjIpZ?e=fea3203902&c2id=b00e5bb4cdbce8e5db7719846a7b67e1) of patriotism, service, and love for country.

# Roundtable in Eloy and visiting a food bank in Casa Grande
---
| | Last week, Jo held a roundtable in Eloy with local leaders and community care providers to hear about the challenges they are facing as they serve their communities. While in Eloy, Jo stopped by the Eloy Veterans Center where there is a mural of [Lance Corporal JoJo Jiménez](https://us.list-manage.com/ylXS4BJBs1R?e=fea3203902&c2id=b00e5bb4cdbce8e5db7719846a7b67e1), an Eloy native who gave his life in service to our country in Vietnam.
Jo also visited the food pantry at Casa Grande Alliance, where she saw firsthand the dedication of the staff, even as shelves ran empty and working families in Casa Grande were [stretched to the brink](https://us.list-manage.com/mi083H7Ukku?e=fea3203902&c2id=b00e5bb4cdbce8e5db7719846a7b67e1) by rising food insecurity due to Juan Ciscomani’s SNAP cuts.
While there, she met Cowboy, a fellow Marine veteran who served in Desert Shield and Desert Storm and still answers the call to serve every day to help people in need.

# Showing up for Graham and Greenlee Counties
---
| | Last week, Jo was in Safford, Thatcher, and Clifton to meet with community service organizations like the Meals on Wheels team that serves the area, and joined them to help deliver meals to seniors. Jo also visited Our Neighbors Farm and Pantry food bank to see the work they do to serve families in need.
Jo also stopped by several local small businesses in downtown Safford, and met with fired-up Democrats in Graham and Greenlee Counties who are ready to flip this seat. In Congress, Jo will continue to show up and be accessible to ALL of AZ-06.

Alex Vindman here. With just 4 days until my FEC fundraising deadline hits, I am humbly asking you to make a donation to my U.S. Senate campaign in Florida.
I hope you will give me a chance to explain — but if you already know the importance of winning in Florida, then you can click here:
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026?refcode=em260626-2&refcode2=796_3892029_TqIhTd&akid=796%2E3892029%2ETqIhTd)
Running for the United States Senate was not an easy decision. I knew the challenges going into this.
Ever since I blew the whistle on Donald Trump’s phone call with Ukraine, the president has had a vendetta against me. He attacks me every chance he gets on social media, and his billionaire allies will spend wherever it takes to pummel us in attack ads.
But as a former combat veteran in the United States Army, we don’t back down from a tough fight. We run towards it.
Our country is in chaos, and my opponent can’t seem to put public service before her own self-interest. Ashley Moody screwed Florida homeowners by caving to the big insurance companies, supported this administration that gutted disaster help for communities trying to rebuild, and traded more than $2 million in corporate stock last year while she had access to insider information only Congress gets.
Ashley was hand-picked to be a ‘yes’ vote for Trump and the billionaire class. She is not Florida’s senator. She’s theirs.
So, that’s why I am running for the United States Senate. Because it’s time for us to make our voices heard and bring real leadership to Washington.**I know we can put Florida in play and save our democracy against an out-of-control president, but I cannot do it alone.**

I want to tell you something that’s not easy to talk about...
A sitting Republican elected official recently tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media and wrote: "I would like to report a foreign occupier. Name: Unpronounceable. Country of origin: Tatooine." He was talking about me. The same official called for the mass deportation of Indian Americans.
I was born in New Delhi. I came to this country as a baby. I grew up in Peoria, Illinois. I went to public schools, got on food stamps for a time with my family, worked my way to Princeton and Harvard Law. I served in government. I got elected to Congress four times.
And someone still looked at all of that and saw a foreign occupier.
I'm telling you this not for sympathy. I'm telling you this because what happened to me is happening to communities all across this country right now, at a scale we have never seen before.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear: if you weren't born here, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
My father came here with nothing. He believed this country would be there for families like ours. It was. Barely. Because people fought for it.
That is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scholten for Congress
body:
The path to a Democratic majority runs through Michigan. I'm proud to be in this fight alongside Haley Stevens.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134095976/630091519/30495591?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2026-06-26_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MGMwYjkxOS1iMzcxLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1B8TmH7xe7gKngq9ZCPR10uj2miucfZpNZEF4sTkINo=)
---
| I want to take a moment to tell you about someone I'm proud to call a colleague and a friend: **Haley Stevens, and why I'm endorsing her for Michigan's U.S. Senate seat.**

Here are my three reasons:

**1\. She's in this for Michigan.**
Senate races get a lot of national attention, but for us here in Michigan, we're choosing our next voice in the United States Senate. Haley is Pure Michigan, born and raised here, and she will never stop fighting for the people of this state.

**2\. She's authentic.**
She is a scrappy, relentless fighter who shows up every single day. I call her Little Truck because no matter how much chaos erupts around us, she just keeps trucking and gets things done.

**3\. She's effective, and she can prove it.**
We're not electing a TV pundit. We're electing a legislator. Haley has been named the most effective Michigan Democrat in Congress by the Center for Effective Lawmaking. She helped protect the pensions of more than 42,000 Michiganders through the Butch Lewis Act. subject: I want you to know about this disinformation

body:
This isn't a maternal health resource

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2948%2E4032634%2E4PCzch)
---
Four years ago this week, the Trump-stacked Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. The anti-choice movement had spent decades working toward that moment. But taking away the constitutional right to abortion was never the end of the story — it was the beginning. Since then, abortion bans have swept across the country. Tens of millions of people have lost access to care. Patients have died after being denied an abortion. Anti-choice extremists have targeted medication abortion, threatened contraception, and looked for new ways to put politicians between patients and their doctors. Now they're at it again. On Mother's Day, the Trump administration quietly launched a website called Moms dot gov (I’m not linking here so people don’t accidentally go to this misleading and horrific website) — presenting it as a “resource” to support the health and well-being of new and expecting mothers. What they didn't advertise is what the site is actually for: Directing pregnant women and their loved ones to unregulated and often nonmedical crisis pregnancy centers. AKA: Anti-abortion facilities. Let me explain what that means: Despite the name, crisis pregnancy centers are not medical clinics. Many are not staffed by licensed medical professionals. They are not bound by HIPAA privacy protections. They have no legal obligation to provide medically accurate information — and many don't. **The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has made its position clear: Crisis pregnancy centers exist to discourage people from accessing reproductive health care, including abortion and contraception.** So, the Trump administration is using taxpayer dollars to prop up a website that pushes pregnant women towards non-medical anti-abortion centers — and also collects data on them. This is not a maternal health resource. It's an anti-abortion operation wrapped in the seal of the United States Department of Health and Human Services. So I’m calling this out — and demanding answers from the Trump administration on this sham of a website. We want to know who built this website and whether medical experts were consulted. And we are demanding that the administration remove these links to the pregnancy centers immediately. The Republican plan is to sneak through anti-abortion resources and backdoor abortion bans because they know Americans don’t support their extreme agenda. Democrats are fighting back. With the support of this movement, we will challenge every attack. We will expose every piece of disinformation. We will fight every effort to take away our rights and our freedom to make our own health care decisions. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

Dear Peter,
Democrats _must_ win back the House if we’re going to put a check on Donald Trump’s corruption and protect working families. **One of the frontline candidates leading that fight is Randy Villegas.**
After placing in the top two of his primary, Randy is moving on to the general election against one of the most vulnerable Republicans in the country in California’s 22nd congressional district.
This is one of our best opportunities to flip a Republican district this year. **[Can you rush $5 to Randy’s campaign and my organization, Truth to Power, to help him win in November?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260626_1_ak.-bVUiJ&refcode=em20260626-41495&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41495%2E3422442%2EpRg6ym)**
In the primary, Randy proved that running on bold priorities wins over voters. **He made bringing prices down a top priority for his campaign, and talked about the importance of passing universal child care and single payer healthcare.**
These are issues that affect everyday Americans. Democrats win when we talk about making life affordable, and that’s _exactly_ what Randy is doing.
Best of all? We know we can trust Randy because _he rejects corporate PAC money_. The same corporations who got us into this mess aren’t buying his vote. Randy has the people’s support, and he’ll fight for us in Washington.
But first, we have to make sure he wins. Donald Trump and his billionaire buddies won’t let us flip this seat without a fight, which is why we all need to support Randy today.

Katie Porter

#
Peter —
There’s no point wasting your time here, so we’ll be direct.
Things aren’t looking good right now.
We’ve got a long way to go to meet our goals, and with an official FEC deadline on June 30th, the timing couldn’t be worse.
The goals VoteVets sets aren’t arbitrary numbers. They are what we need to raise to accomplish our goals this year: elevating Veteran candidates, winning independent and undecided voters in states we can’t afford to lose, and retaking the House and Senate this November.
Democrats are getting pummeled, relentlessly, day-in and day-out. Republicans have virtually no limit to the amount of money they can spend to defend their majorities, and they’ll use every trick in the book to do it. They’ve been stacking the deck with gerrymandering for decades — an insurance policy for years exactly like this one.
That’s why this FEC deadline — and what we raise before it hits — is so important. We have to be able to match their spending, if not dollar for dollar, then with candidates and ads that punch above their weight. We have to compete everywhere we can, or we’re going to come up short.

body:
For me, Emily’s leadership means visibility and unity

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134097535/630095255/1231236074?refcode=RS_EM_EN_2026.06.26_Ainsley&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYTdiNzBiOS1iYTcxLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AShF9CJ8mVFVawDfUF9aY8eWpUCekPRG2U9yCJ-OmKg=&emci=4b426280-7b71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=aa7b70b9-ba71-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&ceid=23483442) | Peter, I’m Ainsley! I grew up in Washington’s 6th Congressional District just like Emily Randall. _And also just like Emily Randall,_ **I’m queer.** Throughout my childhood, I watched as politicians both at home and across the nation fought about my rights and my existence. It has been so isolating to witness just how polarizing discussions of rights for my community can be. When Emily won her congressional seat, I was filled with hope. It was refreshing to see my neighbors celebrate an out and proud queer woman _who ran on the promise to fight for her LGBTQ+ constituents._ And here’s the thing: representation definitely matters, but it matters so much more when it delivers on its promises. **Emily has been an outspoken advocate for queer and trans kids across the country in a moment where even Democrats can’t always agree.
